records.name: LeanLab.GoldbachShort78.goldbach_short_1075
records.entry_name: Goldbach numbers in short intervals of length x^(26/1075+ε)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that for every ε > 0 and all large natural x there is a Goldbach number, an even sum of two primes, in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(26/1075+ε). The theorem is conditional on two cited results taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, and neither is proved here: LiRow052, R. Li, arXiv 2308.04458, Theorem 2, the row θ = 0.52, primes in the intervals from n - n^(0.52+ε) to n with a lower bound of the right order, with some positive constant since the printed constant differs between versions of the paper; and LiPrintedExceptionalCount, R. Li, arXiv 2407.05651 v6, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n to n + n^(1/21.5+ε) for almost all n. The argument adapts Theorem 7.1 of arXiv 2407.05651 v6, page 27, exponent 21/860 from the 0.525 of Baker, Harman and Pintz. The exponent 26/1075 is lower by 1/4300, and the gain is only the replacement of 0.525 by Li's 0.52. Li prints this exponent himself, as Theorem 7 of arXiv 2308.04458, with no ε and no factor 3, so this is a formal check of a known result and not a new exponent. Li's later note, Primes in almost all short intervals II, claims 1/22+ε in place of 1/21.5+ε, so 26/1075 is not claimed as the best exponent. Both cited papers are used here in their arXiv preprint form. Proved with no cited input: the passage from a count of primes in the intervals below n to a count in the windows from x - 2Y to x - Y, and the combinatorial step from the two counts to a Goldbach number. Added in the second version: the same argument at the exponent 13/600, a Goldbach number in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(13/600+ε) for every ε > 0 and all large natural x, goldbach_short_600. It is conditional on LiRow052 and on one more cited result, also an explicit hypothesis and never an axiom: LiIIIExceptionalCount, R. Li, Primes in almost all short intervals III, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n - n^(1/24+ε) to n for almost all n. Li prints the exponent 13/600 himself, as Theorem 8.1 of that paper, with no ε and no factor 3, so the Lean checks a printed result, conditional on the named inputs, and it is not a new result. That paper is an undated preprint on the author's web page, not on arXiv, and has not been peer reviewed as far as the packaging agent found. The one new step, proved with no cited input, turns a count of exceptions for the backward intervals into the forward count the argument uses. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex, Gemini and DeepSeek, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: LennonPittel.lennon_pittel_conjecture
records.entry_name: The Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings
records.doc: We prove the Lennon–Pittel conjecture for balanced stable marriage with independent, uniform strict preferences. Let S_n count the stable complete matchings between two sides of size n. For every positive nonincreasing sequence epsilon_n tending to zero, the probability that S_n is at least epsilon_n times its expectation tends to one. This gives a lower-tail estimate at the scale of Pittel's first-moment asymptotic. An accompanying working paper is in preparation.

records.name: DukeSchulzePillot.card_divisors_le_rpow
records.entry_name: Duke–Schulze-Pillot bounds and squarefree three squares in fixed caps (H1)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization retaining the upper representation bounds and the conditional consequence of Duke–Schulze-Pillot (Invent. Math. 99, 1990), and adding an unconditional fixed-cap theorem for x^2+y^2+z^2. H1: for every unit vector u in R^3 and every epsilon > 0 there is T such that every squarefree t >= T with t congruent to 3 modulo 8 has an integer representation x with sum x_i^2=t and |x_i-sqrt(t)u_i| <= epsilon sqrt(t) for every coordinate. The new statement takes no analytic estimate as a hypothesis. Its proof combines finite-degree harmonic Weyl bounds, odd-degree cancellation, a positive minimum of finitely many degree-dependent savings, and a representation lower bound supplied by the verified Siegel theorem. The threshold is ineffective. The original three unconditional upper/divisor bounds and two conditional statements are retained unchanged; the latter still require hThm1 and hThm3i for general ternary forms. No unconditional general Duke–Schulze-Pillot theorem, sharp 1/175 exponent, spinor-genus lower bound or numerical cutoff is claimed.

records.name: Green64.green_64
records.entry_name: Primes p for which Ω(p − 2) is odd (Green's Problem 64)
records.doc:
For infinitely many primes p, Ω(p − 2) is odd, where Ω counts prime factors with multiplicity. We assign nonnegative weights to integers u in [x, 2x] with Ω(u) odd. Using a shifted correlation estimate, we sieve the values u + 2 and obtain a lower bound for the combined weight of primes and products of two large primes. A separate upper bound for the contribution from those products leaves positive weight on primes for every sufficiently large x.
Proof development and Lean formalization by gpt-6 astra.

records.name: IncrementalCyclic.incremental_represents_nc_coins
records.entry_name: Cyclic n × n Latin Squares Representing Solutions of (n, c)-Coins Problems
records.doc: Formalization of incremental n × n Latin squares and cyclic incremental n × n Latin squares representing n + 1 solutions of (n, c)-coins problems simultaneously for all 0 ≤ c ≤ n. We prove that (1) for every n ≥ 4, any incremental n × n Latin square represents valid (n, c)-coins solutions for all 0 ≤ c ≤ n simultaneously via value thresholding, and (2) for every n ≥ 4 with n ∉ {4, 6}, there exists a column permutation p such that the cyclic Latin square L(i, j) = (i + p(j)) mod n is incremental, using an injective-majorization principle across four infinite modular families modulo 6 and the four exceptional dimensions n ∈ {8, 9, 15, 21}, together with explicit non-cyclic incremental Latin squares for n = 4 and n = 6.

records.name: MinkowskiLorentz.so'_one_three_lieEquiv_sl2C
records.entry_name: Invariant bilinear forms on the Lorentz Lie algebra so(3,1): the two-parameter family a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y), with sl(2,C), the exponential criterion and the complexification
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about the Lie algebra L of the linear endomorphisms of four-dimensional Minkowski space that are skew-adjoint for the Minkowski form. Main theorem, (6): a real bilinear form B on L satisfies B([Z,X],Y) + B(X,[Z,Y]) = 0 for all X, Y, Z if and only if B(X,Y) = a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for exactly one pair of real numbers (a,b); every such form is symmetric. Here tr(XY) is the trace form of L acting on Minkowski space and H is the operator of (4). For a real simple Lie algebra whose complexification is simple the invariant symmetric bilinear forms are the multiples of the Killing form; for a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one they form a plane (Francis-Staite and Leistner, Proposition 4.1). L is of the second kind: it is sl(2,C) regarded as a real Lie algebra ((1), (2)), H is multiplication by -i under that isomorphism ((4)), and tr(H(X)Y) is a second invariant form, not a multiple of the Killing form (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.10, where it is, up to a nonzero factor, K(X, J Y)). Read with X as a field strength, tr(XX) and tr(H(X)X) are, up to normalisation, the Maxwell term and the theta term (Tong's names); that reading is not formalized. Statements (1)-(5): sl(2,C), the exponential criterion, the operator H and the complexification; (2) and (4) are the structure behind the second term of (6). (1) On Mathlib's own objects, with nothing carried: Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R is isomorphic, as a real Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) (Mathlib's sl (Fin 2) C with scalars restricted to R), by the explicit map X -> -(1/2) sum_k (beta_k + i theta_k) sigma_k, where beta_k and theta_k are the boost and rotation entries of X and sigma_k are the Pauli matrices. (2) On the carried copy of Minkowski space: L has dimension 6; the same map is an isomorphism of real Lie algebras from L onto sl(2,C); the three boost generators and the three rotation generators are in L, the boost along the axis k goes to -(1/2) sigma_k and the rotation in the plane of the two other axes goes to -(i/2) sigma_k. (3) The exponential criterion: a continuous linear endomorphism A is in L if and only if exp(tA) is in the carried type ProperLorentz for every real t; the statement also records that the Minkowski form used for L has the carried minkowskiSquare as its quadratic form. (4) The explicit operator H (the boost along the axis k goes to minus the rotation in the plane of the two other axes, and that rotation goes to the boost) maps L into L, is real-linear there, satisfies H[X,Y] = [X,HY] and H(HX) = -X, and the isomorphism of (2) carries it to multiplication by -i on sl(2,C). (5) The complexification C (x)_R L is isomorphic, as a complex Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) x sl(2,C), and the two maps (1/2)(1 + iH) and (1/2)(1 - iH) are the projections onto the two factors, H being the operator of (4) extended C-linearly. Controls: (7) for the definite diagonal form diag(1,1,1,1) the Lie algebra of skew matrices is isomorphic to so(3) x so(3), for the split form diag(1,1,-1,-1) it is isomorphic to sl(2,R) x sl(2,R), and neither of the two is isomorphic to sl(2,C) as a real Lie algebra; (8) there is a bilinear form on L that is not a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for any real a, b; (9) there is a continuous linear endomorphism A with exp(A) in ProperLorentz and A not in L. Numbering as in comparator.json. Statement (1) and part (b) of statement (2) are one isomorphism on two presentations; they are not two results. The Challenge imports Mathlib only. The definitions of Minkowski space and of the Lorentz transformations (Spacetime, minkowskiSquare, ProperLorentz and eight more) are copies carried textually from the public statement of the Yang-Mills release, repository github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028, commit 3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464, file PublicTheory.lean, under the Apache License, Version 2.0; the source file is not imported. Statement (6) is proved from the classification of the linear maps R of L with R[X,Y] = [X,RY], which is the subject of a separate entry in preparation and is not compared here. Audience. Formal developments that use the Lorentz Lie algebra as an object. physlib's lorentzAlgebra is Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R, the object of (1); physlib also proves that the complex coefficient tensors with four vector indices invariant under SL(2,C) acting through the Lorentz group are combinations of the three pairings of the metric and the alternating symbol (independence is not proved there). The Yang-Mills release works with the Lorentz Lie algebra of this entry as the predicate tangent (X^T = -theta X theta) on its own 4 x 4 matrix type, splits it into rotations and boosts (tangent_parts), and proves, under its hypothesis Spin.Port, that its Wick-rotated map into operators on field labels respects brackets whenever the first argument is a boost (rank_bracket), in YM/Next/BOUNDARY/Derived.lean; it does not state or use any of the nine statements here, and its matrix type is not the carried Spacetime. The monograph project hairer/humanise-yang-mills proves that invariant bilinear forms on the compact colour algebra are scalar multiples using a positive invariant inner product (manuscript/existence/trace-free-rank.tex, lines 34-51, commit 0f00ae72); (6) shows that on so(3,1), which is simple but has no such inner product, the invariant forms are a two-parameter family. No one at these projects was contacted, and none of them has asked for or endorsed this entry. Literature. This entry formalizes known mathematics; the clauses not found printed are listed below. (1) and (2) are the Lie-algebra form of Spin(3,1) = SL(2,C) (Woit, Quantum Theory, Groups and Representations, sections 40.2 and 40.4; the formula is printed on generators in section 41.2; Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Lemma A.1, state so(3,1) = sl(2,C)_R); (3) is the description of the Lie algebra of a matrix group by its one-parameter subgroups (Hall, arXiv:math-ph/0005032, Definition 3.13; proved there for O(n;k), which includes O(3;1), Chapter 3, section 5.6), stated here for the proper orthochronous subgroup, and (9) is an exercise of that chapter; (4) is the Hodge operator on so(3,1) (Wise, Class. Quantum Grav. 27 (2010) 155010, Appendix); (5) is the splitting of the complexified Lorentz algebra (Woit, section 40.2; Sahlmann and Seeger, Class. Quantum Grav. 41 (2024) 075010, section 2.2.1); (6) is the description of the invariant bilinear forms of a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Transform. Groups 17 (2012), Remark A.10; Francis-Staite and Leistner, Transform. Groups 26 (2021), Proposition 4.1); parts (a) and (b) of (7) are the companion isomorphisms in the two other signatures (Woit, section 21.2; Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.2); (8) holds by a count of dimensions (the bilinear forms on L have dimension 36 and the forms of statement 6 are a plane). Not found printed in the sources read: the clause of (4) on multiplication by -i, and parts (c) and (d) of (7); README.md says how each follows from what is printed. records.entry_name: Invariant bilinear forms on the Lorentz Lie algebra so(3,1): the two-parameter family a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y), with sl(2,C), the exponential criterion and the complexification
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about the Lie algebra L of the linear endomorphisms of four-dimensional Minkowski space that are skew-adjoint for the Minkowski form. Main theorem, (6): a real bilinear form B on L satisfies B([Z,X],Y) + B(X,[Z,Y]) = 0 for all X, Y, Z if and only if B(X,Y) = a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for exactly one pair of real numbers (a,b); every such form is symmetric. Here tr(XY) is the trace form of L acting on Minkowski space and H is the operator of (4). For a real simple Lie algebra whose complexification is simple the invariant symmetric bilinear forms are the multiples of the Killing form; for a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one they form a plane (Francis-Staite and Leistner, Proposition 4.1). L is of the second kind: it is sl(2,C) regarded as a real Lie algebra ((1), (2)), H is multiplication by -i under that isomorphism ((4)), and tr(H(X)Y) is a second invariant form, not a multiple of the Killing form (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.10, where it is, up to a nonzero factor, K(X, J Y)). Read with X as a field strength, tr(XX) and tr(H(X)X) are, up to normalisation, the Maxwell term and the theta term (Tong's names); that reading is not formalized. Statements (1)-(5): sl(2,C), the exponential criterion, the operator H and the complexification; (2) and (4) are the structure behind the second term of (6). (1) On Mathlib's own objects, with nothing carried: Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R is isomorphic, as a real Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) (Mathlib's sl (Fin 2) C with scalars restricted to R), by the explicit map X -> -(1/2) sum_k (beta_k + i theta_k) sigma_k, where beta_k and theta_k are the boost and rotation entries of X and sigma_k are the Pauli matrices. (2) On the carried copy of Minkowski space: L has dimension 6; the same map is an isomorphism of real Lie algebras from L onto sl(2,C); the three boost generators and the three rotation generators are in L, the boost along the axis k goes to -(1/2) sigma_k and the rotation in the plane of the two other axes goes to -(i/2) sigma_k. (3) The exponential criterion: a continuous linear endomorphism A is in L if and only if exp(tA) is in the carried type ProperLorentz for every real t; the statement also records that the Minkowski form used for L has the carried minkowskiSquare as its quadratic form. (4) The explicit operator H (the boost along the axis k goes to minus the rotation in the plane of the two other axes, and that rotation goes to the boost) maps L into L, is real-linear there, satisfies H[X,Y] = [X,HY] and H(HX) = -X, and the isomorphism of (2) carries it to multiplication by -i on sl(2,C). (5) The complexification C (x)_R L is isomorphic, as a complex Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) x sl(2,C), and the two maps (1/2)(1 + iH) and (1/2)(1 - iH) are the projections onto the two factors, H being the operator of (4) extended C-linearly. Controls: (7) for the definite diagonal form diag(1,1,1,1) the Lie algebra of skew matrices is isomorphic to so(3) x so(3), for the split form diag(1,1,-1,-1) it is isomorphic to sl(2,R) x sl(2,R), and neither of the two is isomorphic to sl(2,C) as a real Lie algebra; (8) there is a bilinear form on L that is not a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for any real a, b; (9) there is a continuous linear endomorphism A with exp(A) in ProperLorentz and A not in L. records.entry_name: Invariant bilinear forms on the Lorentz Lie algebra so(3,1): the two-parameter family a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y), with sl(2,C), the exponential criterion and the complexification
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about the Lie algebra L of the linear endomorphisms of four-dimensional Minkowski space that are skew-adjoint for the Minkowski form. Main theorem, (6): a real bilinear form B on L satisfies B([Z,X],Y) + B(X,[Z,Y]) = 0 for all X, Y, Z if and only if B(X,Y) = a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for exactly one pair of real numbers (a,b); every such form is symmetric. Here tr(XY) is the trace form of L acting on Minkowski space and H is the operator of (4). For a real simple Lie algebra whose complexification is simple the invariant symmetric bilinear forms are the multiples of the Killing form; for a complex simple Lie algebra regarded as a real one they form a plane (Francis-Staite and Leistner, Proposition 4.1). L is of the second kind: it is sl(2,C) regarded as a real Lie algebra ((1), (2)), H is multiplication by -i under that isomorphism ((4)), and tr(H(X)Y) is a second invariant form, not a multiple of the Killing form (Olafsson and Quiroga-Barranco, Remark A.10, where it is, up to a nonzero factor, K(X, J Y)). Read with X as a field strength, tr(XX) and tr(H(X)X) are, up to normalisation, the Maxwell term and the theta term (Tong's names); that reading is not formalized. Statements (1)-(5): sl(2,C), the exponential criterion, the operator H and the complexification; (2) and (4) are the structure behind the second term of (6). (1) On Mathlib's own objects, with nothing carried: Mathlib's so' (Fin 1) (Fin 3) R is isomorphic, as a real Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) (Mathlib's sl (Fin 2) C with scalars restricted to R), by the explicit map X -> -(1/2) sum_k (beta_k + i theta_k) sigma_k, where beta_k and theta_k are the boost and rotation entries of X and sigma_k are the Pauli matrices. (2) On the carried copy of Minkowski space: L has dimension 6; the same map is an isomorphism of real Lie algebras from L onto sl(2,C); the three boost generators and the three rotation generators are in L, the boost along the axis k goes to -(1/2) sigma_k and the rotation in the plane of the two other axes goes to -(i/2) sigma_k. (3) The exponential criterion: a continuous linear endomorphism A is in L if and only if exp(tA) is in the carried type ProperLorentz for every real t; the statement also records that the Minkowski form used for L has the carried minkowskiSquare as its quadratic form. (4) The explicit operator H (the boost along the axis k goes to minus the rotation in the plane of the two other axes, and that rotation goes to the boost) maps L into L, is real-linear there, satisfies H[X,Y] = [X,HY] and H(HX) = -X, and the isomorphism of (2) carries it to multiplication by -i on sl(2,C). (5) The complexification C (x)_R L is isomorphic, as a complex Lie algebra, to sl(2,C) x sl(2,C), and the two maps (1/2)(1 + iH) and (1/2)(1 - iH) are the projections onto the two factors, H being the operator of (4) extended C-linearly. Controls: (7) for the definite diagonal form diag(1,1,1,1) the Lie algebra of skew matrices is isomorphic to so(3) x so(3), for the split form diag(1,1,-1,-1) it is isomorphic to sl(2,R) x sl(2,R), and neither of the two is isomorphic to sl(2,C) as a real Lie algebra; (8) there is a bilinear form on L that is not a tr(XY) + b tr(H(X)Y) for any real a, b; (9) there is a continuous linear endomorphism A with exp(A) in ProperLorentz and A not in L. The definitions of Minkowski space and of the Lorentz transformations (Spacetime, minkowskiSquare, ProperLorentz and eight more) are copies carried textually from the public statement of the Yang-Mills release, repository github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028, commit 3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464, file PublicTheory.lean, under the Apache License, Version 2.0; the source file is not imported. Statement (6) is proved from the classification of the linear maps R of L with R[X,Y] = [X,RY], which is the subject of a separate entry in preparation and is not compared here. Audience. records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about the Lie algebra L of the linear endomorphisms of four-dimensional Minkowski space that are skew-adjoint for the Minkowski form. records.name: RamseyR55.ramsey_number_five_five_lower_bound
records.entry_name: The lower bound R(5,5) ≥ 43: a kernel-checked Ramsey graph on 42 vertices
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Exoo's lower bound R(5,5) ≥ 43 for the diagonal graph Ramsey number: there is a simple graph on 42 vertices with no clique of size 5 and no independent set of size 5. The proof defines a clique scan on natural-number bit masks, proves that a scan with the result `false` excludes every clique of the given size, and lets the Lean kernel evaluate the scan on one explicit graph and on its complement (`decide +kernel`, no `native_decide`). The statement is the one that the Formal Conjectures repository records as `RamseyNumbers.ramsey_number_five_five_lower_bound`. The value of R(5,5) is open; 43 has been the best known lower bound since 1989.

records.name: Autoconvolutions.sharpness
records.entry_name: Sharpness of the Martin–O'Bryant autoconvolution inequality
records.doc: For every real ε > 0, there are finitely many nonnegative real  heights p₀,…,p_d, at least one positive, such that the autoconvolution  of the step function taking height pⱼ on [j,j+1) and zero elsewhere  has the ratio (L² norm)^2 / ((L¹ norm) (L∞ norm)) greater than 1−ε.

records.name: KeevashTri.theorem_2_1
records.entry_name: Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1: triangle decompositions of typical graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, "Counting designs" (arXiv:1504.02909): there are c₀ > 0 and n₀ such that every graph G on n ≥ n₀ vertices with all degrees even and 3 | e(G) that is (c,h)-typical, with density d(G) > n^(-10^-7) and c ≤ c₀·d(G)^(10^6), has a triangle decomposition; h = 2 (the paper's c-typical case, KeevashTri.theorem_2_1_ctyp, new in v2) and h = 16 (KeevashTri.theorem_2_1, v1). (c,h)-typical means |⋂_{x∈S} G(x)| = (1 ± |S|c)·d(G)^|S|·n for every vertex set S with |S| ≤ h; for h = 2 this is degrees (1 ± c)·d(G)·n and pair codegrees (1 ± 2c)·d(G)²·n (the paper asks (1 ± c) for pairs, so the hypothesis here is slightly weaker). The density and typicality thresholds are the paper's (n^(-10^-7) and c₀·d^(10^6)); c₀ and n₀ are not explicit. Quantitative internals of the c-typical proof: c_e = max(c, n^(-1/10)), goodness parameter c' = c_e^(1/4), at most η = 16c'^2·n + 4/(c'^2·d^16) bad one-vertex extensions of a c'-good set of at most 15 vertices. The proof follows the paper's strategy (random algebraic template over F₂^a, Nibble, Cover, Hole, Completion), with every random greedy algorithm of the Completion replaced by a deterministic potential (pessimistic-estimator) argument. Earlier registered entries are imported as lake dependencies: the hypergraph matching nibble of Ehard–Glock–Joos (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000004) and the Steiner triple system material of PALOMAR-2026-10-22-000017 v2. Mathlib does not contain this result.

records.name: Couret.PalomarFour.fibre_cardinality
records.entry_name: Cyclic four-point square fibres and fixed membership reconstruction
records.doc: For a four-point support in Z/nZ with n positive, the complete labelled ordered-square fibre has cardinality one, two or four. At most two fixed binary membership probes separate that fibre. The full square and its fibre are supplied; no computational runtime bound or adaptive query lower bound is asserted.

records.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111.variants.wagon
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 1111: Wagon's bound
records.doc: Every finite graph with no clique of size t and chromatic number at least C(t,2)+1 has two anticomplete vertex sets that each induce a graph of chromatic number at least 2 (Wagon 1980, as noted by El-Zahar and Erdős). In Erdős Problem 1111, d(t,c) is the least d such that every finite graph with clique number less than t and chromatic number at least d has two anticomplete vertex sets A, B with χ(G[A]) ≥ c and χ(G[B]) ≥ c (El-Zahar and Erdős 1985). So the result says d(t,2) ≤ C(t,2)+1. Two anticomplete sets that each induce a graph of chromatic number at least 2 are the same as an induced 2K₂.

records.entry_name: Sharp logarithmic Kakeya estimates in every dimension
records.doc:
We formalize two sharp logarithmic Kakeya upper bounds in every integer dimension n ≥ 2. For 0 < δ ≤
1, the Kakeya maximal operator takes the largest average of |f| over open radius-δ neighborhoods of
unit segments in each direction. Its norm from Lⁿ(ℝⁿ) to Lⁿ(Sⁿ⁻¹) is at most Cₙ[log(2/δ)]^((n−1)/n).
The tube estimate applies to any finite family of N unit directions with pairwise Euclidean distance
at least δ, arbitrary centers, and nonnegative weights aⱼ. Let Tⱼ be the open radius-2δ neighborhood
of the corresponding centered unit segment, let 1_T denote the indicator of T, and set q = n/(n−1).
The integral over ℝⁿ of (∑ⱼ aⱼ 1_{Tⱼ})^q is at most Cₙ log(2/δ) δ^(n−1) ∑ⱼ aⱼ^q. All constants
depend only on n. The same estimate holds for radius-δ tubes. Hölder's inequality gives tube-union
volume at least cₙNδ^(n−1)/[log(2/δ)]^(n−1), and a direction net gives volume at least
cₙ/[log(2/δ)]^(n−1) for the δ-neighborhood of every Kakeya set. This matches the construction of
Fernández-Delgado and de la Salle. The estimates imply the Kakeya maximal function conjecture and
full Minkowski dimension for every bounded Kakeya set. Written lower-bound arguments establish
optimality of the logarithmic powers. Only the two upper estimates are Lean theorems; the geometric
consequences and sharpness arguments are not formalized here. The accompanying abstract and summary
give the fully typeset statements.

records.name: isoperimetric_area
records.entry_name: Isoperimetric Inequality for Spherical Tetrahedra
records.doc: Sharp isoperimetric comparisons for geodesic tetrahedra in the unit three-sphere: conditional on a regular tetrahedron having the same volume or surface area, the regular tetrahedron uniquely minimizes surface area at fixed volume and uniquely maximizes volume at fixed surface area up to congruence.

records.name: LeanLab.Linnik.Decomp1532c.theorem1_of_leaves
records.entry_name: Primes and powers of 2: Gallagher's mean square theorem and the asymptotic count of two primes and k powers of 2
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the two main theorems of P. X. Gallagher, Primes and powers of 2, Invent. Math. 29, 1975, for the base g = 2. Let r'_k of n count the representations n = p + 2^v1 + ... + 2^vk with p prime and 1 <= vi <= L, the integer part of log_2 N, and let r''_k of N count the representations N = p1 + p2 + 2^v1 + ... + 2^vk. Theorem 1, display 3 on page 125: for every k >= 1 and N >= N_k, the sum over odd n <= N of the square of r'_k of n minus 2 L^k / log N is at most C times log^2 2k / k times N L^{2k-2}, with an absolute constant C. Theorem 2, display 4 on page 125: for every k >= 2 and every even N >= N_k, r''_k of N differs from 2 N L^k / log^2 N by at most K times log^2 k / k times 2 N L^k / log^2 N, with an absolute constant K. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: Erdos112.k63_bounds
records.entry_name: Bounds on the Erdős-Rado number k(6,3): 30 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 32 (Erdős Problem #112)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that 30 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 32. Here k(n,3) is the Erdős-Rado number: the least k such that every oriented graph on k vertices has n vertices with no arc between any two of them, or a transitive triangle (vertices x, y, z with arcs x → y, y → z and x → z). The lower bound is an explicit oriented graph on 29 vertices with no transitive triangle and no 6 independent vertices. The upper bound shows that every oriented graph on 32 vertices has one or the other; it rests on a counting argument and on one finite case analysis (every oriented graph on 14 vertices with no transitive triangle and no 4 independent vertices is 6-regular), which is carried out by 49 computations inside Lean's kernel. The upper bounds k(3,3) ≤ 9, k(4,3) ≤ 15 and k(5,3) ≤ 23 are proved on the way and are not cited. The whole proof is checked by the kernel, with no native_decide, and uses only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Before this work the bounds that followed from published results were 26 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 33. The result gives bounds only: k(6,3) is 30, 31 or 32, its value is not determined, and Erdős Problem #112, which asks for k(n,m) in general, remains open. As of 14 November 2026 the community database of Erdős problems lists #112 as unformalized, and the public Lean statements of the problem known to the author prove no bound; to the author's knowledge this is the first machine-checked result on the problem.

records.name: QuantumInfo.knill_laflamme
records.entry_name: The Knill-Laflamme theorem: a set of errors is correctable on a quantum code exactly when P E_i^† E_j P = c_ij P
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of the Knill-Laflamme theorem for finite-dimensional quantum codes, in two forms. For a nonzero code given by an orthogonal projector P and a finite family of arbitrary error matrices E_i, the condition P E_i^† E_j P = c_ij P for some matrix c holds if and only if some quantum channel, with any finite number of Kraus operators, undoes each error on every code state up to its own scalar (knill_laflamme), and also if and only if some channel undoes the combined noise rho -> sum_i E_i rho E_i^† up to a scalar (knill_laflamme_sum). The errors need not form a channel. The recovery is constructed explicitly. Mathlib, at the pinned commit, has no quantum error correction. Four other Lean proofs of the channel form are known to me, one earlier and three later than this proof (listed under related_formalizations); this proof is independent of all four. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed.

records.name: Actions.ActionAutomaton.Reaches.admissible
records.entry_name: Nowakowska Theory of Actions (1982) in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib (v4.36.0-rc2) formalization of Maria Nowakowska's A Formal Theory of Actions (Syntax and Semantics of Behaviour; chapter dated 1982; Praxiological Studies, 1983), synthesizing the parts of Language of Motivation and Language of Actions (1973) that 1982 cites for omitted proofs and for the motivational calculus (here: §§2.1.4, 2.2.4, 5.1–5.3). Framing: rigorous reconstruction/verification of her action–motivation–promise material (precision gaps closed in Lean), plus a formalization contribution proving CF ∩ Regular so Promise/Offense CF theorems are unconditional. Headline compared claims include card_conflictFamilies (her stated 113), Attainable_iff_reaches_length (reachability realization), arrow_impossibility in the finite 2×3 encoding, unconditional PromiseClosed/OffenseClosed.isContextFree with factor-minimal HatU, Language.IsContextFree.inter_regular, and stringDuration_pi / timed ψ-membership. Clinical Arrow abbrevs and MotCalc samples are supporting packaging, not claimed novelty. Maria Nowakowska did not participate in or endorse this formalization. Lean was written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson's direction and review. There is no sorry in the Actions/ development, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency. Palomar Registration: TBD.

records.name: PalomarInghamAP.psi_ap_error_of_zero_free
records.entry_name: Primes in arithmetic progressions with power-saving error from zero-free half-planes of Dirichlet L-functions
records.doc: For a fixed modulus q and a residue a coprime to q: if ζ(s) and every L(s, χ) with χ a nontrivial Dirichlet character mod q have no zeros with real part greater than θ (1/2 ≤ θ < 1), then ψ(x; q, a) = x/φ(q) + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequently the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for all Dirichlet L-functions (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis, verbatim) yields the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions with error O(x^{7/8+δ}). Proof: for each χ ≠ 1, a smoothed twisted Chebyshev function, a contour shift (no residue, L entire), a bound L'/L(σ+it, χ) ≪ log|t| via Borel–Carathéodory after continuing L to Re s > 0 with a polynomial growth bound, then orthogonality of characters and the ζ case for the trivial character.

records.name: CollatzMCycles.Diophantine.terminal
records.entry_name: Collatz m-cycles for m ≤ 91 (conditional on Bařina's 2^71 check) and an explicit linear-form bound for log 2 and log 3
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two results. (1) An explicit lower bound for the linear form Λ = (K + L) log 2 − K log 3: for every K ≥ 2438425051595107335801557824 and every L, Λ cannot satisfy 0 < Λ < 100 · 2^(1 − K/2^68). This new self-contained bound is proved from Mathlib using explicit symmetric multipoint Padé approximants (the z = x(70 − x) kernel of Salikhov and Bouchelaghem–He–Li–Wu) together with an elementary bound on lcm(1, …, n), replacing the use of Rhin's (1987) effective irrationality measure in Collatz cycle arguments. (2) An independent proof of Hercher's (2023) theorem on Collatz m-cycles: assuming Bařina's 2025 computer verification that every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ 2^71 reaches 1 under the Collatz map (passed as an explicit hypothesis), there is no non-trivial cycle of the shortcut Collatz map with m ≤ 91 local minima. Rather than Hercher's finite search and Rhin's (1987) bound, the proof here combines a Raney-type rotation of the cycle, a telescopic lower bound on every local minimum, a 2-adic unimodular reduction, and a kernel-checked chain of continued-fraction steps that forces the number of odd steps past the range of (1). The definitions of the shortcut map and of m-cycles follow Moritz Firsching's formal-conjectures specification. This is an incremental m-cycle certificate plus a formalization; it does not address general cycles or divergent orbits. Both theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Four supporting statements are also compared: the trivial cycle 1 → 2 → 1 is a 1-cycle through 1 and through 2, every m-cycle has m ≥ 1, and (under the same hypothesis) every element of a non-trivial cycle exceeds 2^71.

records.name: MosN8.tower
records.entry_name: McCarthy–Osburn–Straub Conjecture 1.3 for σ₈, with a shifted companion
records.doc: Let A(n) be the sum, over k ∈ [0, n]^4 with k₁ + k₂ = k₃ + k₄, of the products Π C(n, k_i) C(n + k_i, k_i). The package proves A(mp^r) ≡ A(mp^{r−1}) (mod p^{3r}) and A(mp^r − 1) ≡ A(mp^{r−1} − 1) (mod p^{3r}) for every prime p ≥ 5 and all m, r ≥ 1. By McCarthy, Osburn and Straub's Proposition 3.1, A(n) is the leading coefficient of Brown's cellular integral for σ₈ = (8, 3, 6, 1, 4, 7, 2, 5), so the first congruence is their Conjecture 1.3 for σ₈. That link is not formalized. The second congruence is a companion that no source states. σ₈ is the self-dual configuration that MOS single out: their Theorem 1.2 relates A_σ₈((p − 1)/2) to the weight-6 newform η¹²(2z) modulo p².

records.name: MosN8.shifted_tower
records.entry_name: McCarthy–Osburn–Straub Conjecture 1.3 for σ₈, with a shifted companion
records.doc: Let A(n) be the sum, over k ∈ [0, n]^4 with k₁ + k₂ = k₃ + k₄, of the products Π C(n, k_i) C(n + k_i, k_i). The package proves A(mp^r) ≡ A(mp^{r−1}) (mod p^{3r}) and A(mp^r − 1) ≡ A(mp^{r−1} − 1) (mod p^{3r}) for every prime p ≥ 5 and all m, r ≥ 1. By McCarthy, Osburn and Straub's Proposition 3.1, A(n) is the leading coefficient of Brown's cellular integral for σ₈ = (8, 3, 6, 1, 4, 7, 2, 5), so the first congruence is their Conjecture 1.3 for σ₈. That link is not formalized. The second congruence is a companion that no source states. σ₈ is the self-dual configuration that MOS single out: their Theorem 1.2 relates A_σ₈((p − 1)/2) to the weight-6 newform η¹²(2z) modulo p².

records.name: OeisA326097.a326097_existsUnique
records.entry_name: OEIS A326097: the parity of a(k) (Hanna's conjecture)
records.doc: The e.g.f. A(x) of OEIS A326097 satisfies 1 = Σ_{n≥0} ((1+x)^n − A(x))^n/n!. The package proves that this equation has exactly one solution in ℚ[[x]], that every a(k) = k! [x^k] A(x) is an integer, and that a(k) is odd if and only if k ∈ {0, 1, 3} or k ≡ 2 (mod 4). This settles Paul D. Hanna's 2019 parity conjecture in a slightly stronger form. The same holds for OEIS A385907, where (1+x)^n is replaced by 1/(1−x)^n.

records.name: OeisA363985.u_tower
records.entry_name: OEIS A363985 and siblings: Bala's p^(3r) supercongruences for u_m, every integer m
records.doc: For an integer m let u_m(n) = Σ_{k=0}^{n} (−4)^{n−k} C(n,k) C(mn+k, k) C(2k, k), with the binomial C(mn+k, k) taken as a polynomial in its top. The package proves that u_m(np^r) ≡ u_m(np^{r−1}) (mod p^{3r}) for every integer m, every prime p ≥ 5 and all n, r ≥ 1. This is the u-half of Peter Bala's 2023 conjecture on OEIS A363985. It covers A363985 (m = 2), A363987 (m = 3), A363989 (m = 4) and A362676 (m = −1, up to the sign (−1)^n), each stated as its own theorem. The companion v-half of the conjecture (A363986, A363988, A363990) is not covered. Osburn and Sahu's tower for the generalized Domb numbers needs a factor C(n,k)^A with A ≥ 2. The proof here first writes u_m(N) = Σ_j (−1)^j C(mN, N−j) C(2j,j) C(2N−2j, N−j), where C(mN, N−j) occurs only once. The missing powers of p come from the super Catalan factorization of C(2j,j) C(2N−2j, N−j) and from half-block sums of j^{−2}, as in Osburn–Sahu–Straub's proofs of their Theorems 1.3 and 1.2.

records.name: OeisA364111.u_supercongruence
records.entry_name: OEIS A364111: Bala's p^(3r) supercongruences
records.doc: For integers A ≥ 2 and B, C ≥ 1 let u(N) = Σ_{k=0}^{N} C(N+k−1, k)^A C(2N−2k, N−k)^B C(2k, k)^C. The package proves that u(np^r) ≡ u(np^{r−1}) (mod p^{3r}) for every prime p ≥ 5 and all n, r ≥ 1, as conjectured by Peter Bala (OEIS A364111, 2023), and the case (A, B, C) = (2, 1, 1), which is A364111 itself. The proof uses Coster's method, as Osburn and Sahu did for the generalized Domb numbers.

records.name: OeisA258377.isSolution_iff
records.entry_name: OEIS A258377–A258381: Bala's 2-adic periodicity for the type-B series
records.doc: For N ≥ 1 let A_N(z) = 1 + a(1)z + ⋯ be the series with A^(N+1)(z) = 1/(1 − z)·(BINOMIAL(BINOMIAL(A(z))))^N, where BINOMIAL is the binomial transform; A258377–A258381 are N = 1, …, 5. The package proves for every N that A_N exists, is unique and has integer coefficients, that every a(n) is odd, that a(n + 2^(k−1)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^k) for all k ≥ 1, and that for k ≥ 3 the least period of a(n) mod 2^k is exactly 2^(k−1) if and only if N ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4). This settles Peter Bala's 2017 observations on the five entries: odd terms for A258377, A258379 and A258381, period 2^(k−1) for A258377 and A258381, terms ≡ 1 (mod 4) for A258378 and ≡ 1 (mod 8) for A258380, periods dividing 2^(k−1) for A258378–A258380, and his worked examples modulo 4, 8, 16 and 32. His remarks on residues modulo 3 and 5 are not covered.

records.name: OeisA371710.a371710_existsUnique
records.entry_name: OEIS A371710: Hanna's mod-3 pattern
records.doc: The e.g.f. A(x) = Σ a(n)xⁿ/n! of OEIS A371710 satisfies Σ_{n≥0} (A(x)^n − x)^n/n! = 1. The package proves that exactly one A ∈ ℚ[[x]] does, that A(0) = 0 and every a(n) is an integer, and Paul D. Hanna's 2024 conjecture that a(6n + k) ≡ [2, 0, 2, 1, 2, 2](k) (mod 3) for n > 0 and k = 0, …, 5. It also proves the stronger pattern a(m) ≡ 2 for even m ≥ 2 and a(m) ≡ 1 − m for odd m ≥ 3, modulo 3.

records.name: LeanLab.Tolev2009.Decomp83.published_assembly
records.entry_name: The ternary Goldbach problem with primes from arithmetic progressions: Tolev's Bombieri-Vinogradov type mean value theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the main Theorem of D. I. Tolev, The ternary Goldbach problem with primes from arithmetic progressions, arXiv 0902.2669, 2009, display 5 on page 2. Let l3 be a fixed positive integer and lambda of k real numbers with absolute value at most 1. For every A > 0 there is B = B of A > 0 such that, for sufficiently large odd N and L = log N, the sum over k1, k2 up to sqrt N L^-B of the maximum over l1, l2 coprime to k1, k2 of the absolute value of the sum over k3 up to N^1/3 L^-B with k3 coprime to l3 of lambda of k3 times Delta_k,l of N is at most a constant times N^2 L^-A. Here Delta is the weighted count R of representations N = p1 + p2 + p3 with pi congruent to li mod ki, less the main term N^2 S / 2 phi of k1 phi of k2 phi of k3, with the singular series S written out by the formula printed in Halupczok 2008. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Codex by OpenAI, Claude by Anthropic and a lab prover agent, as listed in PORTING.md; the proof reuses code ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, written by its contributors, and is offered for human audit.

records.name: LeanLab.Kaniecki1995.not_lemma7_printed
records.entry_name: Sums of two odd primes in short intervals: a correction to Lemma 7 of Kaniecki's paper on Šnirelman's constant
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of a corrected form of Lemma 7 of L. Kaniecki, On Šnirelman's constant under the Riemann hypothesis, Acta Arith. 72, 1995, pages 361-374. Page 371 defines lambda of x as 2 for 0 < x <= 7 and, for x > 7, as the largest gap p' - p between a prime p <= x and the next prime p'. Lemma 7 as printed says that every open interval from x to x + lambda of lambda of x, x > 4, contains a sum of two odd primes. That statement is false: lambda of 6 = lambda of 2 = 2, and the open interval from 6 to 8 holds no even number; a numerical check by the lab found the failure at every even integer from 6 to 88 and nowhere else below 2000. The entry proves that the printed lemma is false, at the real point x = 6 and at the integer 6, and proves the corrected lemma with the right end included: for every real x > 4 there are odd primes p and q with x < p + q <= x + lambda of lambda of x, and the same for every integer x > 4 with lambda computed on the integers. The printed proof goes through with this change and a repair at x - p1 = 7. Section 3 of the paper applies the lemma only through closed intervals, which contain the half-open ones, so the paper's Theorem is not affected; that remark is not part of the formal statements. No compared theorem uses the Riemann hypothesis or any cited input. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: PLaplacian.pharmonious_exists_converge
records.entry_name: Convergence of the tug-of-war scheme for the normalized p-Laplacian
records.doc:
A Lean 4 formalization, on top of Mathlib, of the convergence of
p-harmonious functions, the solutions of the dynamic programming principle
of tug-of-war with noise, to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem
for the normalized p-Laplacian, 2 <= p < infinity, as the step size tends to
zero, on bounded open sets satisfying the exterior sphere condition with
continuous bounded boundary data. The compared theorem gives, for every step
size, a p-harmonious function with the given data, uniformly bounded, whose
half-relaxed limits agree on the closure of the domain, equal the data on
its boundary, and are the uniform limit of the family. The development also
proves the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity property of the
half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the
comparison principle and uniqueness for the limit equation, Aleksandrov's
theorem and Jensen's lemma.

records.name: EquivEmbed.gunther_fixed_point_equivariant
records.entry_name: Equivariant isometric embeddings via Günther's method
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the algebraic and functional-analytic core of a proof, by Günther's method, of the Moore–Schlafly theorem (Math. Z. 173, 1980): a compact Riemannian manifold with an isometric action of a compact Lie group has an isometric embedding into Euclidean space that is equivariant for an orthogonal representation. It proves unconditionally, with no analytic hypotheses, the equivariant Günther perturbation theorem on the flat torus ℝⁿ/2πℤⁿ: for a map u whose first and second derivatives have a dual frame, with Fourier coefficients in a weighted Wiener algebra, every small symmetric h is realized as a metric perturbation, ⟨∂ᵢ(u+v), ∂ⱼ(u+v)⟩ = ⟨∂ᵢu, ∂ⱼu⟩ + hᵢⱼ pointwise, with a linear bound on v, and u+v inherits every translation-and-rotation symmetry of the data and is real if the data are real. It also proves unconditionally the equivariant Günther fixed point theorem in a Banach space, together with the equivariance of its solution map and its Lipschitz dependence on the data; the uniqueness, least-norm property, equivariance and coordinate independence of the pointwise Nash–Günther right inverse; the freeness of the Veronese map; and the Haar-averaged invariant inner product used in the approximation step. It proves the main theorem for general compact manifolds only conditionally, from explicitly stated analytic hypotheses on an abstract embedding problem.

records.name: Crossing.four_thirds
records.entry_name: Lower bounds for Naslund's crossing problem
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib proofs of the first lower bounds above the trivial bound n for Naslund's crossing problem (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 174 (2020), Problem 12). P(n) is the least r + s such that the tensor [x1 = x4][x2 = x3] on [n]^4 is a sum of r tensors of rank one along {12|34} and s tensors of rank one along {13|24}; in matrix form, the least rank B + rank R(C) over all splittings S_n = B + C of the swap matrix, where R is the realignment. Over every field the project proves P(n) ≥ 4n/3 for n ≥ 3, P(n) ≥ 15n/11 for n ≥ 5, P(n) ≥ 67n/49 for n ≥ 7, P(n) ≥ n + 3 for n ≥ 4, P(5) ≥ 8, P(6) ≥ 9, and P(4) = 7 (with a split that attains 7). The results are original.

records.name: LeanLab.HelfgottPlatt.U1455.proth_iff
records.entry_name: Proth's criterion and the prime ladder reduction for ternary Goldbach up to 8.875 · 10^30
records.doc: Lean 4 proofs, with no unproved steps, of two results from H. A. Helfgott and D. J. Platt, Numerical verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture up to 8.875 · 10^30, Experimental Mathematics 22, 2013, arXiv:1305.3062. First, Proth's criterion of Section 2, Theorem 2.3 in existential form; the converse printed after it, for every such a, is proved as converse but not compared: a Proth number N = k 2^n + 1 with 0 < k < 2^n is prime if and only if some integer a has Jacobi symbol -1 over N and a raised to the power N - 1 over 2 is -1 mod N. Second, Theorem 4.1, every odd number from 7 to T = 8875694145621773516800000000000 is a sum of three primes, derived from the two computations the paper rests on, which are explicit hypotheses and are not proved here: binary Goldbach for every even number from 4 to 4 · 10^18, the verification of Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, and for each of the 492700 ranges of width 2^54 · 10^9 of Section 4 a ladder of odd primes with gaps at most 4 · 10^18 - 2 that starts within 2 · 10^18 above the left end point and ends less than 2 · 10^18 below the right end point, the paper's own computation. The entry does not verify any ladder or any binary Goldbach case, so it does not prove ternary Goldbach up to T; it proves that the paper's computations imply it. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem and binary Goldbach is open; neither is claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: LeanLab.Estermann1938.main
records.entry_name: On Goldbach's problem: proof that almost all even positive integers are sums of two primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the main result of T. Estermann, On Goldbach's problem: proof that almost all even positive integers are sums of two primes, Proc. London Math. Soc. series 2, volume 44, 1938, pages 307-314. Let Q of n be the number of even positive integers less than n that are not sums of two primes. The Introduction on page 307 states that, as n tends to infinity, Q of n is O of n log^-a n for every positive a; this is the compared theorem, LeanLab.Estermann1938.main. The proof is not Estermann's circle method text: it bounds Q of n by E of n plus 1, where E of X counts the even 4 <= m <= X that are not sums of two primes, and uses the bound E of X << X log^-A X for every A, proved by Heath-Brown's 1985 route from the Siegel-Walfisz theorem. That bound is already a compared theorem of the registered entry heathbrown1985 of this repository, LeanLab.PNTPort.PsiChi.goldbach_logPowerSaving, whose Challenge states the same E of X bound; this entry adds Estermann's own count Q of n and his big O form, and the Lean closure is the same as that entry's plus one file. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents, Claude by Anthropic, wrote the lab's Lean code; the ported zeta function code is by the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd contributors, as listed in PORTING.md. It is offered for human audit.

records.name: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19.conjecture19
records.entry_name: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 19: lower bound on the largest induced bipartite subgraph size from average eccentricity and neighborhood independence
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 19 from E. DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc) collection, matching the exact statement in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19.conjecture19). For every finite, nontrivial, connected simple graph G, the size b(G) of a largest induced bipartite subgraph is bounded below by the floor of the sum of the average vertex eccentricity and the maximum local neighborhood independence number sup_v l(v). The proof picks a vertex u maximising l(u), sets e = (G.eccent u).toNat and D = G.diam, and constructs an induced bipartite subgraph as a disjoint union of independent subsets B_d inside the distance spheres {v | G.dist u v = d} colored by distance parity. When D ≤ e, one geodesic vertex per sphere 2 ≤ d ≤ e together with {u} and an independent neighborhood subset I ⊆ N(u) of size l(u) gives b(G) ≥ e + l(u). When e < D, the average eccentricity is strictly less than D, and pairing geodesic vertices from u toward a diametral pair x, y on overlapping spheres (separated by distance at least 2 via the triangle inequality) gives b(G) ≥ D − 1 + l(u). The proof uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorry and no native_decide.

records.name: Projectivization.wigner
records.entry_name: Wigner's theorem for the rays of C^N: unitary or antiunitary, unique up to a phase
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of Wigner's theorem for the complex projective space of C^N. Let f be any map from rays to rays that preserves the transition probability |<psi, phi>|^2 / (|psi|^2 |phi|^2). Then f is induced by a unitary or by an antiunitary (a unitary after coordinatewise complex conjugation), and in each case the inducing operator is unique up to a global phase. Nothing else is assumed about f: not linearity, not continuity, not bijectivity. The theorem is stated twice, with linear isometries (wigner, wigner_unique, wigner_unique_antiunitary) and with unitary matrices acting on rays (wigner_unitaryGroup, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique_antiunitary). Mathlib, at the pinned commit, has no Wigner theorem. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 2 July 2026 (commit c26c0954). Two other Lean proofs are listed under related_formalizations: one for maps on unit vectors of C^n, completed on 13 July 2026, and one whose existence theorem covers complex Hilbert spaces of any dimension, at a snapshot dated 31 October 2026. This proof is independent of both. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.

This proof is independent of both. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.

records.name: OeisA003024.gauss_congruence
records.entry_name: OEIS A003024 and A188457: Bala's exp-integrality conjectures, with Gauss congruences for every q
records.doc: For an integer q let a_q(0) = 1 and a_q(n) = Σ_{k=1}^n (−1)^(k+1) C(n,k) q^(k(n−k)) a_q(n−k). Then a_2 is OEIS A003024 (labeled acyclic digraphs) and a_3 is OEIS A188457 (acyclic 2-multidigraphs). The package proves the Gauss congruences a_q(np^r) ≡ a_q(np^(r−1)) (mod p^r) for every integer q, every prime p and all n, r ≥ 1. Hence exp(Σ_{n≥1} a_q(n) xⁿ/n) has integer coefficients for every q. The cases q = 2 and q = 3 are Peter Bala's 2016 conjectures in A003024 and A188457; the first also shows that every term of A188490 is an integer.

records.name: OeisA372211.u_tower
records.entry_name: OEIS A372211–A372213 and A351859: Bala's p^(3k) towers for [x^(rN)] f^(sN), f = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 − x^a)^a (1 − x^b)^b)
records.doc: For a, b ≥ 1 and m = a + b let f(x) = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 − x^a)^a (1 − x^b)^b) and u_{r,s}(N) = [x^(rN)] f(x)^(sN). The package proves the supercongruences u_{r,s}(np^k) ≡ u_{r,s}(np^(k−1)) (mod p^(3k)) for every prime p ≥ 5 with p ∤ abm, all r ≥ 1, s ∈ ℤ and n, k ≥ 1, and the same for Bala's variant f⁻(x) = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 + x^a)^a (1 + x^b)^b). As corollaries it proves Peter Bala's 2024 conjectures for A372212 ((a, b) = (2, 5), p ≥ 11), A372213 ((3, 4), p ≥ 11, and also p = 5), A372211 ((2, 3), p ≥ 7, both forms), his 2022 conjectures for A351859 (G₃ = (1 + x + x² + x³)⁴/(1 + x + x²)³, p ≥ 5, both forms), and his general clauses for all (a, b) and sufficiently large p, for f and for f⁻ (both read with the power n, as [x^n] f(x)^n and [x^n] f⁻(x)^n). A372211 at p = 5 is not claimed; it is open. For a = b = 1, u_{1,1}(n) = C(2n, n), and the towers are the classical Jacobsthal–Kazandzidis congruences (see Meštrović's survey, cited in A351859). Supercongruences of this strength for diagonals of rational functions are studied for Apéry-like numbers (Straub, Algebra Number Theory 8 (2014)) and for framings of rational functions (Müller, arXiv:2104.10754).

records.name: Erdos593.TripleSystem.isolatedReduction_inc
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 593: classification of obligatory triple systems
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the finite classification of obligatory triple systems. For every finite edge-indexed simple 3-uniform hypergraph F, the compared theorem proves that F is obligatory if and only if its isolated-point reduction is linear, every hyperedge-node of its Levi graph is incident with a bridge, and every Berge cycle has even length.

records.name: CDRBicolour.KBicolor.kbicolour_completion_types_exact
records.entry_name: Prescribed block types and abundance in bicolored Steiner triple systems
records.doc: Four Lean results for bicolored Steiner triple systems. For each fixed number k >= 3 of color classes, sufficiently large compatible labelled profiles with positive class and type margins admit exact prescribed block-type counts while completing any sufficiently sparse allowed packing. Uniformly over such prescribed matrices, the logarithm of the number of realizations has optimal leading coefficient 1/6 in n squared times log n. For any fixed K, the same exact type matrix has K realizations with distinct Pasch counts. For every fixed k >= 4, all sufficiently large admissible orders admit a k-bicoloring. The final threshold is ineffective.

records.name: OeisA000464.not_conjecture1
records.entry_name: OEIS A000464: Bala's conjectures for sin x / cos 2x
records.doc: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] sin x / cos 2x (OEIS A000464: 1, 11, 361, 24611, …; Glaisher, 1914). Peter Bala made four conjectures on it in 2021. The package refutes the first as stated: modulo every multiple of 81, (a(n))_{n≥1} is not purely periodic with any period, because a(55) ≡ 65 ≢ 11 = a(1) (mod 81). It proves the corrected form, a(n + φ(k)) ≡ a(n) (mod k) whenever 2n + 1 is at least the exponent of every odd prime in k, so the conjecture holds eventually for every k and from n = 1 when no odd prime exponent of k exceeds 3. It proves the other three conjectures: the Gauss congruences a(np^k + i) ≡ a(np^(k−1) + i) (mod p^k) for every shift i, with the integrality of exp(Σ a(n+i) x^n/n); a(mn) ≡ a(m)^n (mod 2^(2v₂(m)+4)); and a(2mn) ≡ a(n)^(2m), a((2m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(2m+1) (mod 2^(v₂(m)+4)). Behind them are a(n + 2^(e−1)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for every n, and a(n + (p−1)p^(e−1)/2) ≡ (−1)^((p−1)/2) a(n) (mod p^e) for odd primes p and 2n + 1 ≥ e. The period can be sharpened from φ(k) to the Carmichael function λ(k): a(n + 2^(e−2)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for e ≥ 3, so a(n + λ(k)) ≡ a(n) (mod k) under the same condition on n, and λ(8) = 2 cannot be lowered, since a(1) ≢ a(0) (mod 8). Bala's congruence conjectures for exponential generating functions are recent targets in the study of congruences for Euler-type numbers: Kallat proved Bala's conjectures for A158690 (arXiv:2609.07238), and Blanco Gómez refuted the same pure-periodicity wording for the Euler numbers A000364 and proved its eventual form (Zenodo 23150466, Theorem 2.2). The odd-prime congruence is known (Blanco Gómez, Zenodo 23407292, Theorem 1), and the 2-adic period follows quickly from Nishibuchi's criterion (arXiv:2610.11648, Prop. 3.4). No earlier treatment of the failure modulo 81 or of the power congruences 3) and 4) was found.

records.name: Couret.PalomarCubic.two_cubic_coordinates
records.entry_name: Two fixed cubic coefficients distinguish a cyclic four-point square fibre
records.doc: For a four-point support in Z/nZ with n positive and its full labelled ordered square supplied, at most two fixed labelled coefficients of the ordered cube separate the complete four-point square fibre. Coefficient responses are exact integer values embedded in the reals; they are not binary answers. No query lower bound or runtime claim is asserted.

records.name: OeisA339946.am_congr
records.entry_name: OEIS A339946 and A361717: Bala's prime-level supercongruences
records.doc: Let a_m(n) = [x^(mn)] 1/P_n((1−x)/(1+x)), where P_n is the Legendre polynomial; OEIS A339946 is the case m = 1. The package proves Peter Bala's 2022 conjecture that a_m(p) ≡ a_m(1) = 2 (mod p^5) for every m ≥ 1 and every prime p ≥ 7, and with it his 2020 conjecture a(p) ≡ a(1) (mod p^5) for A339946. It shows that the range p ≥ 7 is optimal: a_m(5) ≡ 2 + 625m² (mod 5^5), so the congruence at p = 5 holds exactly when 5 divides m. It also proves Bala's Conjecture 2 for OEIS A361717: Σ_{k=0}^{p−2} C(p−2, k)² C(p−1+k, k) ≡ 1 − 2p − p² (mod p³) for every prime p ≠ 3. Bala's entry lists A103882 and the Apéry numbers A005258 and A005259 as coefficients of similar Legendre-polynomial expressions that satisfy supercongruences u(np^k) ≡ u(np^(k−1)) (mod p^(3k)), and it presents a(p) ≡ a(1) (mod p^5) as a stronger congruence. A361717 is of the same type: A005258(n) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−1) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) and A361717(n+1) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−2) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) (Bala, December 2020 and August 2026). Supercongruences of Apéry-like sequences are a research topic; see Straub (Algebra & Number Theory, 2014) and the references there.

It also proves Bala's Conjecture 2 for OEIS A361717: Σ_{k=0}^{p−2} C(p−2, k)² C(p−1+k, k) ≡ 1 − 2p − p² (mod p³) for every prime p ≠ 3. Bala's entry lists A103882 and the Apéry numbers A005258 and A005259 as coefficients of similar Legendre-polynomial expressions that satisfy supercongruences u(np^k) ≡ u(np^(k−1)) (mod p^(3k)), and it presents a(p) ≡ a(1) (mod p^5) as a stronger congruence. A361717 is of the same type: A005258(n) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−1) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) and A361717(n+1) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−2) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) (Bala, December 2020 and August 2026). Supercongruences of Apéry-like sequences are a research topic; see Straub (Algebra & Number Theory, 2014) and the references there.

records.name: OeisA012780.bala_conjecture
records.entry_name: OEIS A012780: Bala's periodicity conjecture for arcsin(tan x)
records.doc: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] arcsin(tan x) (OEIS A012780). The package proves that every a(n) is an integer and Peter Bala's 2026 conjecture that a(n) mod k is eventually periodic with period dividing φ(k), for every k ≥ 1. It also proves the prime-power congruences behind it: a(n + 2^(e−1)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for all n, and a(n + φ(p^e)) ≡ a(n) (mod p^e) for odd primes p and 2n ≥ e, and the conjecture with that explicit pre-period. It also proves that a(n + 2) ≢ a(n) (mod 8) for every n, so the Carmichael function λ(k) cannot replace φ(k). Bala's φ(k)-periodicity conjectures for exponential generating functions are recent research targets: Kallat proved Bala's conjectures for A158690 (arXiv:2609.07238), and Blanco Gómez proved the φ(k)-period for the Euler numbers A000364, where Bala's stronger claim of pure periodicity fails (Zenodo 23150466, Theorem 2.2). Kallat's general theorem gives λ(k)-periods, so by the mod-8 result it does not cover A012780.

records.name: LeanLab.Pintz2018.Greedy117.theoremK_ordered_integral
records.entry_name: The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem: the weighted density and optimisation steps
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the elementary core of the method of J. Pintz, A new explicit formula in the additive theory of primes with applications II. The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem, arXiv 1804.09084v2, 2018, whose Theorem 1 is E of X below X to the power 0.72. Pintz turns zero density theorems for Dirichlet L-functions into explicit bounds through two new steps, which this entry proves. Theorem K, display 4.41, solves the extremal problem of displays 4.37 to 4.39: among decreasing configurations d_1 at least d_2 and so on, with caps d_j at most e_j and a density budget, a maximiser of the sum of e to the B d_j minus e to the C d_j saturates every coordinate before its last active one. The proof is the exchange argument of displays 8.10 to 8.16, done here with the cost in the integral form of display 8.11, and a second theorem adds for an abstract concave cost that the budget is used up exactly and the last active coordinate solves the residual equation 4.42. Theorem J, display 4.36, bounds the weighted excess of zeros by 1 minus xi over 2 Delta; it is proved here from the analytic estimate 7.20, which is a hypothesis. Two Section 9 statements are proved in the repository but are outside this submission's selected Comparator check: the basic inequality 9.4 in the form used in 9.22, and Case 8, where e to the minus 7 lambda plus 2.87 times 10.4 times lambda to the 11/7 is below 1 for 0 below lambda at most 0.04. The zero density theorems, the estimate 7.20, the existence of a maximiser and Theorem 1 are not proved and not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, Codex by OpenAI and Gemini by Google, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: FourierTreeRIP.broom_lower_bound
records.entry_name: A Quadratic Lower Bound for Fourier RIP with Tree-Structured Sparsity
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of an explicit lower bound for uniformly row-subsampled discrete Fourier transforms acting on canonical binary-heap tree-sparse vectors. With constant distortion, at least half of frequency sequences violate tree-RIP when 20000 m <= k min(k, log_2(N/k)), with an explicit quadratic corollary. The proof uses broom supports, Fejer-kernel concentration, simultaneous Diophantine approximation, and finite counting. A full-DFT isometry theorem checks the normalization and nonvacuity of the definitions.

records.name: OeisA357559.S_two_dvd
records.entry_name: OEIS A357559: Bala's divisibility conjectures for k^m-weighted Apéry sums (m = 2, 3)
records.doc: Let S_m(n) = Σ_{k=0}^n (−1)^(n+k) k^m C(n,k) C(n+k,k)²; S_3 is OEIS A357559 and S_0 is the Apéry sequence A005258. The package proves Peter Bala's 2022 Conjecture 1, n²(2n+1)² ∣ S_2(2n), and the conjecture in the entry's formula section, n²(2n+1)³ ∣ 3·S_3(2n), for every n ≥ 0. Both follow from stronger statements for every n: n²(n+1)² ∣ 2S_2(n), with n²(n+1)² ∣ S_2(n) for odd n, and n²(n+1)³ ∣ 6S_3(n). These give an extra factor 2 in both conjectures. The constants 2 and 6 cannot be lowered: 36 ∤ S_2(2) = 126, 8 ∤ 3S_3(1) = 12 and 576 ∤ 2S_3(3) = 16896. Bala's Conjectures 2 and 3, for m ≥ 4, are not treated. Divisibility theorems for binomial sums of this kind, including weighted sums of Apéry numbers, are a research topic: see Guo and Zeng (Int. J. Number Theory 2011 and 2012) and Guo's proof of a divisibility conjecture of Z.-W. Sun (Electron. J. Combin. 2013).

records.name: OeisA002439.conjecture3_two
records.entry_name: OEIS A002439: Bala's conjectures for sin 2x / (2 cos 3x)
records.doc: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] sin 2x / (2 cos 3x) (OEIS A002439, Glaisher's T numbers: 1, 23, 1681, 257543, …; Glaisher, 1899). Up to a sign and a factor 1/2, a(n) is the value at −2n − 1 of the Dirichlet L-function of the real character χ₁₂ modulo 12, so these are congruences for values of Dirichlet L-functions. In 2021 Peter Bala conjectured six families of congruences for a(n) and stated the formula a(n) ≡ 23^n (mod 1152). The package proves his power congruences 3)–5): a(mn) ≡ a(m)^n modulo 2^(2v₂(m)+7) and modulo 3^(2v₃(m)+2); a(2mn) ≡ a(n)^(2m) and a((2m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(2m+1) modulo 2^(v₂(m)+7); a(3mn) ≡ a(n)^(3m) and a((3m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(3m+1) modulo 3^(v₃(m)+2), and even modulo 3^(v₃(m)+3); and a((3m+2)n) ≡ a(n)^(3m+2) modulo 9. It proves the formula a(n) ≡ 23^n (mod 1152). records.name: OeisA340882.not_conjecture_A340882
records.entry_name: OEIS A340882 and A340883: Bala's pre-period conjectures, refuted, with the exact pre-period
records.doc: Peter Bala (OEIS, February 2021) defined the polynomials R(n, q) = Σ_{k<n} x^(k²) Π_{j=k+1}^{n−1} (x^(2j) − 1), x = 1 + q, as the rows of a q-series (OEIS A340882); their values a(n) = R(n, 1) are A340883 (1, 5, 91, 6245, …). He noted that, q-adically, R(2n + 1, q − 1) and −R(2n, q − 1) tend to Euler's product Π(1 − q^n). He conjectured that for all integers q and N the sequence R(n, q) mod N is purely periodic or periodic after one term (A340882), and that A340883 modulo m has pre-period 0 or 1 and least period dividing φ(m) (A340883, conjecture 1). The package refutes both conjectures and gives the exact answer. For every q and N ≥ 1 it determines the pre-period of R(n, q) mod N: the maximum, over the primes p dividing both N and 1 + q, of an explicit function of v_p(N) and v_p(1 + q). So A340882 holds for (q, N) exactly when 1 + q = 0 or v_p(N) ≤ 5 v_p(1 + q) for every such prime, and it holds for every N exactly when q ∈ {−2, −1, 0}. For A340883 the pre-period is at most 1 exactly when 64 ∤ m (modulo 64 the sequence is 1, 5, 27, 37, 27, 37, …), while the period part, a(n + φ(m)) ≡ a(n) (mod m) after the pre-period, holds for every m. The proof starts from the recurrence R(n + 1) = (x^(2n) − 1) R(n) + x^(n²). For a prime p ∤ x and x^o ≡ 1 (mod p^e), the first o terms of the sum for R(n + o) vanish modulo p^e and the others match those of R(n). For p ∣ x, the exact valuations v_p(R(n + 2) − R(n)) = c(n) v_p(x), with c(1) = 1, c(2) = 5 and c(n) = 2n for n ≥ 3, give the pre-period modulo p^e, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives it modulo N. For completeness the package also proves Bala's conjecture 2) for A340883: for coprime m₁ and m₂ the period modulo m₁m₂ is the lcm of the two periods. This is the Chinese remainder theorem for sequences that are eventually periodic modulo every m, and it is not claimed as new. The audience is number theorists who study congruences and periodicity modulo m of sequences defined by q-series. Bala's periodicity conjecture for A158690, whose e.g.f. 1 + Σ_{m≥1} Π_{j=1}^{m} (1 − e^(−(2j−1)t)) uses the same products Π(1 − x^(2j−1)), was proved in a recent note (Kallat, arXiv:2609.07238): the sequence is eventually periodic modulo every k with period dividing φ(k). That note gives a pre-period bound that it does not claim to be sharp; for A340882 this package determines the pre-period exactly. Bala's companion conjectures for A340881 were proved in 2026 (umaia1234/agentic-conjectures), and those for A340880 are not part of this package. No earlier treatment of A340882 or of A340883's conjecture 1) was found.

records.doc: Peter Bala (OEIS, February 2021) defined the polynomials R(n, q) = Σ_{k<n} x^(k²) Π_{j=k+1}^{n−1} (x^(2j) − 1), x = 1 + q, as the rows of a q-series (OEIS A340882); their values a(n) = R(n, 1) are A340883 (1, 5, 91, 6245, …). He noted that, q-adically, R(2n + 1, q − 1) and −R(2n, q − 1) tend to Euler's product Π(1 − q^n). He conjectured that for all integers q and N the sequence R(n, q) mod N is purely periodic or periodic after one term (A340882), and that A340883 modulo m has pre-period 0 or 1 and least period dividing φ(m) (A340883, conjecture 1). The package refutes both conjectures and gives the exact answer. For every q and N ≥ 1 it determines the pre-period of R(n, q) mod N: the maximum, over the primes p dividing both N and 1 + q, of an explicit function of v_p(N) and v_p(1 + q). So A340882 holds for (q, N) exactly when 1 + q = 0 or v_p(N) ≤ 5 v_p(1 + q) for every such prime, and it holds for every N exactly when q ∈ {−2, −1, 0}. For A340883 the pre-period is at most 1 exactly when 64 ∤ m (modulo 64 the sequence is 1, 5, 27, 37, 27, 37, …), while the period part, a(n + φ(m)) ≡ a(n) (mod m) after the pre-period, holds for every m. The proof starts from the recurrence R(n + 1) = (x^(2n) − 1) R(n) + x^(n²). For a prime p ∤ x and x^o ≡ 1 (mod p^e), the first o terms of the sum for R(n + o) vanish modulo p^e and the others match those of R(n). For p ∣ x, the exact valuations v_p(R(n + 2) − R(n)) = c(n) v_p(x), with c(1) = 1, c(2) = 5 and c(n) = 2n for n ≥ 3, give the pre-period modulo p^e, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives it modulo N. For completeness the package also proves Bala's conjecture 2) for A340883: for coprime m₁ and m₂ the period modulo m₁m₂ is the lcm of the two periods. This is the Chinese remainder theorem for sequences that are eventually periodic modulo every m, and it is not claimed as new. The audience is number theorists who study congruences and periodicity modulo m of sequences defined by q-series. Bala's periodicity conjecture for A158690, whose e.g.f. 1 + Σ_{m≥1} Π_{j=1}^{m} (1 − e^(−(2j−1)t)) uses the same products Π(1 − x^(2j−1)), was proved in a recent note (Kallat, arXiv:2609.07238): the sequence is eventually periodic modulo every k with period dividing φ(k). That note gives a pre-period bound that it does not claim to be sharp; for A340882 this package determines the pre-period exactly. Bala's companion conjectures for A340881 were proved in 2026 (umaia1234/agentic-conjectures), and those for A340880 are not part of this package. No earlier treatment of A340882 or of A340883's conjecture 1) was found.

For a prime p ∤ x and x^o ≡ 1 (mod p^e), the first o terms of the sum for R(n + o) vanish modulo p^e and the others match those of R(n). For p ∣ x, the exact valuations v_p(R(n + 2) − R(n)) = c(n) v_p(x), with c(1) = 1, c(2) = 5 and c(n) = 2n for n ≥ 3, give the pre-period modulo p^e, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives it modulo N. For completeness the package also proves Bala's conjecture 2) for A340883: for coprime m₁ and m₂ the period modulo m₁m₂ is the lcm of the two periods. This is the Chinese remainder theorem for sequences that are eventually periodic modulo every m, and it is not claimed as new. The audience is number theorists who study congruences and periodicity modulo m of sequences defined by q-series. Bala's periodicity conjecture for A158690, whose e.g.f. 1 + Σ_{m≥1} Π_{j=1}^{m} (1 − e^(−(2j−1)t)) uses the same products Π(1 − x^(2j−1)), was proved in a recent note (Kallat, arXiv:2609.07238): the sequence is eventually periodic modulo every k with period dividing φ(k). That note gives a pre-period bound that it does not claim to be sharp; for A340882 this package determines the pre-period exactly. Bala's companion conjectures for A340881 were proved in 2026 (umaia1234/agentic-conjectures), and those for A340880 are not part of this package. No earlier treatment of A340882 or of A340883's conjecture 1) was found.

records.name: IntegralGeneratorHeights.mulHeight₁_le_mulHeight₁_ρQ_iff
records.entry_name: The integral generators of least Mahler measure of the field of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of three statements, all about one field. Let L = QQ(rho, Q) be the field generated over the rationals QQ by a root rho of x^3 - x - 1 and a root Q of x^4 - x - 1, a number field of degree 12 (below, QQ denotes the rationals and Q the root). For a number field K and x in K write H(x) = Height.mulHeight1 x for Mathlib's multiplicative height of x relative to K (the [K:QQ]-th power of the absolute Weil height), and T2(x) = sum over the [K:QQ] ring homomorphisms sigma : K -> C of |sigma x|^2. M(x) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of an algebraic integer x over Z. (1) The nonzero algebraic integers x of L with H(x) <= H(rho Q) are exactly the fourteen elements +-1, +-rho^(+-1), +-Q^(+-1), +-(rho Q)^(+-1). (2) Every algebraic integer x of L with QQ(x) = L has M(rho Q) <= M(x), with equality exactly for x in {rho Q, -rho Q, (rho Q)^-1, -(rho Q)^-1}; since rho Q generates L (proved in the repository, not compared), the least Mahler measure of an integral generator of L (Dubickas's M(O_L)) is M(rho Q), attained at these four elements only. (3) Let x be an algebraic integer of L with QQ(x) = L such that M(x) <= M(y) for every algebraic integer y of L with QQ(y) = L, and such that sigma(x) is a real Perron number (Lind's definition) for some embedding sigma : L -> C; then x = rho Q (one direction only: that rho Q satisfies these hypotheses is proved in the repository, HeightT2.ρQ_perronNumber_generator_selected, and not compared). The Challenge imports Mathlib only and carries the definition block of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (the field L and its elements) and one definition of this entry (IsPerronNumber). Proved in the repository and not compared, none claimed as this entry's: (i) the inequality T2(x) <= H(x)^2 + n - 1 for x in a number field of degree n, which is Lemma 6 of Dubickas (Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 39 (2023)) applied to the squares max(1, |sigma x|)^2; (ii) its case of equality, T2(x) = H(x)^2 + (n - 1) exactly when x is a root of unity (for n >= 2; HeightT2.sum_norm_sq_eq_mulHeight₁_sq_add_iff); Lemma 6 states no case of equality, no statement of it in print was located (README.md, "Relation to the literature", lists where it was searched) and novelty is not claimed; (iii) the identity that, for subfields K1, K2 of a number field E, linearly disjoint over QQ with K1 v K2 = E, the T2 Gram matrix of the product family b_i c_j is the Kronecker product of the T2 Gram matrices G_b and G_c of b and c (the T2 Gram matrix of a family b in a number field K has entries sum over sigma : K -> C of sigma(b_i) conj(sigma(b_k))) (HeightT2.t2Gram_compositum); special cases are in print (Popov and Zarhin 2021, Lemma 8(iii), coprime cyclotomic fields; Lyubashevsky, Peikert and Regev 2013, eq. (2.6); Bayer-Fluckiger, Oggier and Viterbo 2004, Prop. 6, totally real Galois fields with coprime discriminants), it is the Hermitian counterpart of the trace-form identity of the author's entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 (statement 3), on a totally real field the T2 Gram matrix is the trace Gram matrix, and novelty is not claimed; (iv) the coordinate bound (HeightT2.coord_sq_le_sum_norm_sq): with b, c finite and E_ii the diagonal matrix unit at (i, i), if s, t >= 0 and Re G_b - s E_ii and Re G_c - t E_jj are positive semidefinite, then every rational coefficient vector a satisfies s t a_ij^2 <= T2(sum a_kl b_k c_l), with T2 taken in E; for families that are bases it is the bound (2.9) of Fincke and Pohst (1985) applied to the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices, it also covers singular Gram matrices, and novelty is not claimed; (v) that rho Q satisfies the hypotheses of statement (3). The proofs of the three compared statements use the instance of (i) for L in the copied library (RulerSelection.Emb.T2_le_embHeight_sq_add) and a direct proof of the content of (iii) for L and its power bases (RulerSelection.Emb.T2_coords, from RulerSelection.Emb.sum_norm_sq_tensor); they use neither (ii) nor the theorems (iii) and (iv) as stated; (iv) is proved from the matrix lemma RulerSelection.Kron.kron_ge_diag that they use (README.md, "The proofs").

records.name: CanonicalRV.encodedRv_surjective
records.entry_name: Integration in algebraically closed valued fields
records.doc: Two geometric preparation theorems for integration in algebraically closed valued fields. Proposition 3.19 partitions an original-base definable VF bijection into finitely many definable pieces on which it is open-to-open. Lemma 4.8 decomposes an original-Gamma-base definable subset of VF squared into two-cell fibres of a definable map to a finite RV power. The cell positioning graph and both paradigms are definable over the original base together with the output RV tuple. Actual saturation, characteristic, parameter-base and named-value hypotheses remain in the formal statements. The larger repository develops Sections 2–7, including ordinary and measured integration; those additional results are outside this Palomar selection.
