records.name: KulaichevYantra.kulaichev_unique
records.entry_name: Kulaichev's Sri Yantra is unique
records.doc: Nine isosceles triangles with a common axis in a circle of diameter 1 that meet Huet's conditions in Chiodo's form (the two great triangles inscribed, seven apexes on bases, the 18 marmas and the 6 corner touches), Kulaichev's four conditions (a)-(d) and the admissibility of DICTO's paper #103 (Theorem 1) form exactly one figure (identified with the yantra of #103 Theorem 10 through the slope interval). Its slope w7/b7 is proved to lie in an interval of width 2^-21, [0.7504382776..., 0.7504387544...]; #103 gives the slope as 0.7504385160222140244..., a value computed outside Lean that lies in this interval. This settles Kulaichev's 1984 uniqueness question for admissible (well-formed) figures. The proof combines a kernel-checked branch-and-bound interval certificate (64,613 boxes in 10 charts, with proved monotone-split and slope enclosures), a Krawczyk box (uniqueness by a contraction, existence by Banach's fixed-point theorem), the forced construction from the geometry, and a verified sparse-polynomial normaliser for the identities between them. Not formalised: DICTO's study (outside Lean) finds one other real solution of the same equations, at w7/b7 = 0.66866..., which is not admissible (bases out of order, two negative half-widths), so it is not a yantra. Audiences: the history of mathematics (Kulaichev's question in the Indian Journal of History of Science, called still open in 2021), sacred geometry (the construction of the Sri Yantra), and computer-assisted proof in geometry (a certified interval computation checked by Lean's kernel).

records.name: PrimeCarleson.Palomar.variation_norm_prime_carleson
records.entry_name: A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the two main theorems of Fragkos, Krause, Miheisi and Sun, A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes. For finitely supported f on the integers, consider the modulated sums S_λ f(x) = Σ_{n ≠ 0} f(x − n) Λ(|n|) e(λn)/n, with Λ the von Mangoldt function and e(t) = exp(2πit). Theorem 1.3: for every r > 2 the r-variation of S_λ f(x) over λ in [0, 1) is bounded on ℓ^p(ℤ) for c(r) < p < C(r), where r' < c(r) < 2 < C(r), c(r) → 1 and C(r) → ∞ as r → ∞. Theorem 1.4: the supremum of |S_λ f(x)| over λ in [0, 1) is bounded on ℓ^p(ℤ) for every 1 < p < ∞. The results of other papers that the proofs use are proved in the repository, among them the variation norm Carleson theorem on the real line (Oberlin, Seeger, Tao, Thiele, Wright), the Magyar–Stein–Wainger transference principle for variation norms and the U³ approximation of the von Mangoldt function; none is assumed. The U³ approximation is proved here from the classical zero-free region and the absence of Landau–Siegel zeros, a Lean proof vendored from the openai/math library.

records.name: solovay_kitaev
records.entry_name: The Solovay-Kitaev theorem for Clifford+T words, with the Dawson-Nielsen exponent
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of the Solovay-Kitaev theorem for single-qubit Clifford+T circuits. A word is a finite sequence of the letters H, T and T^-1 (with T^-1 = T^7), and its value is the product of the letters' 2 x 2 matrices. There are constants K > 0 and e > 0 such that for every epsilon with 0 < epsilon <= e, every U in SU(2) is within epsilon of the value of a word of length at most K log(1/epsilon)^c, in the operator norm, where c = log 5 / log(3/2), about 3.97, is Dawson and Nielsen's exponent. A second theorem places c strictly between 3 and 4. The word approximates U itself, not U up to a phase. K and e are not computed. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 6 October 2026 (commit 01e973e9). The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.

records.name: DesignsII.TParams.lemma_3_8
records.entry_name: Keevash, The existence of designs II, Lemma 3.8 (ext*): extensions in the random algebraic template
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Lemma 3.8 (Lemma ext*) of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900): in the random algebraic template M* built from independent uniform injections f_j : [n] → F_{p^a}-like field K (j < z), random colours T_e and orders π_e of the r-sets, random A_φ and activations, the number of configurations of an extension all of whose atoms γ(ψ) lie below ∂^γ M* is at least an explicit expectation-type lower bound minus 2εN^v, except with an explicit failure probability (a with-high-probability statement in the regime described below). The statement DesignsII.TParams.lemma_3_8 is fully quantitative, an explicit finite-N bound: the lower bound is |C|·(z+1−kd)_m·(a^m − m²·K_c·(n^(q−r))^(m−2))·p^m − 2εN^v (K_c occurs once, also for m = 2) with a = ω|V(Φ)|^(q−r) − (q−r)·s·n^(q−r−1), K_c = q^(r+1) n^(q−r−1) q^r n^(q−r) (1+C(q,r)) and p = (2N^(q−r))^(-1) z^(-C(q,r)) ((q−r)!/q!)^C(q,r) |𝒜|^(-1) k_min/N_act, and the failure probability is at most C(z,kd)·p_deg^kd + 2exp(−ε²N/(2c₁)) + 2exp(−ε²N/(2c₂)) with explicit constants c₁ = c₁(z,q,r,m,Δ) and c₂ = c₂(z,q,r,m,Δ,Smax), where Smax bounds the sizes of the non-colour coordinates (|𝒜|, N_act, ...) (p_deg = |F|^s N^(s−1) (N−s)!/N! bounds the probability that a colour is degenerate at the s fixed vertices). The bound holds for all permitted parameters. Asymptotic remarks (the Lean theorem itself is a finite-N inequality): every term of the failure probability tends to 0 as N → ∞ when s ≥ 1, 1 ≤ kd ≤ z and z, q, r, m, Δ, Smax, |F|, s, kd and ε > 0 are fixed (it does not for kd = 0 or s = 0). No claim is made that the lower bound is positive: for m ≥ 1 it is ≤ 0 for instance if m > z+1−kd, k_min = 0 or a ≤ 0, and for any m if 2εN^v exceeds the main term (for m = 0, the empty configuration, the main term is |C|). When q > r and m ≥ 2 the correction is at most a constant times n^((q−r)m−1), hence o(a^m) if moreover a ≥ c·n^(q−r) for a fixed c > 0; when q = r or m = 1 it need not be of lower order. The hypotheses are those of the paper: Φ is a Σ-adapted [q]-complex, (Φ, γ[G]) is (ω,h)-extendable (Definition 2.9), the copies used are Φ-embeddings of A = Σ^≤ and those with γ(φ) ≤_γ G are activated with threshold ≥ k_min. The proof follows the paper (Lemma e|E for the conditional probabilities given the fixed vertices, a two-stage Lipschitz concentration for the covering count, the template decomposition of Designs I Lemma 3.3), with the corrections recorded under fidelity. Mathlib does not contain this result.

records.name: TemporalCliqueSpanners.exists_isTemporalSpanner_card_le_seven_mul
records.entry_name: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry. This repository is a thin wrapper: it contains only the statement and the bridge to the temporal-graphs library, the substantive formalization, on which it depends through its lakefile at the commit given below (release alpha-0.2.0 of the library, on its branch prepared for Palomar). The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.

records.name: FastDynamoChallenge.fast_dynamo_zero_entropy
records.entry_name: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalisation, built on mathlib, of L. Niebel, "A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy" (arXiv:2608.02586v3), an arXiv preprint. The fast-dynamo question, going back to Vainshtein and Zel'dovich, asks whether the exponential growth rate of the magnetic field in the kinematic induction equation survives the limit of vanishing magnetic diffusivity; for autonomous velocities on the flat three-torus it is the conjecture recorded as Problem 1994-28 in Arnold's Problems (Conjecture 1.1 of the paper), which asks for a smooth velocity. For sufficiently smooth velocities the absence of exponential particle stretching excludes fast dynamo action (Vishik; Friedlander and Vishik), and the entropy bound of Klapper and Young excludes a C^infinity fast dynamo with zero topological entropy; the paper shows that at Lipschitz regularity fast dynamo action is compatible with zero topological entropy and zero ideal exponential growth. The theorem concerns Lipschitz velocities and does not address the smooth conjecture, which, as Remark 1.3 of the paper records, has been resolved (Coti Zelati, Sorella and Villringer, arXiv:2609.04153). The compared theorem is Theorem 1.2 of the paper: there are an autonomous, divergence-free, Lipschitz velocity field u on the flat torus T^3 = R^3/Z^3 and constants eps0, gamma0 > 0 such that for every magnetic diffusivity 0 < eps <= eps0 the kinematic induction equation dB/dt = curl(u x B) + eps Laplacian(B), div B = 0, has an induction semigroup on the divergence-free fields L^2_sigma whose operator norm is at least exp(gamma0 t) for all t >= 0 (u is a fast dynamo), with an eigenmode exp(2 pi i K x3) b(y) of eigenvalue of real part at least gamma0 and a real solution of exact growth exp(t Re lambda); while every time map of the particle flow of u is continuous and has topological entropy zero, and the ideal (eps = 0) induction equation has exactly one solution group, whose operator norm grows subexponentially. The statement in Challenge.lean uses only mathlib notions and fourteen documented definitions. The repository formalises, in its own terms and with every deviation recorded in DEVIATIONS.md, all statements of the paper except Conjecture 1.1 and Remarks 1.3, 7.5 and 8.4, in about 129,000 lines of Lean in 411 library modules; every audited declaration depends only on the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and there is no sorry outside the deliberate one in Challenge.lean.

records.name: Triangular.triangular_ht_bound
records.entry_name: Formalization of bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform and Carleson's theorem
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of L^3 bounds for the triangular Hilbert form, following a streamlined version of an OpenAI manuscript. records.name: Superposition.infsuper_subsolution
records.entry_name: Superposition in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of Liu, Manfredi and Zhou, "Superposition property in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation" (RIMS Kôkyûroku Bessatsu B99 (2026); arXiv:2508.17106). If u is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞u = f in a domain U ⊆ ℝⁿ and v one of -Δ∞v = g in a domain V ⊆ ℝᵐ, with f and g continuous, then w(x, y) = u(x) + v(y) is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞w = f(x) + g(y) in U × V. For a continuous, degenerate elliptic and sub-additive operator L, the sum of viscosity subsolutions of L(∇u, ∇²u) = f and L(∇v, ∇²v) = g is a subsolution of L(∇w, ∇²w) = f + g. On proper geodesic metric spaces, the disjoint sum of functions satisfying comparison with cones (from above, below, or both) satisfies comparison with cones on the product with the sum metric d_X + d_Y. Mathlib lacks the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem on sums, so its ingredients (sup-convolution, Alexandrov's theorem, Jensen's lemma) are formalized along the way; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: LatinonEntropy.latinonCutDistance_self
records.entry_name: Entropy and large deviations for Latin squares
records.doc: A large deviation principle for uniform labeled Latin squares in the full ordered Latinon cut distance, at speed n squared with extended relative entropy as a good rate function. The space retains both row and column orders. For every finite family of strict order patterns and every finite-rate target, the development gives bilateral local logarithmic counts with binomial finite normalization and second-order constant -2. Neighborhood radii may depend on the target and are chosen before the order threshold. Empty compatible fibers have eventually empty finite neighborhoods. The proof includes a uniform lower counting theorem for bounded positive tristochastic profiles and a transportation correction with exact support, bounded entries and l1 cost at most 5/2 times the total margin defect. The entropy convention is Ent = -KL.

records.name: FubiniStatement.bounded_fubini
records.entry_name: Bounded Fubini in algebraically closed valued fields
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Forey and Yin's Theorem 5.17. For two definable maps to a common mixed VF/RV base, parameter-definable RV lifts of every pair of fibres with equal bounded residue-field evaluations imply equal bounded invariants of the total VF classes. The saturated canonical equicharacteristic-zero model and small generated-ground hypotheses are explicit. The submission selection contains this one theorem; necessary definition helpers may accompany its vocabulary.

records.name: OeisA181076.a183128_integral
records.entry_name: OEIS A183128, A183129 and four siblings: Hanna's binomial-power exponential conjectures, with his non-integrality notes
records.doc: For U ∈ 1 + zℤ[[z]] put B(n,k) = [z^k] U(z)^n. Paul D. Hanna conjectured in 2010 that exp(Σ_{n≥1} [Σ_k B(n,k)^(e(n,k)) x^k] xⁿ/n) has integer coefficients for six choices of U and e: B = C(n+k−1,k) with e = k²+1 (A183128), k²+k (A183129), n (A181076) and n+k−1 (A181078), and B = C(n,k) with e = n+k (A181082) and n+k+1 (A181084). The package proves all six, and Hanna's notes that the exponents k² and k²+k−1 (in A183128, A183129) and k (in A181070, with B = C(n,k)) do not give integer series. The six conjectures follow from a general criterion on e, in the style of Dold's congruences along the rays (n,k) → (pn,pk), proved here for the diagonal series and any U; its corollaries cover constant exponents and polynomial exponents under a divisibility condition. A converse shows the non-integrality for a class of exponents. Integrality of exp(Σ c(n)xⁿ/n) is governed by Dold's congruences, which arise in topology and dynamics (see the survey of Byszewski, Graff and Ward, Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021)). The congruence B(pn,pk) ≡ B(n,k) used here is a Gauss congruence for the coefficients of the rational function 1/(1 − yU(z)) when U is rational, in the sense studied by Beukers, Houben and Straub (Acta Arith. 184 (2018)).

Hanna conjectured in 2010 that exp(Σ_{n≥1} [Σ_k B(n,k)^(e(n,k)) x^k] xⁿ/n) has integer coefficients for six choices of U and e: B = C(n+k−1,k) with e = k²+1 (A183128), k²+k (A183129), n (A181076) and n+k−1 (A181078), and B = C(n,k) with e = n+k (A181082) and n+k+1 (A181084). The package proves all six, and Hanna's notes that the exponents k² and k²+k−1 (in A183128, A183129) and k (in A181070, with B = C(n,k)) do not give integer series. The six conjectures follow from a general criterion on e, in the style of Dold's congruences along the rays (n,k) → (pn,pk), proved here for the diagonal series and any U; its corollaries cover constant exponents and polynomial exponents under a divisibility condition. A converse shows the non-integrality for a class of exponents. Integrality of exp(Σ c(n)xⁿ/n) is governed by Dold's congruences, which arise in topology and dynamics (see the survey of Byszewski, Graff and Ward, Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021)). The congruence B(pn,pk) ≡ B(n,k) used here is a Gauss congruence for the coefficients of the rational function 1/(1 − yU(z)) when U is rational, in the sense studied by Beukers, Houben and Straub (Acta Arith. 184 (2018)).

records.name: PrimeBHT.Statements.t_maintheorem
records.entry_name: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes. The discrete bilinear Hilbert transform along the primes, H_P(f,g)(x) = sum over n != 0 of Lambda(|n|)/n f(x-n) g(x+n), with Lambda the von Mangoldt function, satisfies ||H_P(f,g)||_{l^r} <= C ||f||_{l^p} ||g||_{l^q} for all finitely supported f, g on the integers, whenever p, q > 1, 1/r = 1/p + 1/q, 2/p + 3/q < 3 and 3/p + 2/q < 3 (the Banach range and part of the quasi-Banach range). The proof is assembled from frozen, author-approved intermediate theorems: a restricted-type tri-tile estimate with an epsilon-loss, the smooth truncated bilinear Hilbert transform on the line and on the integers, a vector-valued bilinear form estimate on R x Z/P, the key proposition p:key0, and the U^3 approximation of the von Mangoldt function, which is taken from the author's earlier formalization of A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes (its import closure is included in this repository, see related_formalizations). All results are checked by Lean and depend only on the standard axioms.

records.name: GHHSBridge.toLatinonMeasure_ofLatinonMeasure
records.entry_name: The kernel and measure representations of Latinons agree
records.doc: On the ground space [0,1], the Latinons of Garbe, Hancock, Hladky and Sharifzadeh, described by Markov kernels with a measure-preserving order map, and the Latinons of the Latinon preprint, described by measures on the unit cube with uniform two-dimensional marginals, are the same objects up to null sets. The correspondence preserves the cut distance, the pattern densities and the entropy, including the value minus infinity; the entropy comparison uses the conditional chain rule for relative entropy, also proved here. Consequently Conjecture 12.4 of Garbe et al., stated with their own definitions and with entropy taken as the negative of relative entropy, follows from the counting theorem of the Latinon preprint. Both the finite case and the case of supremum minus infinity are stated.

records.name: DesignsII.TParams.lemma_e_E
records.entry_name: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma e|E (two-sided) and the thinning probability of the nibble
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two probabilistic estimates in the random algebraic template of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900), as explicit finite-N inequalities. (1) DesignsII.TParams.lemma_e_E (Lemma 3.6 e|E with Remark 3.7(i), two-sided): in the template space conditioned on the values of the colours at a set U of fixed vertices, a copy φ meeting U in at most r−1 vertices, whose revealed values are F-linearly independent, passes the tests of colour j with probability between (1−δ)ρ₀(k) and ρ₀(k)/(1−δ), where δ = (q²+q|U|)/N < 1 and ρ₀(k) = N^(r−q) z^(−C(q,r)) ((q−r)!/q!)^C(q,r) |𝒜|^(−1) k/N_act. (2) DesignsII.TParams.thinning_probability (the computation of P(φ ∈ Φ') in the proof of Lemma 3.9 nibble): for families C_i (i < m) of copies of pairwise distinct colours, with covering masses μ_i = ∑_{x∈C_i} P(x passes) ≤ 1, thinning parameters q_i ∈ [0,1] with μ_i q_i = t for all i, and independent thinning coins whose event for the covering pattern w has probability ∏_i (1 − w_i q_i), the probability that the realised covering pattern's coin succeeds is (1−t)^m up to 2^m((∑_i μ_i)² + (m+1)·errMax), where errMax is an explicit maximum, over subsets of the families, of second-order terms (pairs of copies within a family and copies of different families sharing an edge). Both statements are finite-N inequalities valid for all permitted parameters; no asymptotic claim is part of the statements. Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: BornVolume.born_vector_uniform_of_invariant
records.entry_name: Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes. For a ray [z] of C^(M+1), a pure state measured in the standard basis, its Born probability vector is (|<e_0, z>|^2, ..., |<e_M, z>|^2) / |z|^2, a point of the probability simplex (also the moment map of the torus action on CP^M). Let mu be any probability measure on CP^M invariant under every unitary; there is exactly one, the Fubini-Study measure. The identity is proved as two volume identities and a frequency corollary. First (born_vector_uniform_of_invariant): for a pure state chosen with law mu, the Born probability vector is uniformly distributed on the simplex, so the Fubini-Study measure of the states whose Born vector lies in a region R is M! times the Lebesgue measure of R in free coordinates. Second, for a given state (born_weight_eq_measure_cell, born_weight_eq_measure_apexCell): for a unit vector psi, cone the simplex from the Born vector of psi; the states whose Born vector lies in the cell opposite vertex i have mu-measure |<e_i, psi>|^2, the Born weight of outcome i. This holds for every unit psi, including those with vanishing coordinates, and the cells depend on psi. Third (born_frequencies_tendsto_born_weights): invariant sampling reproduces the Born weights as long-run frequencies; for pure states drawn pairwise independently with law mu, almost surely the fraction of draws in the cell opposite vertex i tends to |<e_i, psi>|^2, by the strong law of large numbers. The theorems show that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes; they do not derive the Born rule or say why measurement outcomes follow it. The first form is classical: Archimedes' hat-box theorem for M = 1 and in general the Duistermaat-Heckman pushforward for the torus action on CP^M. The proof does not use the Duistermaat-Heckman theorem; it goes through Gaussians, proves the first form, and derives the second and third from it. The second and third are elementary corollaries of the first; no source stating them in this form was located. No priority or novelty is claimed.

records.name: AMGMSubmission.quadratic_bounds
records.entry_name: When the noncommutative AM-GM inequality holds
records.doc: For arbitrary real positive semidefinite matrices A_i whose sum is at most n I, the uniform average W of ordered products of m distinct matrices satisfies -I <= W <= I when n >= 2 ceil(m/2)^2. When n >= 4m^2 its lower bound improves to -(1-1/(2m)) I. The formalization also proves the stronger lower bound -(1-1/m) I at the quadratic threshold, the original sine-node criterion, and the cubic-size corollary. The statements retain the original arbitrary PSD and sum-at-most-nI hypotheses. Harmonic decomposition, positive root quadratures, matrix Gram factors, normalized coefficient extraction, and the original rounded-node lower-bound proof are constructed in the repository.

records.name: OeisA54767.bell_period
records.entry_name: Bell numbers modulo a prime are periodic with period (p^p−1)/(p−1) (Touchard, Hall)
records.doc: For a prime p, B(n + (p^p − 1)/(p − 1)) ≡ B(n) (mod p) (Touchard 1933, Hall 1934, Williams 1945). The periods conjectured by G. C. Greubel in OEIS A146107, A146109, A146113, A146119 and A146121 (p = 17, 19, 23, 29, 31) are instances; OEIS already marks them correct. Minimality is not claimed.

records.name: Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.erdos_upper
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 626: Erdős's upper bound g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1
records.doc: For k >= 4 and all sufficiently large n, g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1, where g_k(n) is the largest m such that some graph on n vertices with chromatic number k has no cycle of length <= m. This is Erdős's upper bound (Mathematika 1962, Theorem 1) in the form his printed proof gives. Erdős's g_k(n) is the largest girth, one more than the g_k(n) used here, so the formal bound is one weaker than Theorem 1 as printed. With Erdős's lower bound of order log n, it shows that g_k(n) has order log n. Whether g_k(n)/log n converges is the open Erdős Problem 626.

records.name: OeisA173774.conjecture
records.entry_name: OEIS A173774: Sun's integrality conjecture (Andersen 2010)
records.doc: a(n) = (1/n) Σ_{k<n} (21k+8) C(2k,k)^3 is an integer divisible by 4 C(2n,n). Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured this in February 2010. Kasper Andersen confirmed it in a reply on the NMBRTHRY list by identifying a(n)/(4 C(2n,n)) with A112029(n−1). Sun records Andersen's identity in his paper Super congruences and Euler numbers (Sci. China Math. 2011).

records.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.dirac_erdos
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 766: the Dirac–Erdős bound
records.doc: Every graph on n vertices with floor(n^2/4)+1 edges contains, for each 3 <= k <= n, a subgraph on k vertices with floor(k^2/4)+1 edges. For k = 3 this is Mantel's theorem. Dirac (1963) and Erdős (1964) proved it independently. It is the case l = floor(k^2/4)+1 of Erdős Problem 766, on the least number of edges f(n;k,l) that forces a k-vertex subgraph with l edges.

records.name: PalomarNewtonian.scalarMaximum
records.entry_name: Sharp Cartesian Lipschitz bounds for three-dimensional Newtonian point-source fields
records.doc: For the three-dimensional Newtonian inverse-square field, we determine the exact sharp Cartesian Lipschitz coefficient C3. It is the global maximum on [0,1] of f(t)=(2+6t-2t^2)/(1+2t^2)^(5/2), attained at the unique root t* in [9/50,1/5] of 2t^3-8t^2-4t+1=0. For any finite set of point sources with arbitrary centers a_i, masses 0<=m_i<=M, G>=0 and Cartesian clearance d>0 at both observation points P,Q, the exact Newtonian acceleration g satisfies ||g(P)-g(Q)||_infinity <= (n G M C3/d^3)||P-Q||_infinity. The segment from P to Q need not remain outside the excluded cubes. The coefficient is optimal universally across configurations: for the unit source at the origin it is the least constant controlling all safe pairs. Euclidean radii occur in the physical force law; clearance and force differences use the Cartesian supremum norm.

records.name: GJKKL.Main.gjkkl_theorem_3_5
records.entry_name: Counting matchings in near-regular hypergraphs: Glock-Joos-Kim-Kühn-Lichev, Theorem 3.5 without conflicts
records.doc: A lower bound for the number of matchings of a given size in an almost regular uniform hypergraph with small codegrees. For every k >= 2 there is eps_0 > 0 such that for every eps in (0, eps_0) there is d_0 such that, for all d >= d_0, every k-uniform hypergraph H on n <= exp(d^{eps^3}) vertices with (1 - d^{-eps}) d <= delta(H) <= Delta(H) <= d and codegrees at most d^{1-eps} has, for every natural number m <= (1 - d^{-eps^3}) n / k, at least ((1 - d^{-eps^4}) d / e^{k-1})^m matchings with m edges. This is Theorem 3.5 of Glock, Joos, Kim, Kühn and Lichev, Conflict-free hypergraph matchings, in the case of an empty conflict system, stated for every integral size up to the paper's value of m. The proof analyses the random greedy matching process on a finite history tree: the remaining degrees follow the trajectory d(1 - tk/n)^{k-1}, tracked with explicit errors by Freedman's inequality for stopped supermartingales, and the count follows by comparing the probability of each sequence of chosen edges with the number of available edges at each step. The constants eps_0 = 1/(64k^2) and d_0 = max(2, 2^{16/eps}, (19200k^4)^{2/eps}) are explicit.

records.name: SmallNonrational.theoremOne
records.entry_name: Realization fields of four-polytopes and simple-vertex deletion
records.doc: A seventeen-vertex four-polytope has a face lattice realizable over a subfield of the reals exactly when that subfield contains the square root of five. In particular, this polytope has no rational realization. In every dimension, deleting a simple vertex from a full-dimensional nonsimplex yields a polytope of the same dimension whose face lattice is determined by the original marked face lattice. Deletion preserves all real realization fields and the density of rational labelled realizations.

records.name: Papers.Polytopes.conditional_decomposability_sharp
records.entry_name: The sharp vertex bound for conditional decomposability
records.doc: For every dimension d at least 3, the least number of vertices of a conditionally Minkowski decomposable convex d-polytope is 4d-4. The formalization proves the universal lower bound, all-dimensional attainment, the literal least-number formulation, and the stronger statement that below this threshold decomposability is determined by the face lattice. Polytopes are actual finite convex hulls with their extreme vertices, and Minkowski summands may have any affine dimension.

Polytopes are actual finite convex hulls with their extreme vertices, and Minkowski summands may have any affine dimension.

records.name: PalomarColdSpots.lattice_theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Universal cold spots of E8 and related lattices
records.doc: For E6, E8, the dual E7 lattice, the integral Barnes-Wall lattice BW16, and D_n plus in every even dimension n at least eight, the global minima of every positive-parameter Gaussian lattice sum are precisely all deep holes. The result extends to arbitrary nonzero positive mixtures whenever the literal nonnegative energy is finite at all ambient points. The full squared covering-radius table is proved with actual attainment: 4/3, 1, 7/8, 3, and n/8 in the respective normalizations.

records.name: PalomarLongEdges.ToricExchange.grade_zero
records.entry_name: Quadratic generation for smooth polytopes with long edges
records.doc: A smooth full-dimensional lattice polytope of positive dimension n whose edges have lattice length at least n has the integer decomposition property, and over every field its homogeneous toric ideal is generated by equal-sum quadratic binomials. For smooth polytopes with the same normal fan, edge bound n gives prescribed-parity decompositions of interior lattice points of their Minkowski sum. Edge bound n+1 gives the adjoint Minkowski equality. The latter two are the polytope formulations of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3.

records.name: ArithmeticClassification.cell_classification
records.entry_name: Three gauge-coupling windows isolate the roots of x³ − x − 1 and x⁴ − x − 1 in bounded polynomial families
records.doc: Let ρ and Q be the roots greater than one of x³ − x − 1 and x⁴ − x − 1. We classify the ordered triples (a,b,p) in three inequalities motivated by the inverse fine-structure constant, the weak mixing angle and the strong coupling, with p any natural number. For real roots of monic integer polynomials drawn from the same family, the unique passing triple is (ρ,Q,15) when the degree and coefficient height bounds are (4,3) or (6,2). Both families include reducible polynomials of degree at least two with nonzero constant term. The same triple is the unique solution when a and b are roots of an irreducible monic cubic and quartic, respectively, of height at most ten, with the product ab of norm −1 in ℚ(a,b) over ℚ. Two explicit quartics show where this classification fails. One gives a second pair at height eleven with the same norm. The other gives a second pair at height ten with product norm +1. Both pass at p = 15.

records.name: Characterizations.exists_degree_test_size
records.entry_name: Characterizations of polymatroidal ideals
records.doc: A monomial ideal is polymatroidal exactly when every monomial localization has an actual linear free resolution. Universal pure reverse lexicographic colon quotients characterize the minimal generator antichain even without prior equigeneration. Ordinary ideal integral closedness together with local equigeneration gives another characterization. The real convex hull equals the full lower-rank polytope, and the actual ideal integral closure is the ideal of all its integer bases. A genuine finite linear presentation together with the prescribed distance-four exchange condition also characterizes polymatroidality. The selected consequences include genuine quotient-socle recognition, field independence, localization of universal quotients, every monomial term order, exact retained-variable Koszul homological-position tests through the degree/dimension and triangular cutoffs of Theorems4.2/4.9, exact codimension bands and attained minimum testing-set sizes, exact necessary and sufficient variable-order coverage, sharp test-number formulas and bounds, fixed-degree logarithmic asymptotics, and sharp uniform rejection fractions with attained examples and independent repeated-test bounds.

records.name: LeanLab.KumchevLiu2007.Task129W.thm1_written_of_eq33
records.entry_name: Sums of primes and squares of primes in short intervals: Theorem 1 from Proposition 1
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. V. Kumchev and J. Y. Liu, Sums of primes and squares of primes in short intervals, arXiv 0801.0130, display 9 on page 2, derived from the assumed hypothesis Eq33Hyp: the mean square bound of display 33 of the paper's Proposition 1, page 8, for the primes and the sifted function of display 34 with the weights f1 and f2 of page 15, the input the paper obtains on page 15 by verifying the hypotheses of Proposition 1 for these functions. For n in H2, the even n not congruent to 1 mod 3, R2 of n counts the representations n = p1 + p2^2 with p1 prime in the window from X - Y to X and p2 prime between half the square root of Y and the square root of Y, where Y is X to the 7/12 + eps/2. The theorem says that for every A > 0 there is B > 0 such that, for every delta > 0 and eps > 0, R2 of n is the main term r2 of n times the singular series truncated at log X to the B, up to a relative error K times log X to the -1 + delta, for all but at most C H / log X to the A of the n in H2 with X < n <= X + H. It is proved on the range X to the 7/18 + eps <= H <= X to the 1 - eps that the proof on page 16 writes after display 55, and on the printed range X to the 7/18 + eps <= H <= X when eps is at most 5/18. The Lean proves itself the steps from display 33 to Theorem 1: the Chebyshev step from display 33 to display 53, the lower bound for the singular series from displays 48 and 49 with Lemma 3.8, the residual estimate of Proposition 2 on pages 16 and 17, and the circle method assembly of displays 53 to 55. Neither Proposition 1 nor the paper's verification of its hypotheses on page 15 is proved here. Binary Goldbach and the conjecture that every large n in H2 that is not a square is a prime plus the square of a prime remain open and are not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md; the proof reuses code ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, written by its contributors, and is offered for human audit.

records.name: BoundedEdgeRegularSubgraphs.theorem1_1_arbitrary
records.entry_name: Regular induced subgraphs in bounded independent-edge arrays
records.doc: Lean formalization of regular induced subgraph bounds for finite random graphs with independent, possibly unequal edge probabilities bounded away from zero and one. The selected theorems give two logarithmic lower bounds, and exact-order guarantees for arrays with equal expected degrees, Lipschitz kernels, and bounded-rank symmetric completions. The library also develops the degree-vector estimates, the overlap second moment, and a product model with matching square-root bounds.

records.name: Lyasoff2016.time_reversal
records.entry_name: Lyasoff 2016 Asian options and exp-BM integral in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Andrew Lyasoff, "Another look at the integral of exponential Brownian motion and the pricing of Asian options", Finance Stoch. 20 (2016) 1061–1096. Framing: rigorous reconstruction/verification of the paper’s joint-density, Fokker–Planck, foliation, π/π/2 contour, Yor (1.1)/Rem 5.1, and Asian pricing material. The Comparator family is all 40 proof-chart theorems, each proved using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (including time_reversal, Prop 2.2, Dufresne, joint Fokker–Planck, the §4 conditional rearrangements theorem_4_1_pde / theorem_4_1_striking / formula_4_6 / theorem_4_5, the four cond_density_satisfies_* existence results, g_solves_contour_equation, yor_formula, pi_formula, S_closed_form, SfunC.hasDerivAt, hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun, asian_price_formula, asian_delta), together with compared density/integrand definitions. Tables 1–4 are reported numerical data only (definitions, no theorems), outside Comparator. `hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun` uses the tilted-density/Girsanov route rather than global `(u,w)` domination. Project rule: no Lean `axiom` declarations. The §4 rearrangement theorems are conditional implications (they assume the foliation PDE / striking / ODE / Laplace inputs); the cond_density_satisfies_* theorems discharge those inputs by exhibiting a conditional density (Brownian-scaled Yor) that satisfies each of them. Andrew Lyasoff did not participate in or endorse this formalization. Lean was written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson’s direction and review. There is no sorry in the compared Lyasoff2016 development for the Comparator family, and Mathlib plus pinned public Git dependencies supply the analytic/probabilistic stack.

Framing: rigorous reconstruction/verification of the paper’s joint-density, Fokker–Planck, foliation, π/π/2 contour, Yor (1.1)/Rem 5.1, and Asian pricing material. The Comparator family is all 40 proof-chart theorems, each proved using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (including time_reversal, Prop 2.2, Dufresne, joint Fokker–Planck, the §4 conditional rearrangements theorem_4_1_pde / theorem_4_1_striking / formula_4_6 / theorem_4_5, the four cond_density_satisfies_* existence results, g_solves_contour_equation, yor_formula, pi_formula, S_closed_form, SfunC.hasDerivAt, hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun, asian_price_formula, asian_delta), together with compared density/integrand definitions. Tables 1–4 are reported numerical data only (definitions, no theorems), outside Comparator. `hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun` uses the tilted-density/Girsanov route rather than global `(u,w)` domination. Project rule: no Lean `axiom` declarations. The §4 rearrangement theorems are conditional implications (they assume the foliation PDE / striking / ODE / Laplace inputs); the cond_density_satisfies_* theorems discharge those inputs by exhibiting a conditional density (Brownian-scaled Yor) that satisfies each of them. Andrew Lyasoff did not participate in or endorse this formalization. Lean was written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson’s direction and review. There is no sorry in the compared Lyasoff2016 development for the Comparator family, and Mathlib plus pinned public Git dependencies supply the analytic/probabilistic stack.

records.name: Erdos708.erdos_708.variants.four
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 708 for four and five moduli: g(4) = 5 and g(5) = 6
records.doc: Let g(n) be minimal such that, for any n distinct integers at least two and any set I of consecutive integers whose length is the largest of them, some g(n) elements of I have a product that the product of the n integers divides (Erdős Problem 708). The formalization proves g(4) = 5 and g(5) = 6, stated with exact cardinality as in the source: for four (five) such integers every such interval contains five (six) elements with this property, and for some four (five) integers and some interval no smaller number of elements suffices. Because every such set of n integers has largest element at least n + 1, exact cardinality and "at most" cardinality give the same value when g(n) = n + 1. The formalization proves both forms: the source's exact reading, and the at-most reading with the definitions of the open Formal Conjectures pull request #4388 for Erdős Problem 708, copied verbatim. The general question, whether g(n) is at most 2n or (2 + o(1))n, is not addressed.

records.name: QSSEPtoKPZ.main_theorem
records.entry_name: Convergence of the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process to the KPZ equation
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem (Theorem 1.2) of G. Barraquand, "Convergence of the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process to the KPZ equation" (2026). In the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process (QSSEP) on a box of size L in Z (or on Z), a wave function evolves unitarily under hopping amplitudes given by independent complex Brownian motions, and its squared modulus P(t,x) is a random probability distribution on the lattice. The theorem states that, in a window of size n^{1/2} at distance of order n^{3/4} from the origin, the suitably tilted and rescaled measures built from P converge in distribution, in the space C([0,T], M_+(R)) of continuous paths of finite measures with the weak topology, to the solution Z of the multiplicative stochastic heat equation started from a Dirac mass (whose logarithm solves the KPZ equation), for every sequence n_k going to infinity and all system sizes L_k with L_k / n_k^{3/4} going to infinity. The statement quantifies over every realization of the QSSEP and every solution of the stochastic heat equation on arbitrary filtered probability spaces. Since Mathlib has no stochastic integration, the Ito integral (as a limit in probability of Riemann sums), space-time white noise and the Ito-Walsh integral are defined in elementary terms in the statement file. Seven companion theorems show that these definitions are not vacuous and determine the objects: existence and pathwise uniqueness of the wave function, existence of a space-time white noise, well-posedness and Ito's isometry for the Walsh integral, uniqueness and nonnegativity of the solution of the stochastic heat equation. All eight theorems are proved from Mathlib and the standard axioms.

records.name: DesignsII.kahn_plus_equal_weights
records.entry_name: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma kahn+ with equal weights, and the nibble matching for [0,1]-valued tests
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the equal-weight case of Lemma kahn+ of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900), deduced from the theorem of Ehard, Glock and Joos on pseudorandom hypergraph matchings, and of the form in which it is applied in the proof of Lemma 3.9 (nibble). (1) DesignsII.kahn_plus_equal_weights: for 0 < δ < 1 and k ≥ 2 there is Δ₀ such that, for every real Δ ≥ Δ₀, every finite hypergraph H whose edges have at most k vertices, whose degrees are at most Δ and whose codegrees of distinct vertices are at most Δ^(1−δ), with |H| ≤ exp(Δ^((δ/(50k²))²)), and every family of at most exp(Δ^((δ/(50k²))²)) nonnegative test functions p_j on V(H), there is a matching M ⊆ H such that for every j satisfying the spread condition (every edge sum ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v), multiplied by Δ^(1+δ), is at most the total ∑_{e∈H} ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v)), the covered mass ∑_{v∈⋃M} p_j(v) differs from ∑_{e∈H} ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v)/Δ by at most Δ^(−δ/(50k²)) times the latter. (2) DesignsII.nibble_matching_tests: under the same hypotheses, for every η with 0 ≤ η < 1 and test functions with values in [0,1], the matching can be chosen so that for every j whose support (the vertices with p_j(v) ≠ 0) has degrees at least (1−η)Δ, the mass of p_j on the vertices not covered by M is at most max((η + Δ^(−δ/(50k²)))·∑_v p_j(v), k·Δ^δ/(1−η)). Both statements quantify over all Δ ≥ Δ₀ with Δ₀ depending only on δ and k; Δ₀ is not made explicit. Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: PalomarPolymatroidal.minimal_closure_finiteLength
records.entry_name: Prime-power intersections, regularity and sharp local obstructions for polymatroidal ideals
records.doc: Polymatroidality is equivalent to local equigeneration and an intersection presentation by ordinary coordinate-prime powers, with the exact lower-rank factorization of integral closure. For a nonzero equigenerated monomial ideal whose proper monomial localizations are polymatroidal, the actual integral closure is polymatroidal and its quotient by the ideal has finite length. The maximum hole degree determines actual Koszul regularity, and the least actual maximal-ideal power giving a polymatroidal ideal equals regularity minus generating degree. Deleting one Veronese generator has the complete stated fine and total nonlinear Betti strand. Exact pure and mixed isolators realize the smallest possible degrees and the sharp first nonlinear homological positions at every admissible localization, including necessity of the outer-band generation tests.

records.name: PalomarRankThree.theorem11_euclidean
records.entry_name: Rank-three obstructions to coordinate projection volumes
records.doc: For every n at least five, every positive hollow symmetric rank-three matrix lies outside the closure of actual complementary coordinate projection-volume arrays. The entry includes its inertia, strict perturbation and unconditional open-family conclusions. For every 1 <= k < n it also records the exact mixed-volume compactification by finite marked segments and the affine-dimension bound, including replacement of every marked representation.

records.name: RegistryEndpointRestriction.sphere_exact
records.entry_name: Sharp logarithmic endpoint restriction estimates for the sphere and paraboloid
records.doc: We refine OpenAI's local smoothing argument to obtain sharp endpoint restriction estimates for the unit sphere and for a compact patch of the paraboloid. Let E denote the Fourier extension operator, let n ≥ 2 be the ambient dimension, and put p = 2n/(n−1). For R ≥ 2, we prove the Lᵖ norm of Ef on Ωᵣ is at most Cₙ times (log R)^(1/p) times the Lᵖ norm of f, where Ωᵣ is the ball of radius R for the sphere and the cylinder |x| ≤ R, |t| ≤ R for the paraboloid. For the paraboloid, we work at a fixed frequency in one auxiliary variable and recover a logarithm in the Dirichlet energy estimate. For the sphere, we use both branches of the wave representation to bound the Lᵖ integral directly by the nonnegative term in OpenAI's propagation identity. The estimate is sharp, as can be seen by applying stationary phase to surface measure on the sphere and to a smooth localization of surface measure on the paraboloid. The upper and lower bounds are formalized in Lean.

records.name: PalomarMixedVolume.MainResults.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Undecidability of mixed-volume realization
records.doc: Rational membership in the complete forty-four-body cubic coefficient locus is co-recursively enumerable complete even for nonnegative coefficients, with point-padding extensions. For rational automata with at least one alphabet letter, the uniform algorithm produces the complete cubic array and the quadratic section whose realizability is equivalent to the universal cutpoint condition. Corollary 5.1 fixes a rational quadratic family from the probability simplex in R28 to cubic coefficient arrays for 91 bodies. Even when a rational coefficient input is promised to lie in the real image of this fixed family, deciding its mixed-volume realizability is undecidable. This is a promise problem on that family, not unrestricted membership in its image. The explicit three-parameter, twelve-body section in Theorem 6.1 has infinitely many boundary planes and obstructs semialgebraicity.

records.name: LevelEleven.exists_newform
records.entry_name: The newform of weight 2 and level 11
records.doc: The first newform of weight 2 with trivial character, the one attached to the elliptic curves of conductor 11, is constructed and characterised completely, in one statement that uses only Mathlib definitions. f(z) = η(z)²η(11z)² = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²(1 − q¹¹ⁿ)² (LMFDB 11.2.a.a) is a cusp form of weight 2 for Γ₀(11) with integer coefficients a(n), a(1) = 1, a(2) = −2. It spans the cusp forms of weight 2 for Γ₀(11); a modular form of that weight and level agreeing with it up to q² (the Sturm bound) equals it; and its coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations a(m)a(n) = ∑_{d | (m,n), 11 ∤ d} d·a(mn/d²), hence multiplicativity and the prime-power recursions. Method: (1) η² has a multiplier on SL(2,ℤ), exp(2πiψ(γ)/12), with ψ an explicit function of the entries modulo 12, proved from the S and T laws and a finite check; (2) for γ in Γ₀(11) the multipliers of η²(z) and η²(11z) cancel because 11 ≡ −1 (mod 12); (3) vanishing at the cusps follows from f¹² = Δ(z)Δ(11z); (4) a cusp form of weight 2 and level 11 with a₁ = 0 vanishes, because its norm to level one has weight 24 and order at least 3 at ∞; (5) the Hecke operators preserve the one-dimensional space, and the coefficient formula gives the relations; (6) integrality comes from the pentagonal number theorem.

records.name: InvariantSubspaceProblem.Invariant_subspace_problem_l1
records.entry_name: Read's theorem: a bounded operator on l1 with no nontrivial closed invariant subspace
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that there is a bounded operator on l1(N, C) with no closed invariant subspace other than 0 and the whole space. This is Read's 1985 counterexample to the invariant subspace problem on l1, following Wieslaw Sliwa's explicit version of Read's operator (Rocky Mountain J. Math. 40, 2010), which replaces "sufficiently rapidly increasing" sequences by concrete growth conditions and proves every lemma. Its audience is operator theory and the geometry of Banach spaces. It is the statement Invariant_subspace_problem_l1 of Formal Conjectures (InvariantSubspaceProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The operator is multiplication by x in a basis of the polynomials built from a fast-growing integer sequence; the proof shows that the vector 1 can be approximated by p(T)e for every nonzero e, so no nonzero closed invariant subspace can be proper. The open case of a separable Hilbert space is not addressed.

records.name: FibonacciLucasResultant.resultant_closed_form
records.entry_name: The Fibonacci remainder and Lucas norm of the product resultant for xⁿ − x − 1
records.doc: Let Rₙ(t) be the resultant in x of x² − x − 1 and tⁿ − txⁿ⁻¹ − xⁿ. For every n ≥ 3, we compute Rₙ(t) explicitly in ℤ[t], prove that its remainder modulo t² − t − 1 is (−F₂ₙ + (−1)ⁿ⁺¹)t − F₂ₙ₋₁, and identify the algebra norm of its residue in ℤ[φ] as (−1)ⁿ⁺¹L₂ₙ₋₁. The absolute norm is at least 11, with equality exactly when n = 3. This formalizes Stephanie Alexander’s Theorem 2 for the product resultant and derives the sharp minimum.

records.name: LeanLab.ExceptionalSet.U1539.theorem2_of_named_dq5
records.entry_name: Goldbach numbers in sparse sequences: Theorem 2 on exponential sums
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 2 of J. Brüdern and A. Perelli, Goldbach numbers in sparse sequences, Ann. Inst. Fourier 48, 1998, pages 353 to 378, stated on page 354 and proved in section 8 of the paper. The result is conditional on Theorem 1 of A. A. Karacuba 1973, as cited in the paper's Lemma 10 on pages 370 and 371, which is taken as the explicit hypothesis Lemma10DQ5 and never as an axiom. Let F of x be exp of log x to the power gamma, with 1 < gamma < 3/2. Theorem 2 says that for 0 < c < 1 and 0 < C < gamma - 1 there are kappa > 0 and a constant B such that, for every integer N >= 1 and every real alpha with F of 2N to the power -c <= |alpha| <= F of N to the power C, the exponential sum of e of alpha F of n over N <= n <= 2N has absolute value at most B N exp of -kappa times log N to the power 3 - 2 gamma. The Lean proves the steps of section 8 from Lemma 10: the derivative formulas of Lemmas 11 and 12 for the polynomials Q and q, the bounds of Lemmas 13 to 16 on the derivatives of F, the choice of the parameters, and the application of Lemma 10. Karacuba's theorem itself is not proved here. Binary Goldbach and the paper's Theorem 1 on Goldbach numbers near F of n are not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: DiamondPinning.integrable_lawR
records.entry_name: BKT asymptotics for the quenched free energy of hierarchical pinning
records.doc: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the paper "BKT asymptotics for the quenched free energy of hierarchical pinning" (Hexagon preprint 2611.00654v1), except the Gaussian example of its introduction. For B > 2, a disorder W > 0 with E W = 1 and a field h, the partition functions on the diamond hierarchical lattice satisfy R_0 = e^h W and R_{n+1} = (R_n R_n' + B - 1) / B with independent copies; the free energy is F(h) = lim 2^{-n} E log R_n(h) and h_c = sup {h : F(h) = 0}. The main theorem states that if h_c exceeds the annealed critical point h_a = log(B - 1), then with theta = log 2 / log B, a = log B and Pi_n = prod_{j<n} E R_j(h_c)^theta, the residues l_3 = lim E[R_n^theta (log R_n - a)^3] / Pi_n and kappa = lim d/dh E[R_n(h)^theta (log R_n(h) - a)] at h_c, divided by Pi_n, exist and are positive, Pi_n ~ 3 a^3 n^2 / (2 l_3), and sqrt(u) log F(h_c + u) -> -pi log 2 / sqrt(gamma) as u decreases to 0, with gamma = 3 a^2 kappa / (2 l_3): the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless law with explicit constant. All 24 numbered results of the paper are proved, including the basic bounds, critical moments, return to one, the critical product, the field response, the scaling limit and its identification with an explicit profile, continuation before the pole, and the upper and lower free-energy bounds through a hard integer-valued recursion. Three routine identities of Section 1 are used but not exported as standalone declarations.

The main theorem states that if h_c exceeds the annealed critical point h_a = log(B - 1), then with theta = log 2 / log B, a = log B and Pi_n = prod_{j<n} E R_j(h_c)^theta, the residues l_3 = lim E[R_n^theta (log R_n - a)^3] / Pi_n and kappa = lim d/dh E[R_n(h)^theta (log R_n(h) - a)] at h_c, divided by Pi_n, exist and are positive, Pi_n ~ 3 a^3 n^2 / (2 l_3), and sqrt(u) log F(h_c + u) -> -pi log 2 / sqrt(gamma) as u decreases to 0, with gamma = 3 a^2 kappa / (2 l_3): the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless law with explicit constant. All 24 numbered results of the paper are proved, including the basic bounds, critical moments, return to one, the critical product, the field response, the scaling limit and its identification with an explicit profile, continuation before the pole, and the upper and lower free-energy bounds through a hard integer-valued recursion. Three routine identities of Section 1 are used but not exported as standalone declarations.

records.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.v
records.entry_name: An asymptotic equivalent for the harmonic sum in Erdős Problem 878(v)
records.doc: Let f(n) be the sum over prime divisors p of n of the greatest power of p at most n. The weighted sum of f(n)/n over 1 ≤ n < x is asymptotic to an explicit sum over primes p ≤ (log x)^2. Each prime contributes a term depending on the remainder of log x modulo log p. The proof combines a finite harmonic-sum estimate with a uniform short-interval prime bound.

records.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.iv
records.entry_name: An asymptotic formula for the equality count in Erdős Problem 878(iv)
records.doc: The equality count for the functions f and F of Erdős Problem 878 is asymptotic to an explicit sum of logarithmic integrals indexed by the cofactor of the largest prime. Finite polynomial tests determine the sets of integration. The argument controls the discarded integers and sums a quantitative prime number theorem over the resulting intervals.

records.name: MT.powerlossMT
records.entry_name: Power loss for the local Mizohata–Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the following power-type loss in the local  Mizohata–Takeuchi estimate. For each $0<\beta\le 1$, there is an exponent $\alpha_\beta>0$ such that, in every dimension $d\ge 1$, each $C^{2,\beta}$ hypersurface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point satisfies $\mathcal{C}_\Sigma(R)\ge c_\Sigma R^{\alpha_\beta}$ for all $R\ge R_\Sigma$. Here $\mathcal{C}_\Sigma(R)$ is the local Mizohata–Takeuchi constant, and the positive constant $c_\Sigma$ and threshold $R_\Sigma$ may depend on $\Sigma$.

records.name: PlanarFlow.maxflow_mincut
records.entry_name: Flows and shortest paths in plane graphs, with machine programs including the maximum-flow algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of maximum flows and shortest paths. Plane graphs are combinatorial maps (darts with a reversal, a tail vertex, a face and a next dart along the face boundary) whose graph and dual are connected and which satisfy Euler's formula V + F = D/2 + 2. The machine statements are about one explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run) and fixed encodings of the inputs as lists of natural numbers; each asserts one fixed program for all inputs. Six theorems are compared: (1) the max-flow min-cut theorem for a network with nonnegative integer capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks: some flow and some cut have equal value and capacity, so the flow is maximum and the cut minimum; (2) the theorem of Miller and Naor: on a plane map, given an antisymmetric g with net outflow b at every vertex, a b-flow within the capacities u exists if and only if the dual graph with lengths u - g has a feasible potential; (3) a program decides, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map with V vertices, F faces and S darts, natural capacities, supplies and demands, whether a feasible flow exists, within 26 (S + 2)(V + F + 2) steps; (4) a program prints, for each vertex of a digraph with n vertices, m arcs and natural lengths, its distance from a source capped at a given value INF (so INF for unreachable vertices), within (n + m + 1)(36 floor(log2 n) + 143) steps; (5) a program prints the size of a maximum matching of a bipartite graph with n vertices and m arcs within 80 (n + 1)(n + m + 1) steps; (6) there are a program and constants c and k such that, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map (loops allowed) with n darts, K vertices, natural capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks, and every word bound W >= c (7 s)^k, where s is n + K plus the total capacity plus 2, the program prints a maximum flow from the sources to the sinks, as a table of flow values together with a valid index into it for every dart, within c (n + K + 1)(floor(log2 n) + 1)^3 steps; this is the algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: SmythEntry.nonreciprocal_mahler_bound
records.entry_name: Smyth’s Theorem in Lean — The Plastic Number ρ as a Sharp Lower Bound for Mahler Measure
records.doc: In every degree, an integer polynomial with nonzero constant coefficient whose reverse differs from both it and its negative has multiplicative Mahler measure at least the plastic number. The cubic x³ − x − 1 attains the bound. In the compositum of its root and a root of x⁴ − x − 1, the least Mahler measure of an algebraic integer other than 0 and ±1 equals the plastic number. Each element uses its own minimal polynomial over ℤ. We also deduce Siegel’s theorem that the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number.

records.name: DehnCanon.hilbert_third_problem
records.entry_name: The Dehn Canon: Hilbert's Third Problem, Machine-Checked
records.doc: Dehn's answer to Hilbert's third problem, with the Dehn invariant defined from the solid as a set of points in 3-space rather than from a list of edges. For a set P, the invariant dehnSet P in R (x)_Q (R/Q pi) adds, over the angle classes theta, the length (1-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of the points of P whose cone of directions has a line as its lineality space and the angle class theta there, the angle being 2 pi times the area of the cone in the unit disc across that line divided by the area of the disc. Proved: (1) Hilbert's problem in his words: two tetrahedra on one and the same base triangle, with apexes at the same distance 1 from its plane and volume 1/6, that are neither scissors congruent nor equicomplementable (pieces: convex polytopes moved by isometries); (2) for every convex polytope with interior points, dehnSet P equals the classical sum over its edges of length (x) dihedral angle, with edges, facets and dihedral angles also defined from the set (Dehn's invariant in Jessen's tensor form); (3) the bridge: scissors-congruent convex polytopes have the same invariant, in every 3-dimensional real inner product space, and for finite unions of convex polytopes the total over the pieces does not depend on the dissection and is kept by scissors congruence; (4) Dehn's theorem: no similar copy of the regular tetrahedron is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the cube. The theorem is classical (Dehn 1901) and already formalized in Lean in FormalBook's chapter 10, in an abstract model of edges and angles; what is added here is the set-defined invariant, the proved bridge from geometric dissections, its agreement with the edge sum, and Hilbert's statement for tetrahedra as point sets. The entry is meant for researchers in formalized geometry and in scissors congruence: since the invariant and the bridge are stated for sets and for every dissection into convex polytopes, they can serve as a base in Lean for Sydler's converse, Jessen's work in four dimensions and a theory of valuations in Mathlib; none of these is attempted here.

Proved: (1) Hilbert's problem in his words: two tetrahedra on one and the same base triangle, with apexes at the same distance 1 from its plane and volume 1/6, that are neither scissors congruent nor equicomplementable (pieces: convex polytopes moved by isometries); (2) for every convex polytope with interior points, dehnSet P equals the classical sum over its edges of length (x) dihedral angle, with edges, facets and dihedral angles also defined from the set (Dehn's invariant in Jessen's tensor form); (3) the bridge: scissors-congruent convex polytopes have the same invariant, in every 3-dimensional real inner product space, and for finite unions of convex polytopes the total over the pieces does not depend on the dissection and is kept by scissors congruence; (4) Dehn's theorem: no similar copy of the regular tetrahedron is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the cube. The theorem is classical (Dehn 1901) and already formalized in Lean in FormalBook's chapter 10, in an abstract model of edges and angles; what is added here is the set-defined invariant, the proved bridge from geometric dissections, its agreement with the edge sum, and Hilbert's statement for tetrahedra as point sets. The entry is meant for researchers in formalized geometry and in scissors congruence: since the invariant and the bridge are stated for sets and for every dissection into convex polytopes, they can serve as a base in Lean for Sydler's converse, Jessen's work in four dimensions and a theory of valuations in Mathlib; none of these is attempted here.

records.name: Heilbronn.Nine.optimal_value
records.entry_name: Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit square: nine points
records.doc:
The Heilbronn number H_n of the unit square is the largest possible least area of a triangle with vertices at three of n points in the closed unit square. This entry proves H₉ = (9√65 − 55)/320 ≈ 0.0548760, and that it is attained only by the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002), with two points on each side of the square and one inside, up to the eight symmetries of the square and relabelling.

The proof normalizes a maximizing configuration by affine maps into five families, by the corners of the square it occupies, and excludes or classifies each family by geometric case analysis, sharp inequalities in the chamber of eleven tight triangles, strict local optimality, and polynomial certificates checked by Lean's kernel, about 434,000 weighted terms in all. We found no exact proof of H₉ before this one: a branch and bound had bounded it in an interval, and mixed-integer optimization had found it within solver tolerances (a preprint that claimed a proof in March 2026 withdrew the claim). The repository treats each number of points as a separate entry; nine points is the first.

records.doc: Principal path construction and simultaneous sharp bounds; exact 3-tree, clique-book, multipartite and lattice classifications. It also constructs, for every n ≥ 10, K5-free graphs of treewidth four with 3n − 5 edges supporting full-dimensional lattice indecomposable polytopal summands; no proper edge-subgraph supports a full-dimensional indecomposable polytopal weak summand.

It also constructs, for every n ≥ 10, K5-free graphs of treewidth four with 3n − 5 edges supporting full-dimensional lattice indecomposable polytopal summands; no proper edge-subgraph supports a full-dimensional indecomposable polytopal weak summand.

records.name: Sunlet.paper_theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Dimension and identifiability of three-sunlet models
records.doc: Normalized Latin systems of every order m at least five have three-sunlet image dimension 5m-4 in every characteristic, including the original finite abelian-group coordinates. Two transitive derangement families give the stated dimension 3m+2c-2. Complex generic fibers have unique unordered toric decomposition, normalized degree twice the square of the loop abelianization order, and the character-wreath Galois group. The model is rational over Q. Prime nonassociative loops give precisely two normalized general preimages; cyclic models of every order at least six admit rational reconstruction from the literal 8m-12 retained coordinates. Orbit and inverse-stable partition identifications have the complete dimension classification, which yields the full binary level-one network formula including triangles and two leaves.

records.doc: Normalized Latin systems of every order m at least five have three-sunlet image dimension 5m-4 in every characteristic, including the original finite abelian-group coordinates. Two transitive derangement families give the stated dimension 3m+2c-2. Complex generic fibers have unique unordered toric decomposition, normalized degree twice the square of the loop abelianization order, and the character-wreath Galois group. The model is rational over Q. Prime nonassociative loops give precisely two normalized general preimages; cyclic models of every order at least six admit rational reconstruction from the literal 8m-12 retained coordinates. Orbit and inverse-stable partition identifications have the complete dimension classification, which yields the full binary level-one network formula including triangles and two leaves.

records.entry_name: Mosaic spaces generated by continua and by Peano continua
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of an article on Davison's mosaic spaces and three questions recorded by Lavallee (1964). Formalized: every theorem, lemma, proposition and corollary of Sections 2, 4, 6 and 7 and the classical facts they use (abstract Definition 2.1 and its equivalence with the intrinsic definition; the arc theorem; compact locally connected metrizable spaces are locally path connected; Proposition 2.10 on path-determined spaces), the space G (Tychonoff, locally arcwise connected, not a quasi-curve space), the cone construction, boundary bumping (Lemma 5.2), and the answers to all three questions: Q3 by G, Q2 and Q1a/Q1b by the cone over G. Not formalized (examples, excluded by the author's request): Section 3 and the Appendix (the space E(K)), van Douwen's space in Section 5, Example 7.3 (cZ) and the strictness claims of Theorem 7.4 that use them; also the Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem, which no formalized result needs.

Formalized: every theorem, lemma, proposition and corollary of Sections 2, 4, 6 and 7 and the classical facts they use (abstract Definition 2.1 and its equivalence with the intrinsic definition; the arc theorem; compact locally connected metrizable spaces are locally path connected; Proposition 2.10 on path-determined spaces), the space G (Tychonoff, locally arcwise connected, not a quasi-curve space), the cone construction, boundary bumping (Lemma 5.2), and the answers to all three questions: Q3 by G, Q2 and Q1a/Q1b by the cone over G. Not formalized (examples, excluded by the author's request): Section 3 and the Appendix (the space E(K)), van Douwen's space in Section 5, Example 7.3 (cZ) and the strictness claims of Theorem 7.4 that use them; also the Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem, which no formalized result needs.

records.name: GoldenMahlerEntry.odd_mahler_bound
records.entry_name: The Golden Ratio as the Sharp Mahler Bound for Nonreciprocal Polynomials with Odd Coefficients
records.doc: Every integer polynomial with all coefficients odd that differs from both signs of its reverse has multiplicative Mahler measure at least (1 + √5)/2. The polynomial x² − x − 1 meets all these hypotheses and attains the bound.

records.name: four_color_theorem
records.entry_name: The Combinatorial Four Color Theorem in Lean 4
records.doc: A self-contained, zero-Mathlib Lean 4 formalization of the Combinatorial Four Color Theorem: every finite, complete, Euler-planar, bridgeless orientable combinatorial map (involutive hypermap, `e^2 = id`, `e ∘ n ∘ f = id`) admits a proper 4-coloring of its faces (`Solution.four_color_theorem`). Follows the published mathematics of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour, and Thomas (1996/1997) and Gonthier's hypermap framework (2008), verifying all 633 unavoidable configurations (249 D-reducible and 384 C-reducible) and all 5 cartwheel discharging trees directly inside the Lean kernel without `native_decide`.

records.name: WorkerCompromise.allStableWorkerBounds_tendsto_one
records.entry_name: One extra worker rules out the square-root welfare compromise
records.doc: A clearinghouse observes a market with n firms and n+1 workers and can choose any stable assignment. Both sides draw independent rate-one exponential utilities for every firm-worker pair. Changing partners costs log(n)/(6 sqrt(n)). Write δ = 1/400000. As n grows, with probability tending to one, every stable assignment gives the matched workers a mean partner rank greater than n^(1/2+δ) and a mean utility less than (1/2−δ) log(n). Rank one is best. Consequently, even a clearinghouse that chooses separately for each objective cannot deliver mean partner ranks at the square-root benchmark on both sides, or mean utilities at the half-log benchmark on both sides. A working paper on these results is forthcoming.

records.name: GrunbaumK10.cube_everyZoneHas
records.entry_name: Grünbaum's zone question at k = 10
records.doc: A rhombic monohedral polyhedron of spherical type (surface homeomorphic to a sphere, adjacent faces not coplanar) with exactly 30 faces, all of them congruent rhombi whose diagonals are in the golden ratio, in which every zone has exactly 10 faces, and whose translates by a lattice tile space face to face. This gives an example for k = 10 for the question of B. Grunbaum (Math. Intelligencer 32(4), 2010): "Given an even integer k >= 4, is there a rhombic monohedral parallelohedron such that every zone has exactly k faces?", where he wrote that "no information is available for any k >= 10". The witness is DICTO's Grunbaum-Escher Triacontahedron GET B: the rhombic triacontahedron less four oblate golden rhombohedra, a union of 16 golden rhombohedra (its exact model also has 32 vertices and 60 edges; these counts are properties of the witness, checked in the model, not part of the theorem). Two calibration theorems check that the zone definition gives 4 for the cube and 6 for the rhombic dodecahedron. Earlier solids of the same family (the rhombic triacontahedron with four corners indented) were shown on the web as space-fillers, without proof, without zone sizes and without reference to Grunbaum's question: by D. Hall (Sketchfab, 2016; the same solid as G. Inchbald's dimpled rhombic triacontahedron, by 2023) and by J. Kostick (vZome, 2022), whose concavo-convex triacon array shows GET A, a sibling of GET B. So this entry does not claim the first example for k = 10. GET B itself was not found in the sources checked. Since GET B is an indentation of the triacontahedron and is proved here to be a parallelohedron, it is also a counterexample to Grunbaum's tentative remark (same paper) that "none of the other isozonohedra obtainable by indentation of F or T seem to be parallelohedra". The proof checks exact data in Z[phi] by kernel evaluation (zones, congruence, separating normals, contacts, face matching, cone separation from an interior point) and derives the tiling from volume = covolume with Mathlib's fundamental domains. The entry is meant for researchers on parallelohedra and space-filling polyhedra (nonconvex parallelohedra, Venkov-McMullen belt theory) and on golden-rhombohedron polyhedra.

records.name: SiegelTheta.summable_norm
records.entry_name: The theta series of an even unimodular lattice is a Siegel modular form
records.doc: Let L be an even unimodular lattice of rank 2k and n a finite index type. The theta series Θ_L(Z) = ∑_{x ∈ Lⁿ} exp(πi tr(G(x)Z)), G(x) the Gram matrix of the tuple x, converges absolutely when Im Z is positive definite, is holomorphic in the entries of Z, is bounded on each region Im Z ≥ c·1, and satisfies Θ_L((AZ + B)(CZ + D)⁻¹) = det(CZ + D)^k Θ_L(Z) for every (A B; C D) in Sp(2n, ℤ) and every Z in the Siegel upper half-space. So Θ_L is a Siegel modular form of degree n and weight k. The transformation law is proved on three kinds of generator. Translations Z ↦ Z + S and the maps Z ↦ UZUᵀ are reindexings of the sum. The inversion Z ↦ −Z⁻¹ is reduced to the inversion formula for a theta series in one variable: for Z = τ·Y with Y real positive definite, Θ_L(Z) is the one-variable theta series of the lattice Lⁿ twisted by a square root of Y, to which TauCeti's inversion formula (Poisson summation) applies; the identity theorem along the path s ↦ s·Re Z + i·Im Z then gives all of the Siegel upper half-space. Finally Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the inversion, the translations and the image of GL(n, ℤ).

records.entry_name: The theta series of an even unimodular lattice is a Siegel modular form
records.doc: Let L be an even unimodular lattice of rank 2k and n a finite index type. The theta series Θ_L(Z) = ∑_{x ∈ Lⁿ} exp(πi tr(G(x)Z)), G(x) the Gram matrix of the tuple x, converges absolutely when Im Z is positive definite, is holomorphic in the entries of Z, is bounded on each region Im Z ≥ c·1, and satisfies Θ_L((AZ + B)(CZ + D)⁻¹) = det(CZ + D)^k Θ_L(Z) for every (A B; C D) in Sp(2n, ℤ) and every Z in the Siegel upper half-space. So Θ_L is a Siegel modular form of degree n and weight k. The transformation law is proved on three kinds of generator. Translations Z ↦ Z + S and the maps Z ↦ UZUᵀ are reindexings of the sum. The inversion Z ↦ −Z⁻¹ is reduced to the inversion formula for a theta series in one variable: for Z = τ·Y with Y real positive definite, Θ_L(Z) is the one-variable theta series of the lattice Lⁿ twisted by a square root of Y, to which TauCeti's inversion formula (Poisson summation) applies; the identity theorem along the path s ↦ s·Re Z + i·Im Z then gives all of the Siegel upper half-space. Finally Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the inversion, the translations and the image of GL(n, ℤ).

records.name: Kasteleyn.orientation_exists
records.entry_name: Kasteleyn orientations and the Pfaffian method for plane graphs, with a linear-time orientation, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Kasteleyn's method for counting perfect matchings of plane graphs. Graphs are Mathlib simple graphs on a finite vertex type (no loops, no multiple edges); a rotation system is a permutation of the darts that cycles the darts leaving each vertex, its faces are the cycles of the face permutation, and it is plane if the graph is connected and Euler's formula V + F = E + 2 holds. A Kasteleyn orientation with respect to a face f0 is an orientation of the edges in which every face other than f0 has an odd number of clockwise darts. Since faces are cycles of darts, a graph without edges has no faces in this representation; a connected graph without edges is a single vertex, which is not plane in this sense and is treated by a separate theorem. Five theorems are compared: (1) every rotation system of a connected graph with at least one edge has a Kasteleyn orientation with respect to any face f0; (2) for a plane rotation system, a Kasteleyn orientation and edge weights in any commutative ring, the Pfaffian of the signed weighted adjacency matrix (defined by expansion along the first row for a linear order on the vertices) equals, up to a sign +1 or -1, the sum over the perfect matchings of the products of their edge weights; (3) with unit weights the Pfaffian is plus or minus the number of perfect matchings and the determinant of the signed adjacency matrix is its square; (4) one fixed program for an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run) computes a Kasteleyn orientation of every rotation system of a connected graph with at least one edge, with F faces and S darts, given by a standard encoding of 4 + F + 3S words, within 36F + 39S + 27 steps with every natural word at most 4F + 5S + 8; (5) a connected graph without edges has one vertex, no darts and no perfect matching, and the Pfaffian and determinant identities of (2) and (3) hold for it, both sides being 0. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: ErdosKac.erdos_kac
records.entry_name: Erdős–Kac theorem
records.doc: A complete formalisation, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of the Erdős–Kac theorem: the number of distinct prime factors ω(n), centred by log log N and scaled by sqrt(log log N), satisfies a central limit theorem on {1, …, N}. The proof goes through Mertens' second theorem and a truncated sieve whose moments are compared with an independent-prime model. Moment comparison is carried over to characteristic functions by a Taylor truncation of exp(iτs), whose remainder is controlled by a uniform even-moment bound; the model characteristic function converges to the Gaussian, and Lévy's continuity theorem finishes.

records.name: Cutfast.barenblattConst_spec
records.entry_name: Cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
records.doc: Formalization of the paper "On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations" by D. Chafaï, M. Fathi and N. Simonov. For the Fokker–Planck version of the fast diffusion / porous medium equation in ℝᵈ started from a Dirac mass, whose solution is an explicit rescaled Barenblatt profile, the quadratic Wasserstein distance, the Tsallis-type relative entropy and the Fisher information to equilibrium, maximized over initial points in a ball of radius r√d, exhibit a cutoff phenomenon as d → ∞: they jump from +∞ to 0 at the critical time max(1,α)/2 · log d for a fixed self-similarity exponent α ≠ 1/2, and at 1/2 · log d for a fixed exponent m > 1. The formalization also covers the Wasserstein distance between a measure and its image under an affine map with positive semidefinite linear part, the exact Gamma-function formulas for the moments and Lᵐ norms of the full-space and compactly supported Barenblatt profiles and their high-dimensional asymptotics, the normalization of the Barenblatt profile, and the fact that the explicit solution solves the equation.
