records.doc: Formalization of the paper "On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations" by D. Chafaï, M. Fathi and N. Simonov. For the Fokker–Planck version of the fast diffusion / porous medium equation in ℝᵈ started from a Dirac mass, whose solution is an explicit rescaled Barenblatt profile, the quadratic Wasserstein distance, the Tsallis-type relative entropy and the Fisher information to equilibrium, maximized over initial points in a ball of radius r√d, exhibit a cutoff phenomenon as d → ∞: they jump from +∞ to 0 at the critical time max(1,α)/2 · log d for a fixed self-similarity exponent α ≠ 1/2, and at 1/2 · log d for a fixed exponent m > 1. The formalization also covers the Wasserstein distance between a measure and its image under an affine map with positive semidefinite linear part, the exact Gamma-function formulas for the moments and Lᵐ norms of the full-space and compactly supported Barenblatt profiles and their high-dimensional asymptotics, the normalization of the Barenblatt profile, and the fact that the explicit solution solves the equation.

For the Fokker–Planck version of the fast diffusion / porous medium equation in ℝᵈ started from a Dirac mass, whose solution is an explicit rescaled Barenblatt profile, the quadratic Wasserstein distance, the Tsallis-type relative entropy and the Fisher information to equilibrium, maximized over initial points in a ball of radius r√d, exhibit a cutoff phenomenon as d → ∞: they jump from +∞ to 0 at the critical time max(1,α)/2 · log d for a fixed self-similarity exponent α ≠ 1/2, and at 1/2 · log d for a fixed exponent m > 1. The formalization also covers the Wasserstein distance between a measure and its image under an affine map with positive semidefinite linear part, the exact Gamma-function formulas for the moments and Lᵐ norms of the full-space and compactly supported Barenblatt profiles and their high-dimensional asymptotics, the normalization of the Barenblatt profile, and the fact that the explicit solution solves the equation.

records.name: QuarticGate.root_phase
records.entry_name: When a Gate from X⁴−X−1 Entangles Two Qubits
records.doc: An integral unit constructed from the roots of X⁴−X−1 gives a two-qubit diagonal phase gate whose output on the plus product state has concurrence 0.99813134 rounded to eight decimal places. One use entangles a normalized pure product exactly when both qubits have nonzero amplitudes on both basis states. The maximum occurs exactly when both qubits have equal basis probabilities. Among irreducible trace-zero monic integer quartics with two real roots and a complex conjugate pair, require both the generating root and the three squared complementary-pair sums to be algebraic units. For this fixed embedding assignment, phase rule and one use, the joint maximum over all normalized pure product inputs and all eligible polynomial presentations is reached at four polynomials: X⁴±X−1 and X⁴−2X²±X+1. They present the same field by the generators ±Q and ±Q². All other eligible polynomials have squared concurrence at most 307/356, for coefficients of any height.

records.entry_name: When a Gate from X⁴−X−1 Entangles Two Qubits
records.doc: An integral unit constructed from the roots of X⁴−X−1 gives a two-qubit diagonal phase gate whose output on the plus product state has concurrence 0.99813134 rounded to eight decimal places. Among irreducible trace-zero monic integer quartics with two real roots and a complex conjugate pair, require both the generating root and the three squared complementary-pair sums to be algebraic units. records.name: MeyerGeneralProblem.boundedCount_commonSpace_holeClassification
records.entry_name: Finite-comb and finite-hole classification for relatively separated carriers
records.doc: Let Λ be a locally finite subset of the real line with a uniform bound on the number of points in each integer unit cell. The whole complex Meyer space of tempered distributions T with value-only atomic physical and Fourier records on Λ has finite dimension. Its dimension equals the attained maximum of nullities over finite unions L of translated positive-step full lattices for which L ∖ Λ is finite. For each L, the original physical and Fourier coefficients must both vanish at every missing site. In finite lattice residue coordinates, subtracting the joint rank of these rows from the sum of the cyclotomic block nullities gives the envelope nullity. One such envelope realizes the whole space. With separate relatively separated carriers both members of the Fourier pair are finite sums of translated and modulated lattice Dirac combs. The separately stated one-record H6 theorem only bounds the physical carrier. The active spectral module is finitely generated, and a single nonzero exponential polynomial with frequencies in that module annihilates every member of the fixed-carrier space.

records.name: SymplecticGeneration.closure_eq_top
records.entry_name: Generators of the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ)
records.doc: For every finite index type n, the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the matrix J = (0 −1; 1 0), the translations (1 S; 0 1) with S symmetric, and the matrices (U 0; 0 Vᵀ) with UV = VU = 1 (the image of GL(n, ℤ)). The proof does not induct on n. It inducts on a set s of indices: every symplectic matrix that fixes the basis vectors e_j, j ∈ s, of the first half of ℤⁿ ⊕ ℤⁿ lies in the generated subgroup. In the step, the column M e_i = (a, c) is moved to e_i by elements that fix the e_j: first Euclid's algorithm in each coordinate k ∉ s makes c = 0, using (1 tE_kk; 0 1) and its conjugate by J; then a descent on the sum of |a_k| over k ∉ s, by units of M_n(ℤ) of the form 1 + c·e_lᵀ, reduces a to e_i, the last nonzero entry being ±1 because a row of the inverse matrix gives a Bezout relation.

records.name: UnfairTrinomial.trinomial_factor
records.entry_name: The Unfair 0–1 Polynomial Conjecture for Trinomial Factors
records.doc: If a product of two monic real polynomials with nonnegative coefficients is binary and one factor has exactly three nonzero coefficients, both factors are binary. Two independent finitely supported integer laws are each uniform on their support when their sum is uniform on its support and one law has exactly three support points. This formalization uses Fourier series.

records.name: MeyerGeneralProblem.exists_finiteExponentialAnnihilator_of_finite_lower_ray_count
records.entry_name: Annihilation and finite-comb classification from finite lower density on one ray
records.doc: Let T be a tempered distribution on the real line with value-only atomic records for T and its Fourier transform on locally finite carriers. If the point count on either ray of the physical carrier is bounded by C times the radius along arbitrarily large radii, a nonzero finite real-frequency exponential polynomial annihilates T. The opposite carrier only needs to be locally finite for this implication. When the counted carrier is the actual support and the centred count of the opposite carrier has zero quadratic lower density, both records are finite sums of translated and modulated lattice Dirac combs. The latter conclusion also holds with the Fourier record as the counted actual support. The radii witnessing lower density may be sparse.

records.name: StableManifoldChallenge.stable_manifold_forall_nhds
records.entry_name: The stable manifold theorem for a hyperbolic fixed point of a smooth map, with the hyperbolic splitting
records.doc:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the stable manifold theorem for maps, in graph form. Let f be of class C^n, 1 <= n <= infinity, on a neighborhood of a fixed point p of a finite-dimensional real normed space E, with derivative A = Df(p) invertible and hyperbolic (no complex eigenvalue of modulus 1), and let E_s and E_u be the stable and unstable subspaces of A. Then there are a neighborhood N of p and maps h_s : E_s -> E_u and h_u : E_u -> E_s, of class C^n and vanishing with their derivatives at 0, such that for every neighborhood U of p inside N, the local stable set of f in U (the points whose forward orbit stays in U and tends to p) is the graph {p + x + h_s(x)} of h_s over a neighborhood of 0 in E_s, and the local unstable set (the points with a backward orbit in U tending to p) is the graph {p + y + h_u(y)} of h_u over a neighborhood of 0 in E_u. Inside a small neighborhood of p the convergence is automatic: the local stable set in U is the set of points whose forward orbit stays in U, and the local unstable set the set of points with a backward orbit in U. The stable side is also proved without invertibility, with one h_s for every neighborhood inside a small ball around p. Also proved: the hyperbolic splitting E = E_s (+) E_u for a hyperbolic linear map of a finite-dimensional real space, with E_s and E_u the kernels of the factors of the characteristic polynomial with roots inside and outside the unit circle.

The proof is Perron's method on the Banach space of bounded sequences. The splitting comes from a factorization of the characteristic polynomial and Gelfand's formula, and gives an exponential dichotomy. After a cut-off by a bump function, f is a globally small Lipschitz perturbation F of A near p; the bounded forward orbits of F are the fixed points of a contraction built from the Lyapunov-Perron operator, and form the graph of a Lipschitz map over E_s. Smoothness of every order comes at once, without the fiber contraction theorem: the composition operator x -> phi o x is C^n on bounded sequences when phi is, and the inverse function theorem on the space of bounded sequences makes the graph C^n. The unstable side is the stable side of the local inverse of f. No earlier formal proof of the theorem for maps was found; a concurrent Lean 4 development (TauCeti) proves stable and unstable manifolds for equilibria of vector fields.

records.name: AbcTwoNinths.twoNinths
records.entry_name: An upper bound for log c in the abc conjecture with exponent 2/9
records.doc: For every positive real epsilon, there is a positive constant C such that log c is at most C times rad(abc) to the power 2/9 + epsilon whenever a and b are positive coprime integers and a + b = c. The radical is the product of the distinct prime factors. This is an upper bound for log c. The abc conjecture itself remains open.

records.name: PalomarKaprekar.unique_cycle_iff
records.entry_name: Even bases with exactly one four-digit Kaprekar cycle
records.doc: The four-digit Kaprekar map in base B sends an integer 0 <= x < B^4, written with four base-B digits (leading zeros allowed), to the descending arrangement of its digits minus the ascending arrangement. A cycle is a periodic orbit through an input whose digits are not all equal. Cycles are counted up to cyclic shift, including fixed points of least period one. This formalization uses only Lean 4 core and Std and proves that an even base B >= 2 has exactly one cycle if and only if B = 3*2^(2k+1) or B = 5*2^(2k+1) for some k >= 0, or B = 7*2^n with n >= 1 and n not divisible by 3. In these three families the unique cycle has length 6(k+1), 1 and 3, respectively; base ten is 5*2^1, with the fixed point 6174. This is Corollary 2 of R. Galyavin, "Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases" (2026). It proves the pattern that Chen, Ono, Schwartz and Thakur recorded from numerical evidence (J. Integer Seq. 29 (2026), Remark 28). The map is stated directly as digit sorting and subtraction on natural numbers. The underlying Lean development also proves the paper's Theorem 1, the classification of all cycles in every even base m*2^n; that classification is not part of the statement compared here.

records.name: HardyExtension.four_level_frame_maximum
records.entry_name: The Two-Step Hardy Ladder in Higher Dimensions
records.doc: For the ideal two-step Boschi–Hardy ladder with three binary settings per observer and five exact zeros, the fixed-state maximum for four positive Schmidt coefficients is the best of three disjoint pairings. The proof covers arbitrary complex binary effects and gives attaining projective measurements. Equality at the two-qubit plastic-constant value holds exactly when both pairs have smaller-to-larger ratio ρ⁻². A finite mixture of pure components through Schmidt rank four obeys the same ceiling. Every full-rank pure qutrit is strictly below it. A pure state with twelve distinct positive Schmidt weights attains the value through six orthogonal qubit sectors.

records.doc: A Lean formalization of the sharp upper tail bound for sums of independent identically distributed nonnegative random variables, including all maximizing laws and boundary cases, and the exact Erdős matching bound with its equality classification for every fixed uniformity k >= 3 and all sufficiently large matching parameters, uniformly over n >= k(s+1).

records.entry_name: The Dehn–Hadwiger invariant in four dimensions
records.doc: Hadwiger (Math. Ann. 127, 1954) extended Dehn's invariant to convex polytopes in R^n: for the faces of codimension 2, the sum of their (n-2)-dimensional volume tensored with the dihedral angle modulo rational multiples of pi is kept under dissection. This entry defines that invariant from the set alone, in every finite-dimensional real inner product space: at each point the cone of directions that stay in the set, its lineality space, and, where that space has codimension 2, the angle of the cone in the orthogonal plane; the invariant sums (n-2)-dimensional Hausdorff measure tensored with the angle class, in R tensor_Q (R / Q pi). It proves the bridge: scissors-congruent convex polytopes (pieces are convex polytopes moved by isometries) have the same invariant, in every dimension, also for finite unions of convex polytopes. In R^4 it computes the invariant of the six regular polytopes: zero for the tesseract, the 16-cell, the 24-cell and the 120-cell; for the 5-cell it is A5 tensor arccos(1/4) and for the 600-cell A600 tensor (4 pi / 3 - arccos(1/4)), where A is the area of the ridge points, positive in both; arccos(1/4) is not a rational multiple of pi (Niven's theorem in Mathlib). Hence no similar copy of the 5-cell or of the 600-cell is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the tesseract, the 16-cell, the 24-cell or the 120-cell, and, because the 600-cell's dihedral angle is 4 pi / 3 minus the 5-cell's, their invariants have opposite signs and no similar copy of the 5-cell is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the 600-cell. The non-congruence of the regular simplex and the cube is Hadwiger's (1954, section V); the entry claims no new mathematics, only the formalization. The 600-cell needs the face structure: at every ridge point the two tight facets are neighbours across a triangle; this is proved from exact Z[phi] data (its 600 facet normals, 120 corners and, for every facet, its four corners and four neighbours) checked by kernel evaluation, with a barycentric argument on the facet. Not formalized: Jessen's converse in R^4 (equal volume and equal invariant imply scissors congruence), Hadwiger's other invariants in higher dimensions, and the identification of the set invariant with the face sum for every convex polytope (the six polytopes are computed directly). The library reuses the Dehn Canon development (registered PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000003) for convex polytopes, cones, wedge angles, cuts and dissections. Audience: researchers on scissors congruence, valuations on polytopes and regular polytopes, and Mathlib contributors.

records.name: NLA.MF05.Paper.paper_real_bounded_positive_radius_growth
records.entry_name: Numerical Linear Algebra, Explained: Twenty Problem Resolutions
records.doc: Lean formalizations accompanying twenty numerical linear algebra problem resolutions. They give uniform matrix-product growth and local 1/d-Hölder continuity of the joint spectral radius; two real generators with any prescribed nonnegative polynomial growth exponent; and sharp losses 2^r and 4^r for randomly pivoted Cholesky and LU. They show that concave matrix functions can destroy spectral approximation guarantees and amplify nuclear-norm excess without bound, and give sharp Frobenius transfer bounds with and without semidefinite order. Further results are the random-row adversarial deletion limit and sharp universal deletion constant, a pointwise strict tensor-train bound with unchanged worst-case supremum, and curves with rank savings delayed through any prescribed finite range of tensor powers. Counterexamples concern derivative roots of nonnegative characteristic polynomials, a q-permanent subset inequality, a geometric-mean norm inequality, and weighted log-majorisation. The development also proves the rectangular Rowland-Wu Sinkhorn identity, disconnected quotients of minimal positive semidefinite factors, stable nonsynchronised equilibria on random cubic graphs with high probability, and NP-hardness of exact determinant ranges and solution hulls for regular tridiagonal interval matrices. This repository prepares the proofs for Palomar through a single repository-root Challenge/Solution interface selecting all twenty problem resolutions. Seventeen component environments have recorded Lean 4.35.0 compilation and selected-axiom checks; the combined environment has separate current evidence. Official Palomar and independent NanoDa verification remain pending submission.

records.name: PalomarKaprekar.cycles_odd_core
records.entry_name: Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases
records.doc: The four-digit Kaprekar map in base B sends an integer 0 <= x < B^4, written with four base-B digits (leading zeros allowed), to the descending arrangement of its digits minus the ascending arrangement. A cycle is a periodic orbit through an input whose digits are not all equal. Cycles are counted up to cyclic shift, including fixed points of least period one. This formalization uses only Lean 4 core and Std and proves Theorem 1 of R. Galyavin, "Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases" (2026). For B = m*2^n with m odd, n >= 1 and m >= 5, each cycle of the folded map on odd difference pairs lifts to a cycle of the same length. There is one additional cycle of length n+1 if 2^n is 1 modulo m, or one of length 2(n+1) if m = 5 and n is 2 modulo 4. The two conditions are mutually exclusive and the list is exhaustive. For m = 3, odd n gives one cycle of length 3(n+1), and even n gives two cycles of lengths n+1 and 2(n+1). Base two has two fixed points. In base 2^n for odd n >= 3 there are (n-1)/2 cycles of each length n and n+2. For even n >= 2 there are (n-2)/2 cycles of each of those lengths, one of length n/2 and one of length n/2+1. The map is stated directly as digit sorting and subtraction on natural numbers.

records.name: PlanarSeparator.separator_theorem
records.entry_name: The planar separator theorem and nested dissection, with a linear-time separator program on a word RAM, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the planar separator theorem of Lipton and Tarjan and of nested dissection. A plane graph is a Mathlib simple graph on a finite vertex type with a rotation system (a permutation of the darts cycling the darts at each vertex) such that the graph is connected and Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |E| + 2 holds for the set F of faces (so it has at least one edge: faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). Eight theorems are compared: (1) the separator theorem with constant 6: for nonnegative vertex weights of total at most 1, a set of at most 6 sqrt(n) vertices splits the n vertices into two parts with no edge between them, each of weight at most 2/3; (2) the same for every set U of vertices, with at most 6 sqrt(|U|) vertices of U; (3) every plane graph has a separator tree covering all vertices in which every subtree with k vertices has a separator (or leaf set) and a boundary of at most 50000 sqrt(k) vertices each and parts of at most 2k/3 vertices; (4) the same for the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D, with 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1) in place of 50000; (5) for any separator tree with constants alpha and beta, the filled graph of elimination in its nested dissection order has at most alpha (alpha + beta) n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges; (6), (7) for every plane graph, and for the square of every plane graph of maximum degree at most D, there are a separator tree covering all vertices and the permutation listing its nested dissection order such that the filled graph of that order has at most 2 T^2 n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges (T as in (3) and (4)), and, for every matrix over a field whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of the graph, permuted into that order, elimination restricted to the filled graph computes exactly the matrix after the n in-place elimination steps M_ij - M_ik M_kk^(-1) M_kj, with at most 48 T^3 n^(3/2) ring operations counted in a writer monad that charges every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion of the explicit algorithm; the inverse is Lean's totalized field inverse (0^(-1) = 0), so these steps are Gaussian elimination without pivoting when the pivots are nonzero and leave the matrix unchanged at a zero pivot; (8) one fixed program for an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by W along the run) prints, for a plane graph with n vertices, m darts and natural vertex weights, a separator of at most 6 sqrt(n) + 3 vertices whose two parts each weigh at most 2/3 of the total, within 320m + 191n + 403 steps for word bounds at least 16m + 12n + 3 (total weight) + 22. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

A plane graph is a Mathlib simple graph on a finite vertex type with a rotation system (a permutation of the darts cycling the darts at each vertex) such that the graph is connected and Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |E| + 2 holds for the set F of faces (so it has at least one edge: faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). Eight theorems are compared: (1) the separator theorem with constant 6: for nonnegative vertex weights of total at most 1, a set of at most 6 sqrt(n) vertices splits the n vertices into two parts with no edge between them, each of weight at most 2/3; (2) the same for every set U of vertices, with at most 6 sqrt(|U|) vertices of U; (3) every plane graph has a separator tree covering all vertices in which every subtree with k vertices has a separator (or leaf set) and a boundary of at most 50000 sqrt(k) vertices each and parts of at most 2k/3 vertices; (4) the same for the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D, with 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1) in place of 50000; (5) for any separator tree with constants alpha and beta, the filled graph of elimination in its nested dissection order has at most alpha (alpha + beta) n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges; (6), (7) for every plane graph, and for the square of every plane graph of maximum degree at most D, there are a separator tree covering all vertices and the permutation listing its nested dissection order such that the filled graph of that order has at most 2 T^2 n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges (T as in (3) and (4)), and, for every matrix over a field whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of the graph, permuted into that order, elimination restricted to the filled graph computes exactly the matrix after the n in-place elimination steps M_ij - M_ik M_kk^(-1) M_kj, with at most 48 T^3 n^(3/2) ring operations counted in a writer monad that charges every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion of the explicit algorithm; the inverse is Lean's totalized field inverse (0^(-1) = 0), so these steps are Gaussian elimination without pivoting when the pivots are nonzero and leave the matrix unchanged at a zero pivot; (8) one fixed program for an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by W along the run) prints, for a plane graph with n vertices, m darts and natural vertex weights, a separator of at most 6 sqrt(n) + 3 vertices whose two parts each weigh at most 2/3 of the total, within 320m + 191n + 403 steps for word bounds at least 16m + 12n + 3 (total weight) + 22. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: CutCur.main_wasserstein_estimate
records.entry_name: Cutoff via rigidity for curved diffusions
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of Chafaï and Fathi, "On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions" (Comptes Rendus Mathématique 363 (2025) 1103-1121), in the corrected version arXiv:2412.15969v5. The submitted statement surface PalomarChallenge.lean (Comparator configuration comparator-palomar.json) states the theorems and corollaries of the paper (Theorems 1.1, 1.5, 1.7, 1.9, 3.1, 3.6, Corollaries 1.3, 1.4, 1.6): 9 theorems. The repository also contains a larger surface, Challenge.lean with comparator.json (69 theorems: remarks, examples and Section 4 as well). Both are proved with the standard axioms only. Some statements are restricted or amended; every difference with arXiv v5 is listed in fidelity.divergences.

records.name: Gerstenhaber.finrank_adjoin_triple_le
records.entry_name: The Gerstenhaber dimension bound for three commuting matrices over arbitrary fields
records.doc: Three commuting square matrices of size n over any field generate a unital subalgebra of dimension at most n. The proof studies the actions on the kernel and cokernel of a nilpotent generator.

records.name: ElevenFive.eisenstein_congruence_mod_five
records.entry_name: The Eisenstein congruence modulo 5 for the newform of level 11
records.doc: The newform f(z) = η(z)²η(11z)² = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²(1 − q¹¹ⁿ)² = ∑a(n)qⁿ of weight 2 and level 11 (LMFDB 11.2.a.a, the modular form of the elliptic curves of conductor 11) is congruent modulo 5 to the Eisenstein series of its level: a(n) ≡ ∑_{d | n, 11 ∤ d} d (mod 5) for every n ≥ 1, and in particular a(p) ≡ 1 + p (mod 5) for every prime p ≠ 11. It is the weight-2, level-11 analogue of Ramanujan's τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) (mod 691); 5 is the numerator of (11 − 1)/12. Method, as for 691: (1) the lattice L = B ⊕ B with B = (2 1; 1 6), the norm form of x² + xy + 3y² of discriminant −11, is even of rank 4, level dividing 11 and determinant 11², so its theta series θ is a modular form of weight 2 on Γ₀(11) with trivial character (Hecke–Schoeneberg), with integer coefficients r(n) and r(0) = 1; (2) at prime level a weight-2 form minus the Eisenstein multiple with the same constant term at ∞ is a cusp form, so θ = Ẽ + c·f with Ẽ = (E₂(z) − 11E₂(11z))/(−10) = 1 + (12/5)∑σ*(n)qⁿ, because the cusp forms are the multiples of f; (3) comparing coefficients, 5r(n) = 12σ*(n) + (5r(1) − 12)a(n), so 5 divides 12(σ*(n) − a(n)).

records.name: M2Polymath.exact_degree_cheap
records.entry_name: M2Polymath: the exact degree of divisor-sum identities for the prime-counting function modulo prime powers
records.doc: Consider integer combinations f = sum_z c_z (G_z * h_z) of Dirichlet convolutions in which each core G_z is the Dirichlet power zeta^z (z >= 0) or mu^|z| (z < 0) and each correction h_z vanishes on squarefree integers greater than 1. Target D_k asks that f(q) = p^v u_q (mod p^(v+k)) at every prime q with p not dividing u_q, and that f(n) = 0 (mod p^(v+k)) whenever n has at least two distinct prime factors; summing an f that meets a strong form of D_k (one value at every prime power) gives pi(x) modulo p^k. The development proves that, for every prime p and every k >= 1, the least Z for which some combination with degrees in {-Z..Z} meets D_k is S(p^ceil(k/2)), and with degrees in {1..Z} (no inverse factors) it is S(p^k), where S(m) is the least s with m dividing s! (the Kempner function). As corollaries no combination detects primes modulo p, and the divided target needs a degree divisible by p. It also proves D_3(x) = floor(x^(1/3)) + 3H(x), where H(x) counts triples (a, b, c) with abc <= x, a <= b and a < c, and certifies an algorithm for pi(x) mod 3 through D_3.

Target D_k asks that f(q) = p^v u_q (mod p^(v+k)) at every prime q with p not dividing u_q, and that f(n) = 0 (mod p^(v+k)) whenever n has at least two distinct prime factors; summing an f that meets a strong form of D_k (one value at every prime power) gives pi(x) modulo p^k. The development proves that, for every prime p and every k >= 1, the least Z for which some combination with degrees in {-Z..Z} meets D_k is S(p^ceil(k/2)), and with degrees in {1..Z} (no inverse factors) it is S(p^k), where S(m) is the least s with m dividing s! (the Kempner function). As corollaries no combination detects primes modulo p, and the divided target needs a degree divisible by p. It also proves D_3(x) = floor(x^(1/3)) + 3H(x), where H(x) counts triples (a, b, c) with abc <= x, a <= b and a < c, and certifies an algorithm for pi(x) mod 3 through D_3.

records.name: NumberField.multiplicity_classNumber_eq_of_finrank_eq_pow
records.entry_name: Formalization of Iwasawa Theory in Lean
records.doc: A formal proof of Iwasawa's classical class-number growth theorem. For an increasing tower of finite cyclic Galois extensions K_n/K of a number field with degrees p^n, the p-adic multiplicity of the class number of K_n equals mu*p^n + lambda*n + nu for all sufficiently large n, with natural mu and lambda and integer nu. The compared statement uses only Mathlib concepts. Its proof constructs the union as a Z_p-extension and discharges the Hilbert class field inputs using the external Nyll class field theory library. The library also contains the cyclotomic specialization. This formalizes a known theorem and makes no claim of a new mathematical result.

records.name: Frobenius.mobius_levels
records.entry_name: Frobenius: Frobenius congruences for the Möbius function and the exact number of divisor levels
records.doc: For a prime p and k >= 1, the least L for which the Möbius function is congruent modulo p^k to a sum of zeta^z * E_p(g_z) over the levels z <= L, with zeta^z the Dirichlet powers of zeta, E_p the Frobenius pushforward (E_p g)(j^p) = g(j) and integer valued g_z, is S(p^k) - 1, where S(p^k) is the Kempner value, the least N with p^k dividing N!. The same upper bound holds for the Dirichlet inverse of every f with f(1) a unit, over every commutative ring; over Z and Z_p it is exact as soon as there are n primes q with p not dividing f(q) and p^n >= S(p^k), with no multiplicativity assumed. In the power series rings Z[[x_1, ..., x_n]] and Z_p[[x_1, ..., x_n]] with the lift x_i -> x_i^p, and in the Dirichlet ring over Z and Z_p, the exact level count of every unit is given by a depth-flag formula of Legendre type. The development also proves Conjecture 4 of Kauers, Krattenthaler and Müller for every prime p: the least t-degree of a monic A in Z[z][t] with A(z, Phi_p(z)) congruent to 0 modulo p^gamma, where Phi_p(z) is the sum of z^(p^n), is S(p^gamma).

records.name: OptimalControlChallenge.maximum_principle
records.entry_name: The Pontryagin maximum principle, Filippov's theorem and Noether's theorem for optimal control
records.doc:

Sachkov, Control Theory from the Geometric Viewpoint (Encyclopaedia of Mathematical Sciences 87, Springer, 2004), Chapter 12 and Theorem 10.1, and Noether's theorem for optimal control, following H. records.name: OeisA357513.general_supercongruence
records.entry_name: OEIS A357513: u_m(p-1) ≡ 0 (mod p^4) for all primes p ≥ 2m + 6
records.doc: For m ≥ 0 let u_m(n) be the numerator of the sum over k = 1, ..., n of binomial(n,k)^2 binomial(n+k,k)^2 / k^(2m+1). Peter Bala conjectured in OEIS A357513 (2022) that u_m(p-1) ≡ 0 (mod p^4) for all primes p, with finitely many exceptions that depend on m. This project gives a Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of that statement: for every m and every prime p ≥ 2m + 6, p^4 divides u_m(p-1). The proof writes T_k = binomial(p-1,k) binomial(p-1+k,k) as T_k^2 ≡ p^2/k^2 - 2p^3/k^3 (mod p^4), reduces the sum to the harmonic-type sums H(s) = sum of k^(-s) over 1 ≤ k ≤ p-1, shows H(2m+4) ≡ 0 (mod p) with the power sums of the finite field F_p, and shows H(2m+3) ≡ 0 (mod p^2) by pairing k with p - k. The compared theorem is the statement `OeisA357513.general_supercongruence` of the Formal Conjectures repository. The result is not new: Ondrej Kutal proved it in July 2026, with the exact set of exceptional primes and a Lean formalization. The proof here was found independently of Kutal's work and gives only the bound p < 2m + 6 on the exceptional primes.

records.name: EmlRichardson.decE_encE
records.entry_name: EML trees: zero-equivalence and root existence are undecidable, assuming Richardson's theorem
records.doc: The binary operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y), with the constant 1 and a variable x, generates the elementary functions (Odrzywolek, arXiv:2603.21852). We formalize, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, a computable translation of Richardson expressions (built from rationals, pi, ln 2, x, +, *, sin, exp and |.|) into EML trees evaluated over the complex numbers with the principal logarithm. The translation preserves the value at every real x, including 0 and negative values, and no compiled tree ever applies log to 0 at any real input. Consequently, assuming Richardson's theorem as an explicit hypothesis, deciding whether an EML tree is identically zero on the reals, and deciding whether it has a real root, are both not computable. Both results also hold when log 0 is left undefined or is assigned any fixed value, so they do not depend on a convention for log 0. With the same compiler, three further problems are undecidable under the same hypothesis: whether two EML trees agree at every real x, whether a tree takes a negative real value at some real x, and whether a tree is constant on the reals (using continuity of Richardson expressions). The delicate part is controlling the branch cuts of the complex logarithm: signed arithmetic is carried out through positive quantities, pi and sin are obtained through complex values with imaginary parts kept inside (-pi, pi], and the absolute value is computed as a times the sign of a, where the sign is read off the branch cut of log without ever taking log 0.

records.doc: The binary operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y), with the constant 1 and a variable x, generates the elementary functions (Odrzywolek, arXiv:2603.21852). We formalize, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, a computable translation of Richardson expressions (built from rationals, pi, ln 2, x, +, *, sin, exp and |.|) into EML trees evaluated over the complex numbers with the principal logarithm. The translation preserves the value at every real x, including 0 and negative values, and no compiled tree ever applies log to 0 at any real input. Consequently, assuming Richardson's theorem as an explicit hypothesis, deciding whether an EML tree is identically zero on the reals, and deciding whether it has a real root, are both not computable. Both results also hold when log 0 is left undefined or is assigned any fixed value, so they do not depend on a convention for log 0. With the same compiler, three further problems are undecidable under the same hypothesis: whether two EML trees agree at every real x, whether a tree takes a negative real value at some real x, and whether a tree is constant on the reals (using continuity of Richardson expressions). The delicate part is controlling the branch cuts of the complex logarithm: signed arithmetic is carried out through positive quantities, pi and sin are obtained through complex values with imaginary parts kept inside (-pi, pi], and the absolute value is computed as a times the sign of a, where the sign is read off the branch cut of log without ever taking log 0.

records.name: FastGE.strassen_count
records.entry_name: Strassen's algorithm, inversion in O(M(n)) and nested dissection with fast matrix multiplication, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization, in the arithmetic cost model, of fast matrix multiplication and its use in Gaussian elimination. Algorithms are written in a writer monad that charges one unit for every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion performed through its primitives; costs are statements about these explicit algorithms, whose definitions are part of the statements. A matrix multiplication algorithm is a counted procedure together with proofs that it computes the product and performs at most M(n) operations on n x n matrices, M monotone. Six theorems are compared: (1) over every ring, Strassen's algorithm on matrices of size 2^k computes the product with exactly 7^k multiplications and 6(7^k - 4^k) additive operations; (2) 2 < log2(7) < 3, and over every ring Strassen's algorithm padded with zeros to the next power of two is a multiplication algorithm with at most 49 n^(log2 7) operations for n >= 1, whose bound satisfies 4 M(2^k) <= M(2^(k+1)) and 1 <= M(1); (3) over a field, for every multiplication algorithm whose bound satisfies these two conditions, block inversion of diag(A, 1) padded to size 2^ceil(log2 n) returns the inverse and the determinant of an n x n matrix A whose leading principal minors are all nonzero, and performs fewer than 5 M(2^ceil(log2 n)) operations (at most 5 C 2^omega n^omega when n >= 1, omega >= 0 and M(m) <= C m^omega for all m >= 1); (4)-(6) for every field K, every multiplication algorithm over K with M(m) <= C m^omega for m >= 1, omega > 2, satisfying the two conditions above, and every plane graph (respectively the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D) on n vertices, there is a separator tree covering all vertices such that block elimination along it computes the determinant of every matrix over K whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of that graph, provided the elimination meets only invertible blocks (theorem (6): no such hypothesis for positive definite matrices, on squares of plane graphs, over a field with a partial order and a star structure satisfying IsOrderedRing, PosMulReflectLT and StarRing, such as the real numbers), with at most (5 C 2^omega + 2C + 2)(2T + 1)^omega / (1 - (2/3)^(omega/2 - 1)) n^(omega/2) operations, T = 50000, respectively T = 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1). Plane graphs are rotation systems of connected Mathlib simple graphs satisfying Euler's formula, so they have at least one edge (faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: SerrinEpigraph.verticalDerivative_pos
records.entry_name: Serrin epigraph monotonicity and rigidity
records.doc: Lean 4 and Mathlib proofs of three theorems on Serrin's overdetermined problem in epigraphs. Let Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, n ≥ 2, be the epigraph of a continuously differentiable function g on ℝⁿ⁻¹, and let u be positive, twice continuously differentiable in Ω and continuously differentiable up to the boundary, with −Δu = f(u) in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, and outward normal derivative equal to a negative constant on ∂Ω. The reaction f is continuously differentiable on [0, ∞) and satisfies f(s) − s f′(s) ≥ 0 for s > 0. (1) If log(1 + ∫_{Ω∩B_R} u²)/R has liminf zero as R → ∞, then the vertical derivative ∂u/∂xₙ is positive throughout Ω. (2) If moreover f > 0 on (0, 1), f(1) = 0, f′(1) < 0 and u < 1, and n ≤ 8, then g is affine and u depends only on the distance to the hyperplane ∂Ω. (3) Under the assumptions of (2) with n ≥ 9 instead, the same conclusion holds when g has a global linear lower bound or a global linear upper bound. Theorems (2) and (3) are the rigidity theorem of Beuvin and Farina for vertically monotone solutions (arXiv:2502.04812, Theorem 2.1, which builds on work of Wang and Wei), with the monotonicity hypothesis removed by theorem (1), for this class of reactions. Every step is proved in Lean from Mathlib, using only the standard axioms.

records.name: Bruck.bruck_conjecture
records.entry_name: Brück's conjecture
records.doc: Let f be a nonconstant entire function of finite hyper-order outside the positive integers. If f and its derivative share a finite complex value a counting multiplicities, then f' - a = c(f - a) on the complex plane for a nonzero complex constant c.

records.name: PDTGauge.Result.joint_degree_classification
records.entry_name: Rational Recovery on a Common Ruler
records.doc: For the rational plane curve parametrization x ↦ ((x-1)/x^n, (x-1)^2/(x-K)^m) with real K>1 and integers n,m at least two, the index of its coordinate field in R(x) is one except at (n,m,K)=(2,4,2), where it is two. In the exceptional case the involution x ↦ x/(x-1) preserves both coordinates.

Parts (ii) and (iii) are new mathematical results proved in ZFC + GCH (Cardinal.GCH): ω₃ → (ω₂ + ω₁, ω₂ + ω)² and ω₂ → (ω₁^(ω + 2) + 2, ω₁ + 2)², matching Baumgartner, Hajnal, and Todorčević (1993, p. 2) and the 1999 Budapest problem booklet [Va99, 7.87] verbatim, both previously open in the set-theory literature. Part (iv) gives the first formalization of the known relative consistency result (Laver 1982; Foreman-Hajnal 2003) for the ω₁ + ω case posed by Erdős and Hajnal (1974, p. 272): relative to a huge cardinal κ with target θ (IsHugeWithTarget κ θ, Kanamori Theorem 24.8) and ground GCH at and above θ, the first-order theory ZFC + GCH + ω₂ → (ω₁ + ω, ω₁ + ω)² (gchPart4Theory) is syntactically consistent; the stronger simultaneous all-target question ∀ ξ < ω₂, ω₂ → (ξ)²₂ under GCH remains open and is not addressed. For Part (i), erdosproblems.com/1172's cropped-scan binary reconstruction is omitted, and the original un-cropped Baumgartner-Hajnal-Todorčević (1993, p. 2) countable-color question ω₃ → (ω₂ + 2)²_ω under GCH remains open and is not claimed (an unselected remark in Erdos1172/CountableNeighborhoodStep.lean notes that our countable-color neighborhood ideal on ω₃ recovers the known ω₂ + 1 case GCH → ω₃ → (ω₂ + 1)²_ω due to Erdős and Rado, [ErRa56]; [BHT93, Theorem 2.1]).

records.name: R1212.lower_bound_1661
records.entry_name: R(12,12) ≥ 1661: a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12
records.doc: The diagonal Ramsey number R(12,12) is at least 1661: there is a simple graph on 1660 vertices such that neither the graph nor its complement contains a clique on 12 vertices, that is, a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12. The graph is built from the Mathon–Shearer (11,11)-colouring M(797) on 1596 vertices by deleting a set of 21 vertices, which contains two antipodal pairs of M(797), and adding 85 core vertices, each of which copies a deleted vertex or has a single colour towards the remaining 1575 vertices. The proof is a clone-projection argument with an antipodal rule. It uses that M(797) has no monochromatic K_11 (proved in Lean here, following r1212-1642), that antipodal vertices of M(797) have opposite colours towards every other vertex, and finite checks on the 85 core vertices that the Lean kernel evaluates with decide +kernel. The construction and the proof are described in the preprint hexagon:2611.00248. This repository is a port of the formalization in https://github.com/YueMa0/r1212-1661 (Lean 4.32.1) to Lean 4.35.0 and the module system.

records.name: WEdgeNS.necessity
records.entry_name: A necessary and sufficient condition for edge universality of Wigner matrices
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Theorem 1.2 of Lee and Yin, "A necessary and sufficient condition for edge universality of Wigner matrices" (Duke Math. J. 163 (2014), arXiv:1206.2251), for real symmetric Wigner matrices and the largest eigenvalue lambda_N. Let x_12 be an off-diagonal entry. Sufficiency: if s^4 P(|x_12| >= s) -> 0 as s -> infinity (condition (1.4)), then the distribution of N^{2/3}(lambda_N - 2) agrees with that of the GOE up to a shift N^{-delta} and an additive error epsilon_N -> 0 uniform in s (the comparison (4.9)). Necessity: if (1.4) fails, then limsup_N P(lambda_N >= 3) > 0, and N^{2/3}(lambda_N - 2) is not tight and converges in distribution to no probability law. No result of another work is assumed: the local semicircle law, rigidity, the Green function comparison and the edge universality results that the paper cites are proved in the library from Mathlib.

records.name: ExtriangulatedRealization.Challenge.theoremA
records.entry_name: An extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the paper An extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding. Over every field k there is an essentially small k-linear extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding into a triangulated category in any universe, whose countable families of objects lie in extension-closed subcategories with algebraic realizations, and which is hereditary and Krull–Schmidt, has enough injectives and ℵ₁ isomorphism classes of indecomposables with endomorphism ring k, extension spaces of dimension at most one between indecomposables, and morphism spaces of countable dimension (Theorem A). It is the category C(D) attached to an inverse system D of vector spaces with surjective transition maps over an ordinal; C(D) has a triangulated embedding iff every projection lim D → D_i is surjective iff it has an algebraic realization (Theorem B). The library also proves Propositions 2.3, 4.4 and 4.6, Corollary 2.4, Example 4.2, Jech's Aronszajn tree and Bergman's lemma on linearized inverse limits.

records.name: Erdos213.erdos_213.variants.KK08
records.entry_name: The Kreisel-Kurz heptagon: seven points in the plane, no three on a line, no four on a circle, with integer distances
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that there are seven points in the Euclidean plane, no three on a line and no four on a circle, whose 21 pairwise distances are all integers. This is the case n = 7 of Erdős Problem 213, which asks whether such sets exist for every n; for n >= 8 the question is open, and seven is the largest size known. The proof checks the integral heptagon of diameter 22270 found by Kreisel and Kurz (2008), using the exact coordinates they give, each of the form (a, b sqrt 2002) with a, b rational. Writing every point this way reduces the three conditions to integer identities: each squared distance, each triangle's cross product and each four-point circle determinant equals an explicit integer times a power of 2227 (and, for the last two, sqrt 2002), and the kernel checks those integers with decide. The geometric half proves that a collinear triple has zero cross product and that four concyclic points have zero circle determinant. The construction is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed. It is the statement erdos_213.variants.KK08 of Formal Conjectures, which marks it research solved.

records.name: PalomarRamsey.ramsey_three_eighteen_gt_100
records.entry_name: A Lean proof of the Ramsey lower bound R(3,18) >= 101
records.doc: There exists a simple graph on Fin 100 with no triangle and no independent set of size 18. This is the witness formulation of R(3,18) > 100. The proof checks the adjacency data of the 100-vertex graph published in Zenodo record 24285935. In the complement, a greedy coloring bounds the clique size at each search node and the branches cover all candidates that exceed the color bound. Lean checks the resulting subproblems and their composition using only Lean core and Std.

records.name: Erdos112.k73_ge_39
records.entry_name: Lower bounds for four small Erdős-Rado numbers: k(7,3) ≥ 39, k(8,3) ≥ 47, k(6,4) ≥ 78, k(3,6) ≥ 71 (Erdős Problem #112)
records.doc: Lean 4 proofs of four lower bounds for Erdős-Rado numbers: k(7,3) ≥ 39, k(8,3) ≥ 47, k(6,4) ≥ 78 and k(3,6) ≥ 71. Here k(n,m) is the least k such that every oriented graph on k vertices has n vertices with no arc between any two of them, or a transitive tournament on m vertices (Erdős Problem #112). Each bound is one explicit oriented graph that avoids both structures: bicirculants on 38 and 46 vertices for k(7,3) and k(8,3), and circulants on 77 and 70 vertices for k(6,4) and k(3,6). Every property of each graph is checked by computations inside Lean's kernel (decide +kernel), with no native_decide, and the proofs use only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. The previous best public lower bounds were k(7,3) ≥ 37, k(8,3) ≥ 46, k(6,4) ≥ 65 and k(3,6) ≥ 68, from circulants in an unrefereed, AI-generated GitHub repository (rsvaultpudgy-create/erdos-112-lower-bounds, 11 November 2026). The four new graphs were first made public in the author's Zenodo record of 20 November 2026 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24390891), which this project formalizes; to the author's knowledge no other proof of these bounds exists, so these are the first Lean proofs of them. Earlier computational work on the problem includes D. Kirtchakov's certified value k(3,4) = 21 and bound k(6,3) ≥ 29 (Zenodo, August 2026). The known upper bounds k(7,3) ≤ 45 and k(8,3) ≤ 59 (Ihringer, Rajendraprasad and Weinert, 2021) are not improved. The results are lower bounds only: none of the four values is determined, and Erdős Problem #112 remains open.

records.name: CEIPalomar.essential_incomplete_iff_inseparable
records.entry_name: Logical consequence and essential incompleteness in recursion categories
records.doc:
We realize Di Paola and Heller’s objective to give an algebraic account of generalized incompleteness theorems in recursion categories. From two disjoint domains of partial morphisms on the same object in a recursion category we construct a first-order theory internal to that category. Its nonlogical axioms assert the nullary predicates indexed by the first domain and the negations of those indexed by the second. If the generated theory is consistent, the two domains are inseparable if and only if every consistent closed internal extension of the theory in the same language is incomplete.
On pairs generating consistent theories, this construction is left adjoint to the functor that takes a consistent theory to its theorem and refutation subobjects. A second construction associates to a consistent theory the Turing category of partial maps in the slice over its theorem object. records.name: LPPMonotonicity.speed_monotone_of_interval_certificates
records.entry_name: The speed of biased random walk on leafless Bienaymé trees is monotone
records.doc: Conditional on the two interval verifications of Appendix A, this Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization proves Theorem 1.1 of the paper. For every offspring law with no mass at zero and mean 1 < m < ∞, the speed v of the λ-biased random walk on the Bienaymé tree, constructed as the almost-sure limit of |X_n|/n, is positive and C^1 on [0, m) and strictly decreasing there, with v'(λ) < 0 for 0 < λ < m and right derivative -2 E[1/ν] at 0. The hypotheses are the closed propositions CertACovers and CertBCovers that the interval verifications of Lemmas A.1 and A.2 check, over all feasible normalized data; the proof derives the two lemmas from them at the actual law. The two propositions are proved in a companion repository, not in this one.

records.name: CopWin.copNumber_eq_one_iff_dismantlable
records.entry_name: Cop-win graphs are exactly the dismantlable graphs (Nowakowski-Winkler), and trees have cop number 1
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of the Nowakowski-Winkler theorem in the game of cops and robbers: a finite graph has cop number 1 if and only if it is dismantlable. A vertex u is a corner if some other vertex w has N[u] contained in N[w] (closed neighbourhoods), and a graph is dismantlable if corners can be deleted one at a time until one vertex is left. The proof defines a one-cop game played inside a vertex set, with a bridge lemma showing that on the whole vertex set it is exactly Formal Conjectures' game CopsCatchWithin with one cop. A general shadow-map lemma says that if f maps S into T, sends legal moves to legal moves, and a cop on f x can reach every vertex the robber can step to from x, then a cop that wins on T also wins on S, by chasing the robber's shadow f r. Folding a corner onto the vertex that covers it is such a map, so induction on dismantlability gives one direction. For the converse, following the robber's longest escape gives a corner just before capture: the robber's vertex, covered by the cop's. Folding that corner away is a retract, and a cop that wins on a set also wins on any retract of it by standing on the image of its position, so induction on the number of vertices shows every cop-win finite graph is dismantlable. As a corollary, every finite nonempty tree is dismantlable (each leaf is a corner covered by its neighbour) and so has cop number 1. This is the statement meyniel_conjecture.variants.tree of Formal Conjectures, which marks it research solved. The mathematics is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed; to our knowledge this is the first published Lean 4 formalisation.

records.name: GapExtremal.R434.nearly_quadratic_gap_with_linear_connectivity
records.entry_name: Nearly Quadratic Additive Gaps for Edge-Clique Partitions of Split Graphs
records.doc: For all sufficiently large n there is an n-vertex split graph that stays connected after removing any set of fewer than ceiling(n/5) vertices. Its exact edge-clique partition number exceeds the fractional optimum by at least a positive constant times n^2 (log n)^(-5/2) times exp(-2 sqrt(log(24/7) log n)). The same lower bound holds with the fractional optimum restricted to cliques of order at most four. The construction combines a local triangle-packing obstruction, a signed weight estimate on affine blocks, and host assignments in a split graph.

records.name: OeisA189286.conjecture_1
records.entry_name: Formal Proof of OEIS A189286 Integrality and 2-adic Divisibility Conjectures
records.doc: Complete Lean 4 formal proofs of two conjectures by Zhi-Wei Sun (2011) on OEIS A189286, defined by a(n) = (sum_{k=0}^n C(6k,3k) C(3k,k) C(6(n-k),3(n-k)) C(3(n-k),n-k)) / ((2n-1) C(3n,n)). This combined submission proves two distinct results: (1) an independent, self-contained elementary proof of the previously proved integrality conjecture (conjecture_1; earlier proved in T. Adamczewski, arXiv:2608.11941), via termwise p-adic divisibility using Legendre's formula and a 3-adic lifting argument; and (2) an original proof of Conjecture (ii) (conjecture_3: for every n >= 1, 8 divides a(n) and a(n)/8 is odd iff n is a power of two), via Kummer's theorem, binary submask counting, and a fixed-point-free involution mod 4. As of November 2026, conjecture_3 was listed without proof on OEIS A189286 and marked research open in FormalConjectures/OEIS/189286.lean, though no exhaustive literature search is claimed to rule out other proofs.

records.name: Rng3d.output_iff
records.entry_name: Expected linear time for the relative neighborhood graph of uniform points in the unit cube
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof about an algorithm (SPoIF, Secure Posts on Increasing Fence) that computes the relative neighborhood graph of N points of the unit cube in three dimensions. The points are binned into a grid of about N cells. For each point p, a cube of grid cells around p (the fence) grows until the points collected inside it cut every patch of its surface off from p: a patch is cut off by a collected point q when it lies beyond the plane through q with normal q - p, so that q lies in the lune of p and any point beyond the patch. The neighbours of p are then found among the collected points by the direct lune test. Two theorems are proved. Correctness: for any points of the cube, the neighbours reported at each point are exactly its neighbours in the relative neighborhood graph. Expected linear time: for N independent uniform points of the cube, the expected operation count of the whole algorithm is at most C N for a constant C.

records.name: CheeseCutM.maxCutCount_eq_F_ge_700
records.entry_name: Maximum Unit Cubes Cut by a Plane in [0, n]^3 (Cheese-Cutting Theorem M)
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization over R of the exact maximum number m(n) of open unit cubes of the n x n x n cube [0, n]^3 met by a single plane, proving m(n) = floor((9n^2 + 4n - 17)/4) for all 3 <= n <= 32 (in particular m(10) = 230, settling the open case stated by Barany and Frankl, 2021) and for all n >= 700, refuting Barany and Frankl's Section 5 "+2" remark for all n >= 700, and proving the universal upper bound m(n) <= floor((9n^2 + 6n - 20)/4) for every n >= 2. The finite intermediate window 33 <= n <= 699 is not discharged inside Lean and is certified separately by exact-integer programs documented in the accompanying paper.

records.name: GaussianQuartics.theorem1i
records.entry_name: The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers
records.doc: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of the results of F. Najman, "The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers" (Amer. Math. Monthly 117 (2010)). In the Gaussian integers ℤ[i], the equation x⁴ − y⁴ = iz² has only trivial solutions (xyz = 0); the nontrivial solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ = iz² with gcd(x, y, z) = 1 are exactly those with x, y ∈ {±1, ±i} and z = ±i(1 + i), and all its nontrivial solutions are given by x ∈ {±y, ±iy}, z = ±i(1 + i)y²; and the equations x⁴ ± y⁴ = z² have only trivial solutions (a theorem of Hilbert, reproved in the paper). As the paper remarks, the same holds over ℚ(i). The proofs go through the elliptic curves y² = x³ + x and y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), whose groups of ℚ(i)-points, the point at infinity included, are formalized as ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 and ℤ/2 × ℤ/4. Where the paper computes the ranks with a computer program, the formalization determines the ℚ(i)-points directly: the line through a point and its complex conjugate reduces them to rational points, which Fermat's descent determines. 9 theorems and 2 definitions, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

In the Gaussian integers ℤ[i], the equation x⁴ − y⁴ = iz² has only trivial solutions (xyz = 0); the nontrivial solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ = iz² with gcd(x, y, z) = 1 are exactly those with x, y ∈ {±1, ±i} and z = ±i(1 + i), and all its nontrivial solutions are given by x ∈ {±y, ±iy}, z = ±i(1 + i)y²; and the equations x⁴ ± y⁴ = z² have only trivial solutions (a theorem of Hilbert, reproved in the paper). As the paper remarks, the same holds over ℚ(i). The proofs go through the elliptic curves y² = x³ + x and y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), whose groups of ℚ(i)-points, the point at infinity included, are formalized as ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 and ℤ/2 × ℤ/4. Where the paper computes the ranks with a computer program, the formalization determines the ℚ(i)-points directly: the line through a point and its complex conjugate reduces them to rational points, which Fermat's descent determines. 9 theorems and 2 definitions, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: DavenportProject.exists_length_forcing_zeroSet
records.entry_name: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper of C. G. Pop, G. C. Rad and G. C. Țurcaș on the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups of rank three. An incidence identity of degree t of a sequence is a family of coefficients indexed by its zero-sum subsequences whose sum is one and whose moments of degree 1 to t vanish. Theorem A (a transfer principle): if every sequence of L(t) terms over a finite abelian group Q has such an identity over F_p, or over the integers, then D(Q ⊕ H) ≤ L(D(H) − 1) for every finite abelian p-group H. Theorem B: for m = 2, 3, 4, every sequence of m(t + 3) − 2 terms over C_m^3 has an integral identity of degree t, and the invariant κ_t(C_m^3; K) equals m(t + 3) − 2 for every field K of characteristic zero or prime to m. Corollary C: D(C_{mp^a} ⊕ C_{mp^b} ⊕ C_{mp^c}) = m(p^a + p^b + p^c) − 2 for m = 2, 3, 4, every prime p not dividing m and 0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ c; in particular D(C_15^3) = 43 and D(C_20^3) = 58. All lemmas, propositions, theorems and corollaries of the paper are formalized. The computer-assisted Lemmas 5.1(1) and 5.3 are checked by Lean's kernel, and every result depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: TuzaChallenge.tuza_bound_81_29_nat
records.entry_name: Universal 81/29 Bound for Tuza's Triangle-Cover Conjecture
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving 29 * tau(G) <= 81 * nu(G) (tau(G) <= (81 / 29) * nu(G) ~= 2.793103 * nu(G)) for every finite simple graph G, where nu(G) is the triangle packing number and tau(G) is the triangle transversal number, strictly improving Sichen Wang's 165/59 bound (arXiv:2609.13831). Main theorem: 1 of 1 in Lean (100%); companion 32-vertex gadget checked separately in exact rational Python. Extends Wang's MIT-licensed sichen-wang/tuza-lean library with helper-arborescence coupling, unmerged colored-family covers, and opposite-edge elimination, together with non-vacuity checks nu(K_4) = 1 and tau(K_4) = 2.

records.name: Matematyka.Erdos132.fc_hopf_pannwitz
records.entry_name: Partial Results and Regular-Polygon Moment Obstruction for Erdős Problem #132 (Rare Planar Distances)
records.doc: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of partial results toward Erdős Problem #132 (rare planar distances: whether every n >= 5 points in ℝ² determine at least two distances occurring between 1 and n times). Using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (no sorry, no native_decide), the repository proves unconditionally: (1) the Hopf–Pannwitz diameter theorem (fc_hopf_pannwitz); (2) sharpness at n = 4 via the unit rhombus (fc_four_points); (3) g(2) = 5, i.e., no 6-point planar 2-distance set exists (no_six_point_two_dist); (4) Erdős #132 for n = 5 and n = 6 via kernel-verified 3x3 Gram-minor integer Positivstellensatz certificates across all 1,024 K_5 edge 2-colorings and all 30 symmetric (1,7,7) 6-point extensions (fc_erdos_fishburn); and (5) a general m >= 4 regular-polygon 2nd/4th-moment obstruction theorem (no_regPoly_violator_extension, reducing impossibility to 3m > 9). Combining even-size endpoint descent with this unconditional moment obstruction yields fc_fourteen_of_wei_and_class13, which establishes a conditional reduction for n = 14 depending on two explicit hypotheses not proved here: Wei's bound g(6) = 13 (hwei) and the unproved 13-point <= 6-distance classification restricted to multiplicities <= 15 (hclass13). Both an unconditional resolution of n = 14 and the full conjecture for arbitrary n >= 5 (with the asymptotic growth question) remain open.

records.entry_name: Partial Results and Regular-Polygon Moment Obstruction for Erdős Problem #132 (Rare Planar Distances)
records.doc: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of partial results toward Erdős Problem #132 (rare planar distances: whether every n >= 5 points in ℝ² determine at least two distances occurring between 1 and n times). Using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (no sorry, no native_decide), the repository proves unconditionally: (1) the Hopf–Pannwitz diameter theorem (fc_hopf_pannwitz); (2) sharpness at n = 4 via the unit rhombus (fc_four_points); (3) g(2) = 5, i.e., no 6-point planar 2-distance set exists (no_six_point_two_dist); (4) Erdős #132 for n = 5 and n = 6 via kernel-verified 3x3 Gram-minor integer Positivstellensatz certificates across all 1,024 K_5 edge 2-colorings and all 30 symmetric (1,7,7) 6-point extensions (fc_erdos_fishburn); and (5) a general m >= 4 regular-polygon 2nd/4th-moment obstruction theorem (no_regPoly_violator_extension, reducing impossibility to 3m > 9). Combining even-size endpoint descent with this unconditional moment obstruction yields fc_fourteen_of_wei_and_class13, which establishes a conditional reduction for n = 14 depending on two explicit hypotheses not proved here: Wei's bound g(6) = 13 (hwei) and the unproved 13-point <= 6-distance classification restricted to multiplicities <= 15 (hclass13). Both an unconditional resolution of n = 14 and the full conjecture for arbitrary n >= 5 (with the asymptotic growth question) remain open.

records.name: SixExponentials.six_exponentials_theorem
records.entry_name: The six exponentials theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of the six exponentials theorem of Lang and Ramachandra: if x₁, x₂ are complex numbers linearly independent over ℚ and y₁, y₂, y₃ are complex numbers linearly independent over ℚ, then at least one of the six numbers exp(xᵢyⱼ) is transcendental. The proof is Schneider's method in the form of Lang and Ramachandra, relativised to a number field K: Siegel's lemma gives an exponential polynomial with integer coefficients, not all zero, that vanishes on a box of lattice points ∑ mⱼyⱼ; a Cauchy estimate with zeros, played against Liouville's inequality in K, extends the vanishing from each box to the next; and an exponential polynomial vanishing on the whole lattice has zero coefficients, by Dedekind's independence of characters. The library proves the number-field form for d numbers x and l numbers y with d + l < dl, and the theorem is its case d = 2, l = 3. This repository is a self-contained extract of the theorem from the library github.com/carlok/diaz-modulus-lean, which is the canonical home of the proof.

records.name: ThreeFactorials.solution_iff_squarefree
records.entry_name: Products of three factorials (partial)
records.doc: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of parts of A. Dujella, F. Najman, N. Saradha, T. N. Shorey, "Products of three factorials" (Publ. Math. Debrecen 85 (2014)), on the equation a₁!(a₁ − 3)!a₃! = y². Proved unconditionally: Theorem 1.1 for a₃ = 26 (the only solutions are a₁ = 324 and a₁ = 2738), by reducing to squarefree Pell systems, excluding all but two of them with congruences, fundamental units and an elementary argument for the quartic case, and solving the last two with simultaneous Padé approximations; that the seven pairs listed in Theorem 1.1 are solutions; Theorem 1.2(a); Theorem 1.2(b) in two forms with changed hypotheses, because the proof of the printed part (b) has a gap; and Theorem 1.2(c) for a₃ ≥ 101. The completeness of Theorem 1.1 for a₃ ≤ 100 is not proved; it appears only as an explicit premise, as do the completeness of a Magma computation of integral points and a consequence of a theorem of Bennett, in alternative derivations. 21 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: InducedDegreeRepetition.logScale_repetition
records.entry_name: A subexponential bound for induced degree repetition
records.doc: Every sufficiently large N-vertex graph contains an induced subgraph of order between r and 2r−1 with a degree class of proportion at least 1−η, where r is the ceiling of K log N, for every K>0 and 0<η<1. Consequently log g(k)=o(k) for the least Caro–Yuster repetition threshold.

records.name: Couret.PalomarCayley.abelian_isomorphism_iff
records.entry_name: Directed Cayley non-isomorphism and abelian generation dichotomy
records.doc: For exceptional three-increment directed Cayley graphs in an abelian group, under the displayed torsion, nondegeneracy and generation assumptions, the reflected pair is isomorphic exactly when the singleton and half-turn increments do not generate the ambient group. A separate theorem proves non-isomorphism for two explicit three-increment digraphs on Z/(12r)Z for every positive natural r, with no affine restriction on vertex equivalences. These are adaptations of prior public Couret formalizations; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.name: MuchaSankowski.elimination_matching_machine
records.entry_name: Perfect and maximum matchings by Mucha-Sankowski elimination on a word RAM, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of randomized perfect-matching and maximum-matching algorithms through the Tutte matrix, on an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, including natural division and remainder; natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run). The machine also has exact real registers; both statements require the program to be a word program, containing no real instruction, so that every run uses only the bounded natural words. Two theorems are compared. (1) There is one fixed word program such that, for every simple graph G on the vertices 0, ..., n - 1 whose m edges (u, v), u < v, are listed once, every prime p and every W with W >= p^2 + p and W >= 3 n^2 + n + 3 m + 6, the program run on the input words (n, p, m, then u, v and the value x{u, v} in 0, ..., p - 1 for each listed edge) halts, for every substitution x of the indeterminates of the Tutte matrix by elements of ZMod p (a function on the unordered pairs of vertices), within 62 n^3 + 116 n^2 + 91 n + 24 n (floor(log2 p) + 1) + 27 m + 31 steps; and if G has a perfect matching, the fraction of the substitutions x for which the printed words are not the pairs of a perfect matching of G (every pair an edge, every vertex exactly once) is at most n / p. The program builds the substituted Tutte matrix, inverts it by Gauss-Jordan elimination modulo p and runs the elimination of Mucha and Sankowski with rank-two updates of the inverse. (2) There is one fixed word program such that, for every such G, p and W with W >= p^2 + p and W >= 15 n^2 + 2 n + 3 m + 6, the program run on the input words (n, p, m; for each listed edge u, v and the value z{u, v} in 0, ..., p - 1; then for all i, j < n the words i, n + j and the value z{i, n + j}) halts, for every assignment z in ZMod p to the unordered pairs of the 2n vertices of G padded with n vertices adjacent to every vertex of G, within 522 n^3 + 579 n^2 + 248 n + 60 n (floor(log2 p) + 1) + 54 m + 58 steps; and the fraction of the assignments z for which the printed words are not the pairs of a maximum matching of G (a matching with at least as many pairs as any matching of G) is at most 2n / p. This program computes the rank r of the substituted Tutte matrix of G modulo p (twice the matching number with high probability, by Lovasz's theorem), pads G with n - r vertices adjacent to every vertex, runs the elimination algorithm on the padded graph and prints the matched pairs of original vertices. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: DoubleMidset.Paper.lemma_2_2_a
records.entry_name: The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua" (Lucas Alves de Almeida, 22 November 2026), which proves the Loveland-Wayment conjecture: a nondegenerate compact connected metric space in which every pair of distinct points has exactly two equidistant points is homeomorphic to the circle (Theorem A). Formalized: every definition, lemma, fact (in the form used), proposition, corollary and theorem of Sections 2-12, including Theorems A, B and C, the converse (the Euclidean circle has the DMP), the characterization of the metrizable continua admitting a DMP metric, and the facts that arcs and simple triods are finite trees. Not formalized: figures, remarks and the open questions of Section 13, and R. L. Moore's general theorem behind Fact 2.5 (only its consequence "a dendrite without branch points is an arc" is proved, which is all the paper uses).

Formalized: every definition, lemma, fact (in the form used), proposition, corollary and theorem of Sections 2-12, including Theorems A, B and C, the converse (the Euclidean circle has the DMP), the characterization of the metrizable continua admitting a DMP metric, and the facts that arcs and simple triods are finite trees. Not formalized: figures, remarks and the open questions of Section 13, and R. L. Moore's general theorem behind Fact 2.5 (only its consequence "a dendrite without branch points is an arc" is proved, which is all the paper uses).

records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua" (Lucas Alves de Almeida, 22 November 2026), which proves the Loveland-Wayment conjecture: a nondegenerate compact connected metric space in which every pair of distinct points has exactly two equidistant points is homeomorphic to the circle (Theorem A). Formalized: every definition, lemma, fact (in the form used), proposition, corollary and theorem of Sections 2-12, including Theorems A, B and C, the converse (the Euclidean circle has the DMP), the characterization of the metrizable continua admitting a DMP metric, and the facts that arcs and simple triods are finite trees. Not formalized: figures, remarks and the open questions of Section 13, and R. L. Moore's general theorem behind Fact 2.5 (only its consequence "a dendrite without branch points is an arc" is proved, which is all the paper uses).

records.name: NajmanTrbovic.represents_iff_rational_twist
records.entry_name: Splitting of primes in number fields generated by points on some modular curves (partial)
records.doc: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of parts of F. Najman, A. Trbović, "Splitting of primes in number fields generated by points on some modular curves" (Res. Number Theory 8 (2022)). For the 18 hyperelliptic models y² = f_N(x) of the paper (its explicit equations; their identification with the modular curves X₀(N) is not formalized), and quadratic fields ℚ(√D) generated by points with x ∈ ℚ and y ∉ ℚ: Theorem 2.2 (Table 2: primes that split, are unramified or not inert, and conditions on D), the square-residue conclusion of Theorem 2.8 (Table 3), Theorem 2.12 (infinitely many such fields in which a given prime ramifies, Table 4), and Theorem 2.13 with Table 7 in the corrected form of the authors' erratum (non-exceptional points), with the ring of integers, discriminant and residue rings of ℚ(√D). For Proposition 3.1 (complete splitting, in cubic fields K with E(K)_tors ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/14, of primes of multiplicative reduction): the local and algebraic steps, the passage from the torsion hypothesis to a point on the model of X₁(2,14), and the splitting conclusion under an explicit hypothesis replacing the step of the paper's proof that is not formalized. Also numerical checks against an exceptional point at level 26 and the printed Lemmas 2.6(b) and 2.9. 51 theorems and 1 definition, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: StrongDiracChallenge.dirac_counterexample_all_ge_8
records.entry_name: Strong Dirac Counterexamples for All n >= 8 and Infinite Refutation of Grunbaum's 2010 Conjecture
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization in the Euclidean plane R^2 proving: (1) every n >= 8 admits a non-collinear n-point set with every point incident to at most floor(n/2) connecting lines (self-contained across all 12 residue classes modulo 12, adapting Felsner's family for several classes and adding an explicit 8-deletion construction for n = 12k + 11, k >= 2); (2) three infinite straight-line knight-lattice families with deficit 5/2 below n/2 (n = 60s + 53 and n = 60s + 69 for all s >= 0, and n = 60s + 61 for all s >= 1); and (3) a refutation of Grunbaum's 2010 conjecture G(n) = 2 * floor(n/4) by at least 2 across four infinite congruence classes modulo 60. Companion write-ups and logged prior-work searches (arXiv, CORE, Google Scholar as of 2026-11-22, and surveys through 2025) are published at mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-through-every-point and mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-five-halves-short; neither the n = 12k + 11 construction nor infinite straight-line families with deficit > 3/2 were found in those logged searches, though paywalled pages 323-326 of Akiyama et al. (2011) and print monographs remain unread/unsearched.

Companion write-ups and logged prior-work searches (arXiv, CORE, Google Scholar as of 2026-11-22, and surveys through 2025) are published at mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-through-every-point and mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-five-halves-short; neither the n = 12k + 11 construction nor infinite straight-line families with deficit > 3/2 were found in those logged searches, though paywalled pages 323-326 of Akiyama et al. (2011) and print monographs remain unread/unsearched.

records.name: LychrelBase6.infinite_lychrel6
records.entry_name: Two infinite families of base-6 Lychrel numbers
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 formalization of two explicit, strictly increasing, pairwise disjoint infinite families x(m) and y(m) (m >= 0) of base-6 Lychrel numbers under repeated base-6 reverse-and-add T(n) = n + rev_6(n). Family 1 has 110 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed x(0) with 86 decimal digits) and Family 2 has 108 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed y(0) with 84 decimal digits), with middle blocks linked by base-6 digit complement d |-> 5 - d. Both satisfy the exact period-12 self-similar recurrence T^[12](x(m)) = x(m + 3) and T^[12](y(m)) = y(m + 3) while avoiding all base-6 palindromes, proving unconditionally that infinitely many base-6 Lychrel numbers exist.

records.name: FibSumPermChallenge.layman_unique_if
records.entry_name: Uniqueness Characterization of Fibonacci-Sum Permutations (Layman's Conjecture / Hajnal Conjecture 1)
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving that there exists a unique permutation p of {1, ..., k} with every i + p(i) a Fibonacci number if and only if k belongs to Layman's sequence w(n) = floor(F_{n+3} / sqrt(5)) (equivalently Hajnal's M4 sequence). Formalizes Hajnal's (2022) "only if" direction and Reshetnikov's (2015, OEIS A097083) floor formula alongside a step-lemma proof of the "if" direction (Hajnal Conjecture 1). Companion write-up and dated prior-work searches (arXiv, OEIS, zbMATH, CORE 2026-11-20, Google Scholar 2026-11-22) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/fibonacci-sum-permutations; the "if" direction was not found in those logged searches (MathSciNet and print problem sections remain unsearched).

records.name: HypercubeChallenge.theorem1_f_lower_bound_nat
records.entry_name: Lower Bounds on Diameter-Preserving Spanning Subgraphs of the Hypercube
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization for Graham and Harary's hypercube diameter-preserving spanning subgraph problem: proves the universal lower bound 2^n + ceil((2^n - 2n)/(n - 1)) <= f(n) for all n >= 2, raises the asymptotic second-term coefficient to 3/2 on the scale 2^n/(n - 1), and certifies 39 <= f(5) <= 40, f(6) >= 76, f(7) >= 150, f(8) >= 294, and improved lower bounds through dimension n = 32. Companion write-up and prior-work search log (including Google Scholar sweep on 2026-11-22) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/hypercube-edge-bounds; no priority is claimed over unread sources (the full body of Bouabdallah-Delorme-Djelloul 1995 and Djelloul's 1993 thesis could not be accessed).

records.name: PatternPosetChallenge.mcnamara_steingrimsson_Q9_5_false
records.entry_name: Non-Sperner Intervals and Exact Deficiency Family in the Permutation Pattern Poset
records.doc: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization refuting McNamara and Steingrimsson's Question 9.5 (2015) via an explicit 19-element closed interval [213, 2574613] of largest rank size 7 and width 8, and proving that for every k >= 1 there exists a principal downset [empty, tau_k] whose width exceeds its largest rank size by exactly k. Companion write-up and dated prior-work searches (arXiv, CORE 2026-11-20, Google Scholar 2026-11-22, Zenodo, DataCite, HAL, OSF, and Elizalde-McNamara 2015 / Vatter 2026) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/pattern-poset-not-sperner; no prior non-Sperner interval of the classical pattern poset was found in those logged searches, while Pouzet-Rosenberg (1986), Burosch et al. (1990, 1996), and print monographs remain unread/unsearched.
