records.name: OverfullWork.BipartiteRegularitySource.robust_vertex_sampling_explicit
records.entry_name: Robust expanders: spanning structures and Hamilton decompositions
records.doc: Seven Lean results on robust expansion. Fixed-cardinality sampling preserves robust out-expansion with an explicit expansion parameter and failure bound. Sufficiently large robust outexpanders of linear minimum semidegree have a Hamilton cycle. Robust graphs of linear minimum degree admit spanning vertex-disjoint paths between prescribed pairs. Almost regular robust graphs admit edge-disjoint realizations of small layouts with a robust remainder. The final three results prove approximate and exact Hamilton decompositions for regular digraphs and exact Hamilton decompositions for even-regular graphs.

Sufficiently large robust outexpanders of linear minimum semidegree have a Hamilton cycle. Robust graphs of linear minimum degree admit spanning vertex-disjoint paths between prescribed pairs. Almost regular robust graphs admit edge-disjoint realizations of small layouts with a robust remainder. The final three results prove approximate and exact Hamilton decompositions for regular digraphs and exact Hamilton decompositions for even-regular graphs.

records.name: MainResult
records.entry_name: Schauder bases in unitary orbits
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the following theorem: a strongly continuous one-parameter group of unitary operators on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space has simple continuous spectrum if and only if one of its orbits contains a Schauder basis, that is, there are a vector g and pairwise distinct real numbers t_n such that (U_{t_n} g) is a Schauder basis.

records.name: LSBA.thm1_4
records.entry_name: The localization scale of the block Anderson model in one dimension at arbitrary coupling and volume
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Yin, "The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume" (arXiv:2611.09776). The model is H = (g (S + S^{-1}) tensor I_W + diag(V_1, ..., V_L)) / max{1, g} on C^L tensor C^W, with independent GUE blocks V_a of size W and the cyclic shift S of Z_L. Theorem 1.4: for 0 < kappa < 1/2 and all D, tau > 0, for all large W, every L >= 3 and every coupling g >= 0, the expected fraction of the eigenvalues in the bulk energy set J_{g,kappa,L} that are simple and whose eigenvector has localization length between W^{-tau} l and W^{tau} l, where l = min{WL, max{W, W^2 g^2}}, is at least 1 - W^{-D}. Corollary 1.5: if also L <= W^{B_L}, then with probability at least 1 - W^{-D} this holds for every eigenvalue in J_{g,kappa,L}. No result of another work is assumed; every result that the paper uses is proved in the library from Mathlib.

records.name: Auto.DIRX.thm_1_1
records.entry_name: Formalization of sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube
records.doc:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of the two papers 
"Sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube II: The
critical exponent" by P. Durcik, P. Ivanisvili, J. Roos and X. Xie,
and "Sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube near the
critical exponent" by P. Durcik, P. Ivanisvili and J. Roos.
The central result of this sequence of two papers is a sharp isoperimetric
inequality on the Hamming cube at the critical exponent.
Additional results include the resolution of a conjecture of Kahn and Park on
cube partitions, a sharp L^1 Poincare inequality for Boolean-valued functions
and some improved isoperimetric inequalities for large subsets of the Hamming cube.
The structure of the formalization closely follows the structure of the paper and most
mathematical claims of the two papers are represented by Lean statements within the repository.
The Lean code was generated by coding agents.

records.name: SchurFormal.main_result
records.entry_name: Schur decomposition with logarithmic precision in cubic time up to squared logarithmic factors
records.doc: A finite randomised floating-point program computes an approximate complex Schur decomposition for every input of spectral norm at most one. For tolerance delta and requested failure probability p in (0,1/2), the joint residual and orthogonality errors are at most delta with probability at least 1-p. The program uses logarithmically many significand and natural control-word bits, and cubic work times a squared logarithm. Exact triangular storage and the work bound hold on every execution.

records.name: LeanLab.Song2020.Palomar1122Song.songWindow_margin_of_lemma3
records.entry_name: The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of Yanbo Song, The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes, arXiv 2012.06322 v1, 2020, with any positive margin in the window, by the deduction of Section 4 on page 9. Theorem 1 says that for 44/45 < gamma < 1 every large enough odd n is p1 + p2 + p3 with each pi a prime of the form floor of m to the power 1/gamma and |pi - n/3| <= y, for every y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8. The margin results rest on one cited input, the paper's Lemma 3, which is Theorem 3 of C. D. Pan and C. B. Pan, Goldbach Conjecture, Science Press, Beijing, 1988, taken at the exponent 7/8 as the explicit hypothesis Lemma3 7/8 and never as an axiom. From it the entry proves Theorem 1 for every window y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8 plus delta with delta > 0, and the page 9 asymptotic formula for R of n on the same windows; the paper's Lemmas 4 and 5 are proved. The exact window result also takes the transfer step of page 9 at the exact threshold, LogTransferDQ, as a second hypothesis. An independent check of the lab could not prove that transfer step at the exact threshold, since Lemma 4 holds with a loss of n to the epsilon only, so Theorem 1 at the exact window remains open here and the headline result is the margin version. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott 2013. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: LeanLab.Linnik1951.linnik1951_decomposed_final_b1122
records.entry_name: Prime numbers and powers of two
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the theorem of Yu. V. Linnik, Prime numbers and powers of two, Trudy Mat. Inst. Steklov 38, 1951, pages 152 to 169, in its qualitative form: conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, there is a constant K such that every sufficiently large even integer is the sum of two primes and at most K powers of two, each power 2^v with v >= 1. The one hypothesis is GRH, taken as an explicit hypothesis and never as an axiom: for every modulus q >= 1, every Dirichlet character chi modulo q and every s in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1, if the L-function of chi vanishes at s then Re s = 1/2. The constant K is not explicit. The theorem printed on page 154 is an asymptotic formula for the number of representations of N as two primes and exactly k powers of two, for each fixed k >= 3; the entry proves the qualitative consequence that Linnik draws from it on pages 168 and 169, and not the asymptotic formula itself. Linnik 1953 and Gallagher 1975 later removed the hypothesis GRH, and the gallagher1975 entry of this repository is the unconditional result. The route uses a repaired bound for the mixed integral of page 160 with log N to the power 7 in place of the power 6 printed in display 5.5, whose power 6 form the lab could not derive; the extra logarithm does not change the conclusion. Binary Goldbach, the case K = 0, is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: LeanLab.KadiriLumley2014.PalomarEntry57.corollary57_of_inputs
records.entry_name: Short effective intervals containing primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of conditional forms of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of H. Kadiri and A. Lumley, Short effective intervals containing primes, Integers 14, 2014, A61, arXiv 1407.7902. Theorem 1.1 says that for each row of Table 2, with threshold x0 and denominator Delta, every real x > x0 has a prime p with 1 - 1/Delta times x < p < x. The three main compared results are conditional, and every cited input is an explicit hypothesis, never an axiom. The main result, corollary57_of_inputs, says that every odd n with 5 < n < 1886389443 * 4 * 10^18 is a sum of three primes, from five inputs: 1, even Goldbach up to 4 * 10^18, the verification of Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi 2014; 2, Theorem 2 of Montgomery and Vaughan 1973, the Brun Titchmarsh inequality; 3, Dusart 2010 Theorem 5.2 at eta = 0.05, the bound |theta t - t| < 0.05 t / log^2 t for t >= 122568683, from which the Costa Pereira bound that the paper cites as Lemma 2.1 is proved; 4 and 5, the paper's own numerical display 2.64, in a slightly strengthened form, at the Table 2 rows log 4 * 10^18 and 57, taken as hypotheses. The range is the row 57 range, about 4 percent below the range 1966196911 * 4 * 10^18 printed in Corollary 1.2, which uses row 60. Ternary Goldbach itself is known unconditionally by Helfgott's work, so the interest of the corollary here is the method; binary Goldbach is open. The entry also proves kl45_of_inputs, Table 2 row 45 of Theorem 1.1 in a natural number form, from inputs 2, 3 and display 2.64 at row 45, and row_of_inputs, any row of Table 2 from the Costa Pereira bound, input 2 and display 2.64 at that row. Responding to review, the entry also proves zeroError_hasSum and row_zeroError_hasSum: the weighted series over the nontrivial zeros of zeta inside zeroError is summable, with zeroError its sum, for all positive m, delta, u and X, and so at every Table 2 row at the X where display 2.64 is asked. The zero contribution in each display 2.64 hypothesis is therefore the true sum, with no summability assumption needed. AI agents, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, wrote the Lean code, with ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; it is offered for human audit.

records.entry_name: Conditional independence for a literal 451-state Turing machine
records.doc: This formalization concerns a binary machine with 451 working states. Under consistency of ZF plus a Berkeley cardinal, arithmetic Σ₁-soundness of ZFC plus I₀, and a proof in ZF plus a Berkeley cardinal of consistency of the specified Craig presentation of the arithmetic consequences of ZFC plus I₀, the machine never halts on the blank tape and neither halting nor nonhalting is provable in ZFC plus I₀ or ZF plus I₀.

records.name: MeyerGeneralProblem.LevOlevskii.theoremA1
records.entry_name: Finite modulated lattice-comb decompositions for crystalline measures
records.doc: In every positive dimension, a crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and uniformly discrete spectrum is a finite complex linear combination of translated, modulated combs on full-rank lattices. The support and spectrum each lie in finitely many lattice translates. The lattices can differ between terms, and the nonzero atomic weights can approach zero. This gives the physical-support covering conclusion in the question of Lev and Olevskii.

records.name: ChallengeScrewRH.Psi_eq_tsum_zeros
records.entry_name: Certified Positivity: the explicit formula for Suzuki's zeta screw function, and positive semidefiniteness of its Gram kernel on every finite grid under the Riemann Hypothesis
records.doc:
Suzuki's screw function of the Riemann zeta function is the even function Psi defined, for t >= 0, as an archimedean profile minus the von Mangoldt weighted prime sum over n <= e^t of Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) times (t - log n); its Krein Gram kernel is G(t,u) = Psi(t) + Psi(u) - Psi(t-u). This entry uses exactly the Lean definitions of Psi and G from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-11-14-000017 (RequestProject/V5_1.lean) and proves two results about them in Lean 4 and Mathlib.
(1) Explicit formula, unconditional. For every real t >= 0, Psi(t), viewed as a complex number, equals the unconditionally convergent sum (a tsum over the subtype of zeros) over the nontrivial zeros rho of riemannZeta, that is the zeros with 0 < Re rho < 1, of m(rho) (exp((rho - 1/2) t) - 1) / (rho - 1/2)^2, where m(rho) is the analytic order of riemannZeta at rho. This is Suzuki's zero-sum representation of the screw function (arXiv:2206.03682, Theorem 1.1(2), eq. (1.3)). In Lean: ScrewRH.Psi_eq_tsum_zeros (t : R) (ht : 0 <= t) : ((V5_1.Psi t : R) : C) = tsum over rho in Z of zeroTerm t rho.
(2) Gram positivity, conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis. Assuming Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis (as a hypothesis), for every N and every grid t : Fin N -> R, the N by N matrix (G(t_i, t_j)) is positive semidefinite in the quadratic-form sense: x^T M x >= 0 for every real vector x. In Lean: ScrewRH.screw_gram_psd_of_RH : RiemannHypothesis -> for all (N : Nat) (t : Fin N -> R), Horizon.IsPSDq (Matrix.of fun i j => V5_1.G (t i) (t j)). This is the direction RH implies positivity of Suzuki's Theorem 1.2 (that -Psi is a screw function in Krein's sense), restricted to finite grids. Both compared results use only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.
Combined with a Lean proof of RiemannHypothesis, (2) becomes the unconditional statement that the Gram matrix of G is positive semidefinite on every finite grid. Such a proof was announced by Levent Alpöge in November 2026 and has been reported compiled and kernel-checked by several independent parties, on Lean v4.33.1. This entry does not import that proof and makes no claim about it; result (2) is compared and verified here only as the implication from Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis.
Significance. The registered entry certifies positivity of the genuine screw kernel on explicit grids (three Gram matrices at fixed rational nodes); this entry upgrades that, conditionally on RiemannHypothesis, to every finite grid. It is to our knowledge the first Lean formalization of Suzuki's zero-sum representation of the screw function and of the direction RH implies screw-function positivity. Scope: positive semidefinite, not strictly positive definite; real test vectors (for this real symmetric kernel equivalent to Suzuki's complex condition (1.5), but the complex form is not stated); the converse direction (positivity implies RH) is not formalized; and nothing is claimed about the Riemann Hypothesis itself.

records.name: LeanLab.BhowmikGrimmelt2026.theorem31_ported1122
records.entry_name: The exceptional set of the Goldbach problem
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of Theorem 3.1 of G. Bhowmik and L. Grimmelt, The exceptional set of the Goldbach problem, arXiv 2607.27282 v2, 2026, page 9, a result the paper attributes to Hardy and Littlewood. Let E of X be the number of even integers up to X that are not a sum of two primes. The theorem is conditional on two hypotheses, Theta < 3/4 and the zero bound at Theta: every zero of every Dirichlet L-function, for every modulus and every character, primitive or not, has real part at most Theta, stated for the zeros in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1 of Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction. Under them, for every epsilon > 0 there is a constant C with E of X at most C times X to the power 2 Theta - 1/2 + epsilon for every X >= 1. The zero bound is unproved for every Theta below 1 and false for every Theta below 1/2, since the Riemann zeta function has zeros on the critical line; the generalized Riemann hypothesis gives it at Theta = 1/2, and then the bound X to the power 1/2 + epsilon. No cited input enters: the explicit formula for psi of x and chi with a primitive character, Davenport chapter 19, the Gallagher type mean square estimates of the major and minor arcs and the zero expansion are all proved in the entry. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. Claude and Codex agents wrote the Lean code, with ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files and two other ported files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; it is offered for human audit.

records.name: JSP523Palomar.rank_three_upper
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #643: Extremal Disjoint-Union Hypergraphs
records.doc: Yilin Liu's mathematical proof and Lean formalization establish an upper bound of n choose 2 for every n in rank three, an asymptotic forcing threshold of n choose (r - 1) at each fixed rank r at least three (Erdős #643(ii)), and the eventual exact avoiding maximum (n - 1) choose (r - 1) plus floor((n - 1)/r) at each fixed rank r at least four. This repository contains the substantive Lean development ported from Liu's September 2026 submission.

records.name: h1Atom_memL2
records.entry_name: Derivatives of Theta Functions and a Problem of Lyubarskii and Nes
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the main result of the paper "Derivatives of Theta Functions and a Problem of Lyubarskii and Nes" by L. Liehr, I. Shafkulovska and M. A. Taylor (arXiv:2609.27846): if Λ = Mℤ² ⊂ ℝ² is a lattice of density D(Λ) = q/p, where p and q are coprime positive integers with q ≥ p + 2, then the Gabor system of the first Hermite function h₁(t) = t·exp(−πt²) along Λ is a frame for L²(ℝ).

records.name: gaborAtom_memL2
records.entry_name: Gabor Frames of Totally Positive Functions
records.doc: We formally verify in Lean 4 the following statement: if g : ℝ → ℝ is a continuous, integrable and totally positive function and if α, β > 0 satisfy αβ < 1, then the Gabor system {e^{2πiβnx} g(x − αm) : m, n ∈ ℤ} is a frame for L²(ℝ). This is the new implication in the solution of the frame set problem for totally positive functions, which is Theorem 1.1 of the paper "Gabor Frames of Totally Positive Functions: A Complete Characterization" by de Dios Pont, Gröchenig, Liehr, Shafkulovska and Taylor (arXiv:2608.04992).

records.name: SpectralGeometry.AmmannBeenker.admitted_zero
records.entry_name: A One-Edge Change Splits Two Energy Levels in an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph
records.doc:
We study how local changes affect waves in an infinite Ammann–Beenker network, a mathematical model with an octagonal structure.

At a particular energy, the network has two localized wave patterns, which we call A and B. An earlier theorem, registered with Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012, proved that these two patterns account for all independent states at that energy in the entire infinite network.

Further results proved in Lean establish that, at this special setting, no other real energy level lies within a distance of 1/128 of their common energy.

We can influence the two localized patterns in two different ways.

The first is to change a parameter that affects the first ring of the network. This raises or lowers the energy of A by exactly the parameter change, while leaving the energy of B unchanged. Both patterns remain exact eigenstates of the infinite system, without spreading outside their original localized forms. The spectral gap was proved at the original setting; for sufficiently small changes to this parameter, separation from the other energy levels also follows from the general eigenvalue-stability estimates already established in Lean.

The second is to change the strength of a single edge connecting the two rings. Here the situation is more subtle. One combination of the original patterns, called the dark state, remains protected at the original energy. The other, called the bright state, responds to the change and interacts with the rest of the infinite network.

Our main theorem proves what actually happens in this second case. For a sufficiently small, nonzero edge change, there are exactly two distinct real energy levels represented by eigenvectors in a specified narrow range. One remains fixed, while the other moves upward when the edge is strengthened and downward when it is weakened. Each level has only one independent wave pattern.

The theorem also gives two precise numerical guarantees. The moving energy differs from the original energy plus one quarter of the edge change by no more than 112 times the square of that change. For a normalized wave at the moving energy, the size of the part extending beyond the original two-state space is at most 64 times the square root of 7, multiplied by the absolute size of the edge change.

This means that we can make the external part of the moving wave as small as desired while keeping the two energy levels distinct. These are exact results for the infinite system, not predictions from a simplified two-state model.

What happens if the edge change is temporary? Separate theorems, already proved in Lean, study an edge change applied for a period of time and then switched off. They give a bound on the wave's component outside the original two-state space: no more than 512 times the absolute size of the edge change, multiplied by the initial wave's size. This bound is independent of the duration of the pulse and of the time elapsed after switching it off.

These temporal conclusions are conditional: they assume that the supplied evolution preserves norms, preserves the operator's mathematical domain, and commutes with the relevant Hamiltonian during each stage. A general physical quantum propagator has not yet been constructed in this formalization.

The results fit together in a natural way. Changing the first-ring parameter offers an exact way to adjust the relative energies of the two original patterns without changing their shapes. Changing the connecting edge produces a genuine energy separation involving a bright-derived state, while the associated spreading into the infinite network can be kept small. The temporal results complement these spectral findings by showing that, under suitable evolution assumptions, the wave remains close to the original two-state space during and after a temporary edge change.

Together, these results provide a mathematical foundation for investigating whether changes to the first-ring parameter and to the connecting edge can be combined to control localized waves. They do not yet prove that any desired mixture of the two original patterns can be prepared. The results concern the real infinite-operator model, not a separately proved classification of the complete complex spectrum.

The research direction was conceived and directed by Alessandro Odasso, who is not a mathematician. According to the maintainer, AI generated the mathematical proofs and Lean formalizations under his direction. The originality and scientific significance of these results have not yet been independently assessed.
